 The Brunet Palace (Romantic Museum).

name: Manaca Iznaga Tower
overview: A 45-meter high slave-watching tower located in the Valley of the Sugar Mills (Valle de los Ingenios).
history_significance: Built in 1816. It was used to watch over the slaves working in the cane fields and its bell signaled the start and end of the workday.
highlights:
Climbing the wooden stairs to the top.
 The view of the Sugar Mill Valley.
 The history of the sugar plantation.

name: Che Guevara Mausoleum
overview: A memorial complex housing the remains of revolutionary Ernesto 'Che' Guevara and twenty-nine of his fellow combatants.
history_significance: Built near the site of the Battle of Santa Clara, the decisive victory of the Cuban Revolution led by Che. It contains his personal artifacts.
highlights:
The massive bronze statue of Che.
 The eternal flame.
 The museum of Che's life.

name: Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca
overview: A multi-level fortress built into a rocky promontory overlooking the bay of Santiago de Cuba.
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Designed by Italian engineers in 1637 to defend against pirates. It is the best preserved example of Spanish-American military architecture.
highlights:
The views of the Caribbean Sea.
 The drawbridges and moats.
 The piracy museum inside.

name: Santa Ifigenia Cemetery
overview: The necropolis where many of Cuba's most famous figures are buried, including Jose Marti and Fidel Castro.
history_significance: It is the resting place of national heroes ('Founding Fathers'). The changing of the guard ceremony takes place at Jose Marti's mausoleum.
highlights:
The Mausoleum of Jose Marti.
 The simple stone boulder grave of Fidel Castro.
 The changing of the guard ceremony.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Charity
overview: A basilica dedicated to the Patron Saint of Cuba, located in the copper mining village of El Cobre.
history_significance: The image of the Virgin was found floating in the sea in 1612. Ernest Hemingway donated his Nobel Prize medal to this shrine.
highlights:
The statue of the Virgin of Charity.
 The room of offerings (votos).
 The location in the Sierra Maestra mountains.

name: Cienfuegos Historic Centre
overview: A city known as the 'Pearl of the South', founded by French immigrants. It features unique French-influenced neoclassical architecture.
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Unlike other Cuban cities, it was laid out in the 19th century with wide streets and French elegance.
highlights:
The Jose Marti Park.
 The Tomas Terry Theatre.
 The Ferrer Palace.

name: Palacio de Valle
overview: An architectural jewel located at the tip of the Punta Gorda peninsula. It looks like an Arabian palace.
history_significance: Built in 1917 by a wealthy merchant. It blends Gothic, Venetian, and Neo-Moorish styles in a flamboyant display of wealth.
highlights:
The rooftop terrace bar.
 The intricate Moorish carvings.
 The sunset views over the bay.

name: Camagüey Historic Centre
overview: A city known for its maze-like street pattern designed to confuse pirates. It is the 'City of Tinajones' (clay pots).
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its irregular urban layout is unique in colonial Latin America. The large clay pots were used to collect rainwater.
highlights:
The winding, confusing streets.
 Plaza San Juan de Dios.
 The tinajones found in courtyards.

name: Castillo de la Real Fuerza
overview: A star fort on the western side of Havana harbor. It is the oldest stone fort in the Americas.
history_significance: Built in 1558. It houses the maritime museum and is topped by 'La Giraldilla', a weather vane that is the symbol of Havana.
highlights:
The La Giraldilla statue.
 The maritime museum and ship models.
 The moat and drawbridge.

name: Bacardi Building
overview: An Art Deco skyscraper in Old Havana. It was the headquarters of the Bacardi rum company.
history_significance: Completed in 1930, it was the tallest building in Havana. Its facade features colorful granite, limestone, and terracotta bats (the company symbol).
highlights:
The bell tower with the bronze bat.
 The lavish Art Deco lobby.
 The view from the tower.

name: Moncada Barracks
overview: A military barracks that was the site of the first armed attack of the Cuban Revolution.
history_significance: Attacked by Fidel Castro's group on July 26, 1953. The bullet holes on the facade are preserved (recreated) as a symbol of the revolution's start.
highlights:
The bullet-riddled yellow facade.
 The July 26 Museum inside.
 The history of the assault.

name: Nassau Straw Market
overview: A world-famous market located on Bay Street. It is the home of handmade Bahamian straw crafts.
history_significance: Straw plaiting is a tradition dating back to the 1940s when it became a booming industry. The market is the heartbeat of Bahamian souvenir trade.
highlights:
Hand-woven straw hats and bags.
 Wood carvings.
 The lively bargaining atmosphere.

name: Oranjestad Historic Center
overview: The downtown area of Aruba's capital, featuring colorful Dutch Colonial architecture with a Caribbean twist.
history_significance: Named after King Willem van Oranje-Nassau. The architecture reflects the Dutch influence, particularly the restored buildings along Wilhelmstraat.
highlights:
The bright lime, pink, and blue buildings.
 Fort Zoutman.
 The Main Street tram.

name: Heritage Collection Museum
overview: A private museum curated by historian Colville Petty. It offers the most comprehensive history of Anguilla.
history_significance: It covers the island's history from the Arawaks to the 1967 Anguilla Revolution, providing deep insight into the island's struggle and identity.
highlights:
Artifacts from the Arawak era.
 Relics from the 1967 Revolution.
 Photographs of early island life.

name: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison
overview: A UNESCO World Heritage Site comprising the historic city center and the military garrison of St. Ann.
history_significance: Established in the 17th century, it is an outstanding example of British colonial architecture and urban layout in the Caribbean.
highlights:
The Chamberlain Bridge.
 The Parliament Buildings.
 The George Washington House.

name: Willemstad Historic Area
overview: The inner city and harbor of Willemstad, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It includes the districts of Punda and Otrobanda.
history_significance: Established in 1634, it represents the organic growth of a multicultural trading settlement with distinct Dutch architectural influence.
highlights:
The Handelskade waterfront.
 The Queen Emma Pontoon Bridge.
 The narrow alleys of Punda.

name: Kalinago Barana Aute
overview: A model traditional village located in the Kalinago Territory. It showcases the culture and heritage of the Kalinago people (Caribs).
history_significance: It preserves the history of the Caribbean's indigenous people who resisted colonization for centuries. It offers a glimpse into pre-Columbian life.
highlights:
The Karbet (men's house).
 Traditional canoe building demonstrations.
 The Isulukati waterfall.

name: Castries Central Market
overview: A bustling market housed in an orange-roofed building and spreading into the streets. It is considered one of the best markets in the Caribbean.
history_significance: Built in 1891, the iron structure is a historic landmark. It has been the commercial hub of St. Lucia for over a century.
highlights:
The bright orange roof.
 The Vendor's Arcade.
 Local spices and hot sauces.

name: Castillo de San Felipe de Lara
overview: A Spanish colonial fort located at the entrance to Lake Izabal from the Rio Dulce.
history_significance: Built in 1644 to protect inland communities from Caribbean pirates. It is a classic example of military architecture adapted to a river setting.
highlights:
The Torre de Bustamante.
 The scenic views of the Rio Dulce.
 The cramped dungeons and maze-like interior.

name: Museo Nacional de Arqueología y Etnología
overview: The national museum dedicated to the history and culture of the Maya people. It holds the country's most significant archaeological collection.
history_significance: It houses thousands of artifacts spanning the Pre-classic to Post-classic periods, preserving the heritage of Guatemala's indigenous civilizations.
highlights:
The jade mask of Tak'alik Ab'aj.
 The massive stone stelae from Tikal and Piedras Negras.
 The extensive textile collection.

name: Kaminaljuyu
overview: An ancient Maya city located largely beneath modern-day Guatemala City. The park preserves the Acropolis and several mounds.
history_significance: A major trade hub in the Late Preclassic period. It is unique for its adobe architecture and strong influence from Teotihuacan in central Mexico.
highlights:
The Acropolis and Plaza.
 The earthen adobe mounds.
 The archaeological park surrounded by the modern city.

name: Ozama Fortress
overview: The oldest military structure of European origin in the Americas. It stands guard at the entrance to the Ozama River.
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built in 1502 to protect the city from pirates and foreign invaders. It served as a prison until the 1960s.
highlights:
The Tower of Homage (Torre del Homenaje).
 The panoramic view of the river and city.
 The statue of Gonzalo Fernández de Oviedo.

name: Malecon de Santo Domingo
overview: A 14-kilometer long sea-front boulevard (George Washington Avenue). It is the center of nightlife, dining, and open-air events.
history_significance: It serves as the city's living room, hosting the Merengue Festival and carnival parades. It reflects the vibrant modern culture of the capital.
highlights:
The Obelisk (El Obelisco Macho).
 The ocean views and sea breeze.
 The vibrant nightlife and casinos.

name: National Palace, Dominican Republic
overview: The seat of the Dominican government and the Presidency. It is a large neoclassical building made of pink marble.
history_significance: Built in 1947 during the Trujillo era. Designed by Italian architect Guido D'Alessandro, it represents the center of political power in the country.
highlights:
The Hall of Caryatids.
 The amber room.
 The neoclassical pink marble facade.

name: Catedral Primada de América
overview: The oldest cathedral in the Americas, dedicated to Santa María la Menor. It combines Gothic and Baroque architectural styles.
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Commissioned by Pope Julius II in 1504 and completed in 1541. It once housed the remains of Christopher Columbus.
highlights:
The golden coral limestone facade.
 The silver altar.
 The 14 chapels inside.

name: Port Royal
overview: Once known as the 'wickedest city on earth', this former pirate haven is now a quiet fishing village with historic ruins.
history_significance: It was the pirate capital of the Caribbean until a massive earthquake sank much of the city in 1692. It preserves Fort Charles and the Giddy House.
highlights:
Fort Charles.
 The Giddy House (tilted artillery store).
 The sunken city archaeological site.

name: Spanish Town Historic District
overview: The former Spanish and British capital of Jamaica. It features the finest collection of historic buildings in the English-speaking Caribbean.
history_significance: Founded in 1534 as Villa de la Vega. Emancipation Square is the only Georgian square in Jamaica, where the proclamation of freedom was read.
highlights:
The Rodney Memorial.
 The Old King's House ruins.
 St. Jago de la Vega Cathedral.

name: Copan Ruinas
overview: An ancient Maya city located in western Honduras, not far from the border with Guatemala. It was a major capital city of the Classic Maya period.
history_significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. Known as the 'Athens of the New World' for its artistic stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway, which contains the longest known Maya text.
highlights:
The Hieroglyphic Stairway.
 The Great Plaza and Stelae.
 The Ballcourt.

name: Fortaleza de San Fernando de Omoa
overview: A colonial-era fortress located on the Caribbean coast. It is one of the largest fortifications built by the Spanish in Central America.
history_significance: Built in the 18th century to defend against pirates and British forces. It is famous for its triangular shape and well-preserved walls.
highlights:
The triangular design.
 The dungeons and tunnels.
 The view of the Caribbean Sea.

name: Comayagua Cathedral
overview: The Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception in the heart of Comayagua. It is one of the oldest cathedrals in Central America.
history_significance: Famous for housing the oldest functioning clock in the Americas (and possibly the world), constructed by the Moors around 1100 AD.
highlights:
The ancient Moorish clock.
 The intricate Baroque facade.
 The colonial altarpieces.

name: Christ of El Picacho
overview: A massive statue of Jesus Christ standing atop the El Picacho hill, overlooking the capital city of Tegucigalpa.
history_significance: Erected in 1997, it is a major landmark and pilgrimage site, visible from almost anywhere in the city.
highlights:
The panoramic view of Tegucigalpa.
 The 20-meter high statue.
 The surrounding United Nations Park.

name: Museum of National Identity (MIN)
overview: A museum dedicated to the history and culture of Honduras, housed in the beautiful 19th-century Palace of Ministries.
history_significance: The building itself is a National Heritage site. The museum provides a comprehensive journey through Honduran history from geological formation to the present.
highlights:
The virtual tour of Copan.
 The restored neoclassical architecture.
 The rotating art exhibits.

name: Fort San Cristobal
overview: A white-walled fortress located on a hill overlooking the colonial town of Gracias.
history_significance: Built in the 19th century to guard the city. It contains the tomb of Juan Lindo, a former president of both Honduras and El Salvador.
highlights:
The tomb of President Juan Lindo.
 The views of Gracias and the Celaque mountains.
 The well-preserved cannons.

name: Maya Sculpture Museum
overview: A world-class museum located at the entrance of the Copan ruins archaeological park.
history_significance: It houses original stelae, altars, and the full-scale replica of the Rosalila Temple, which was found buried intact under another pyramid.
highlights:
The full-size Rosalila Temple replica.
 The original Altar Q.
 The intricate stone carvings protected from the elements.

name: Mona Lisa
highlights: Undoubtedly the most famous painting the world has ever seen. Painted between 1503 and 1519, this elegant portrait of Lisa Gherardini is created with oil on wood and captures the true spirit of the Renaissance.

name: Girl With A Pearl Earring
highlights: Shows a young woman with a captivating look and enigmatic expression, wearing an exotic dress and a shiny pearl earring created with masterful use of light and shadows.

name: The Starry Night
highlights: A brilliant work of art painted while Van Gogh was recovering in an asylum. It features vibrant colors, brushwork, stars, the moon, and a symbolical Cypress tree, influencing modern Expressionism.

name: The Last Supper
highlights: Captures the dynamic moment of the disciples' reaction to Jesus declaring one will betray him. Painted as a wall painting, it uses perspective and hidden meanings to showcase Vinci's genius.

name: The Birth of Venus
highlights: Inspired by the myth of Venus riding on a seashell. A bold work featuring nudity during the early Renaissance, painted with tempera on canvas.

name: The Creation of Adam
highlights: One of the biblical images from the Sistine Chapel ceiling, depicting God creating the first man, Adam. It reflects the belief that man is created in the image of God.

name: The Kiss
highlights: Depicts a sensual kiss by a couple in rich patterned clothes. Unique for its use of gold leaves, silver, and platinum, marking it as a masterpiece of Symbolism.

name: Guernica
highlights: A powerful anti-war oil painting in grey, black, and white. Painted as a reaction to the bombing of Guernica, it uses a bull and horse to represent the horrors of war.

name: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
highlights: A true representation of Romanticism, showing a man standing on a rock looking at the mist. The contrast between light and dark makes it extraordinary.

name: School of Athens
highlights: A pure presentation of philosophy depicting greatest mathematicians and philosophers like Plato and Aristotle. It represents the spirit of the Renaissance and knowledge.

name: Sunflowers
highlights: Part of a series painted in Arles, symbolizing gratitude and harmony. It showcases Van Gogh's experiments with vibrant colors.

name: Irises
highlights: Painted while staying in the asylum of Saint Remy. It depicts the movement in still flowers, showing his true talent during a time of isolation.

name: View of Toledo
highlights: A landscape artwork that shows what the place feels like rather than looks like. Painted with moody colors depicting a stormy sky and dynamic movement.

name: Persistence of Memory
highlights: A famous Surrealist work featuring melting watches, representing the subconscious paranoia about time. It explores themes of softness, hardness, and metamorphosis.

name: Café Terrace at Night
highlights: Features Van Gogh's iconic starry sky for the first time. Painted from memory with rich blue, orange, and yellow colors, capturing a night more vibrant than day.

name: The Fall of Icarus
Museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
highlights: Depicts the mythical story of Icarus falling into the water while the surroundings remain indifferent, suggesting humankind's ignorance of others' suffering.

name: The Hay Wain
highlights: Depicts a pastoral rural image on the River Stour. Notable for its stark contrast between sky and land and the depiction of rural life.

name: The Transfiguration
highlights: Raphael's last painting, showing Jesus Christ on Mount Tabor and a possessed boy on land. Masterful use of colors to create aura, lights, and shadows.

name: Happy Accident on the Swing
highlights: A dynamic Rococo masterpiece showing a woman on a swing with a man hiding in the bushes. The painting is lively, featuring a flying shoe and statues.

name: Luncheon of the Boating Party
highlights: Combines still life and landscape, depicting friends of the painter relaxing. Notable for the flickering light that dominates the work and the contrast between emptiness and fullness.

name: The Third of May 1808
highlights: A historical anti-war painting showing the attack of Napoleon's army on the Spanish. Goya is known as an early modernist for this unique style.

name: Luncheon of theLuncheon of thee
highlights: A portrait of Cecilia Gallerani holding an ermine. It is one of the few surviving female portraits by Da Vinci, painted on a walnut board.

name: Sistine Madonna
highlights: Shows Madonna carrying infant Jesus with St. Sixtus and St. Barbara. Famous for the two cherubs at the bottom and the intense, perhaps fearful expressions.

name: Olympia
highlights: A controversial painting depicting a nude woman, presumed to be a prostitute, and her black servant. The sensuous elements like the orchid and ribbon provoked critics.

name: The Great Wave of Kanagawa
highlights: The most iconic Japanese woodblock print. Features a mighty wave, Mount Fuji, and boats, symbolizing the great force of nature in contrast to weak humans.

name: The Nude Maja
highlights: Depicts a sensuous nude woman. It created controversy leading Goya to paint a clothed version. Both versions now hang side by side.

name: Almond Blossom
highlights: Painted as a gift to his nephew, representing new hope. It bears elements of Japanese Ukiyo-e prints with bold outlines and no horizon.

name: Dora Maar au Chat
highlights: A large surrealist portrait of Dora Maar. The black cat represents female aggression. It depicts her temperament rather than beauty.

name: Massacre of the Innocents
highlights: Depicts the biblical slaughter of innocents in Bethlehem. Shows despair and the horrors of war, inspired by Italian Renaissance painters.

name: The Scream
highlights: Iconic representation of human anxiety and fear of modernity. Inspired by a blood-red sunset Munch witnessed while walking.

name: American Gothic
highlights: Influential American painting depicting a farmer and his daughter. Represents the Great Depression and is open to multiple interpretations.

name: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
highlights: Pioneer of Neo-impressionism using pointillism. Depicts people relaxing in a park, contrasting beauty and sunlight with shadow and stillness.

name: Medusa's Raft
highlights: Depicts the gruesome shipwreck of Frigate Meduse involving starvation and cannibalism. A standout Romanticist work for choosing a disturbing subject.

name: Self-Portrait
highlights: Van Gogh's last self-portrait before death. The background pattern resembles Starry Night, representing his psychological turmoil and rejection of the outside world.

name: The Bridge at Narni
highlights: Famous landscape painting depicting a Roman bridge in the town of Narni. Inspired by Corot's travels and fascination with the view.

name: Arnolfini Portrait
highlights: Double portrait of a merchant and his wife. Famous for its detailed reflection in the mirror on the wall and the representation of aristocracy.

name: The Starry Night Over The Rhone
highlights: Depicts gaslighting on the Rhone river at night. Features rich blue colors and two lovers in the foreground, connecting nature with the human world.

name: Dogs Playing Poker
highlights: A series of paintings influential in American Pop culture. Commissioned for advertisements, it became popular on calendars and merchandise.

name: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
highlights: Depicts five nude prostitutes from Barcelona using geometric patterns. A break from traditional style, it is one of Picasso's largest and most distinct works.

name: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1
highlights: Commonly known as Whistler's Mother. Famous for its composition and use of musical terms in the title. A controversial yet iconic American artwork.

name: The Garden of Earthly Delights
highlights: A triptych oil painting full of symbols and moral narratives. Depicts fears and worldly activities across three distinct panels.

name: Liberty Leading the People
highlights: Depicts the July Revolution with Liberty holding the tricolor flag. The woman wears a Phrygian cap symbolizing liberty, leading people over barricades.

name: Nude Descending a Staircase
highlights: An abstract depiction of motion combining cubist and futuristic elements. Initially unappreciated, it is now considered a modern masterpiece.

name: The Ambassadors
highlights: Depicts two ambassadors with a table full of symbolic items. Famous for the anamorphic skull in the foreground representing memento mori.

name: Nighthawks
highlights: Depicts a downtown diner at night representing urban isolation. Inspired by a restaurant in Greenwich Avenue, New York.

name: Rain's Rustle
highlights: A contemporary impressionist oil painting showing a couple walking in the rain. Famous for its vivid colors and dreamy ambiance.

name: Three Musicians
highlights: A Cubist masterpiece depicting three musicians in geometric shapes. Uses bright colors and flat shapes to represent a clarinet player, guitar player, and singer.

name: The Night Café
highlights: Shows the interior of a café using rich and vivid colors to create an illusion of vibration. It is uniquely vigorous and full of life.

name: Impression, Sunrise
highlights: The painting that gave Impressionism its name. Depicts a hazy sunrise in the port of Le Havre, symbolizing the rebirth of France.

name: Christina's World
highlights: Realist painting evoking nostalgia. Shows a woman lying in a field facing a house, representing a mental portrayal more than a physical place.

name: The Fighting Temeraire
highlights: Symbolizes the decline of the British Navy and the rise of industrialization. Depicts the warship Temeraire being towed away against a setting sun.

name: The Flower Carrier
highlights: Depicts a man struggling with an overloaded basket of flowers. Symbolizes laborers in the industrialized world who are too weak to work yet must earn a livelihood.

name: Flaming June
highlights: A Victorian masterpiece inspired by Greek nymphs. Shows a woman in a bright orange dress with brilliant realism, more decorative than comfortable.

name: Saint George and the Dragon
highlights: A miniature panel celebrating the court of Urbino. Represents Chivalry and Christianity, showing Saint George slaying a dragon.

name: Annunciation
highlights: Depicts Archangel Gabriel blessing Mary. An early work featuring Vinci's recurring landscape elements and Mary's reaction of astonishment.

name: Breezing Up
highlights: Represents American spirit and hope. Shows a man and three boys enjoying a boat ride, appreciated for its perfect combination of light and shadow.

name: The Ladies Waldegrave
highlights: Depicts three daughters of Earl Waldegrave working on needlework. Created to find suitors, it represents contemporary aristocracy and tradition.

name: Et in Arcadia Ego
highlights: A French Baroque pastoral scene showing shepherds beside a tomb. The title implies 'Even in Arcadia, there I am,' symbolizing death.

name: Watson and the Shark
highlights: Depicts the dramatic rescue of Brook Watson from a shark attack in Havana. The composition is full of action and dynamic movement.

name: The Avenue in the Rain
highlights: Impressionist painting of Fifth Avenue decorated with flags during WWI. One of Hassam's flag paintings, now in the White House collection.

name: Madame Recamier
highlights: A neoclassic portrait of a beautiful woman in a vintage dress. Notable for using a horizontal format typically reserved for historical paintings.

name: Patrocles
highlights: Depicts the muscular physique of the mythical warrior Patroclus. Shows Caravaggio's influence by focusing on the nude body rather than the face.

name: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
highlights: Famous series of portraits commissioned by the King of Spain. Shows Napoleon in a dynamic horse-riding pose, yet painted as a still but lively image.

name: The Musicians
highlights: Depicts four boys in classical costumes playing music. Features a representation of Cupid and invites the viewer to join with a violin.

name: Narcissus
highlights: Depicts the mythical character Narcissus obsessed with his reflection. The surrounding darkness suggests his eventual downfall.

name: The Sleeping Gypsy
highlights: A fantastical painting of a gypsy and a lion. Rousseau described it as a poetic representation of an exhausted gypsy visited by a lion.

name: The Gleaners
highlights: Depicts the miserable life of agricultural workers gleaning corn. Contrasts the workers with the abundant harvest in the distance.

name: Primavera
highlights: Also known as 'Spring'. Depicts mythological figures celebrating spring in an orange grove, featuring Venus, Cupid, and the Three Graces.

name: Wheatfield with Crows
highlights: Believed to be Van Gogh's last work. Shows a wheatfield with three paths and crows, evoking confusion and dynamic movement.

name: The Tower of Babel
highlights: Depicts the biblical construction of the Tower of Babel with immense detail. It portrays the story of the monolingual community authenticly.

name: A Cotton Office in New Orleans
highlights: Depicts a working day at a cotton office. Degas painted this while visiting his uncle in New Orleans, a rare subject for a French artist.

name: Bacchus and Ariadne
highlights: Depicts the dramatic meeting of Bacchus and Ariadne in Naxos. Bacchus declares his love arriving on a chariot drawn by cheetahs.

name: The Gross Clinic
highlights: A realist masterpiece showing Dr. Gross in an operation theater. Eakins included himself in the painting, adding dramatic elements to the scene.

name: The Two Fridas
highlights: Depicts two versions of Frida: one weak and traditional, the other strong and modern. Symbolizes her duality and pain holding a portrait of Diego Rivera.

name: The Astronomer
highlights: Portrays an astronomer studying a globe. Features Vermeer's mastery of light and shadow, with details like an open book and exotic tapestry.

name: Christ of Saint John of the Cross
highlights: Depicts Jesus on the cross without nails or blood, floating in a dark sky. Inspired by a dream, it represents the unity of the universe.

name: The Wounded Deer
highlights: Shows a deer with Frida's face shot by arrows. Painted after her spine operation, it symbolizes her physical pain and distant hope.

name: Paris Street in Rainy Weather
highlights: A large oil painting blending Impressionism and Realism. Uses photography-like focus to depict a couple in the foreground and a blurry background.

name: The Old Guitarist
highlights: From Picasso's Blue Period, depicting a ghostly figure with a guitar. The guitar's warm color contrasts with the blue, symbolizing hope amidst poverty.

name: Water Lilies
highlights: A series of 250 paintings of lilies from Monet's own pond. Blends impressionism and expressionism, giving Monet universal recognition.

name: The Son of Man
highlights: A surreal self-portrait with a green apple hovering in front of the face. It provokes ambiguity with peculiar elements like the backward-bending arm.

name: The Treachery of Images
highlights: Famous for the phrase 'This is not a pipe.' It highlights the gap between words and reality, showing that the painting is just a representation.

name: No. 5, 1948
highlights: A pioneering abstract expressionist work created with the drip method. Also known as 'action painting,' it allows psychological connection.

name: Composition with Red Blue and Yellow
highlights: Iconic Neoplasticism featuring bold colors and black borders. Aims to achieve aesthetic balance through contrastive colors.

name: Ophelia
highlights: Depicts Ophelia from Hamlet drowning while singing. The surrounding flowers represent purity and innocence, portrayed from imagination.

name: Salvator Mundi
highlights: Shows Jesus as the savior of the world holding a crystal orb. It became the most expensive painting ever sold at auction in 2017.

name: Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird
highlights: Features symbolic elements like a thorn necklace, monkey, and black cat. Represents Frida's painful life and mental state after her divorce.

name: The Peaceable Kingdom
highlights: Naïve art depicting a biblical prophecy of harmony between animals and humans. Also features William Penn enacting a treaty in the background.

name: The Ninth Wave
highlights: Depicts a boat surviving a storm with debris forming a cross. Symbolizes Christian salvation and the beauty of the sea.

name: Mr. and Mrs. Andrews
highlights: A celebrated double portrait of a newly married couple in a pastoral setting. Represents British art and aristocracy.

name: Pollice Verso
highlights: Depicts a defeated gladiator pleading for mercy while spectators give a thumbs-down. Inspired many films with its dramatic portrayal.

name: The Embarkation to Cythera
highlights: Depicts a 'fête galante' celebration in a pastoral setting. Known for its hazy, dreamy ambiance created by soft brush strokes.

name: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
highlights: Manet's last work depicting a barmaid at a famous venue. Famous for the mirror reflection showing a customer and the bustling hall.

name: The Laughing Cavalier
highlights: A portrait of an unknown man whose upward mustache and eyes provoke humor. A masterpiece of male portraiture from the Dutch Golden Age.

name: The Fox
highlights: A cubist painting experimenting with abstract styles and vibrant colors. Features symbolic animals violating realistic forms.

name: The Lady of Shalott
highlights: Depicts the cursed character from Tennyson's poem. Shows her floating on a boat after looking at Sir Lancelot, painted in landscape style.

name: The Night Watch
highlights: Depicts the Militia Company of District II. Famous for the mysterious girl in gold representing the company and the dynamic composition.

name: The Card Players
highlights: Part of a series showing peasants playing cards. Focuses on humble figures and their intense concentration rather than grand subjects.

name: The Grand Canal, Venice
highlights: A brilliant romantic landscape capturing the light and atmosphere of Venice, showcasing Turner's mastery of marine painting.

name: A Boat Passing a Lock
highlights: A classic landscape by Constable depicting the rural life of the Stour Valley with his signature attention to sky and natural detail.

name: Sacred and Profane Love
highlights: A wedding gift for Nicolo Aurelio and Laura Bagarotto. The landscape is symbolic: the hill for prudence, the plain for peace, and rabbits for fertility.

name: The Ancient of Days
highlights: Depicts God as the Great Architect at the moment of creation. He is shown not establishing order, but limiting freedom and denoting the limits of imagination.

name: The Madonna Litta
highlights: Named after Count Litta, its former owner. Theories suggest the baby figure, with its unusual pose, might have been painted by one of da Vinci's students.

name: Las Meninas
highlights: Depicts Infanta Margarita and includes the painter himself. The complex composition with mirror reflections makes it a three-dimensional masterpiece of philosophy in art.

name: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
highlights: An iconic work depicting the murder of John the Baptist in a prison setting. Known for its incredible realism, semi-darkness, and expressive faces.

name: The Return of the Prodigal Son
highlights: Rembrandt's largest religious canvas, painted in his final years. Dedicated to the parable of the prodigal son, it is a masterpiece of forgiveness.

name: Christ Carrying the Cross
highlights: One of at least seven copies, showing its popularity. El Greco focused on the humanity of Christ rather than the divine, emphasizing emotion.

name: Perseus and Andromeda
highlights: A Classical Baroque masterpiece illustrating struggle, victory, and love. The almost monochrome coloring helps the characters harmonize with the dark stone background.

name: Deposition from the Cross
highlights: Created in the Mannerism style, distinguished by special pretentiousness and artistic positions. Reveals the essence of Vasari's creative approach to biblical themes.

name: Geopoliticus Child Watching the Birth of the New Man
highlights: A prophetic work where the Old World is a biological process and a New Man is born in the other hemisphere. Represents a shift in global power.

name: Blue Dancers
highlights: Dates back to Degas's late period when his vision weakened. Painted in large spots of color, prioritizing the decorative organization of the surface.

name: Souvenir from Havre
highlights: A notable work from Picasso's Analytic Cubism period, utilizing oil and sand on canvas. It deconstructs the subject into geometric forms.

name: The Luncheon on the Grass
highlights: A pivotal work in modern art that caused a scandal for depicting a female nude with fully dressed men. It bridges Realism and Impressionism.

name: Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette
highlights: A masterpiece of Impressionism capturing a lively Sunday afternoon in Montmartre. Famous for its dappled light and vibrant depiction of Parisian social life.

name: The Calling of St Matthew
highlights: A defining work of the Baroque period, renowned for its dramatic use of chiaroscuro (light and shadow) to depict the moment Jesus inspires Matthew to follow him.

name: Grande Odalisque
highlights: A Neoclassical painting depicting an odalisque. Famous for the elongated proportions of the figure's back, prioritizing aesthetic line over anatomical reality.

name: Dance II
highlights: A key work of Fauvism featuring five dancing figures in red against a green and blue background. It conveys primal energy and emotional liberation.

name: The Milkmaid
highlights: One of Vermeer's most famous works, depicting a domestic kitchen scene with incredible attention to light, texture, and quiet concentration.

name: David
highlights: A masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture created in marble. It depicts the biblical hero David before his battle with Goliath, symbolizing the defense of civil liberties.

name: The Thinker
highlights: Originally conceived as part of The Gates of Hell, this bronze sculpture portrays a nude male figure sitting on a rock in deep contemplation, representing philosophy.

name: Venus de Milo
highlights: One of the most famous works of ancient Greek sculpture. Notable for the mystery of her missing arms, it depicts Aphrodite, the goddess of love and beauty.

name: Pietà
highlights: A marble structure depicting the body of Jesus on the lap of his mother Mary after the Crucifixion. It balances the Renaissance ideals of classical beauty with naturalism.

name: Campbell's Soup Cans
highlights: A defining work of the Pop Art movement. It consists of 32 canvases, each depicting a flavor of Campbell's Soup, challenging traditional definitions of art.

name: Nefertiti Bust
highlights: A 3,300-year-old painted limestone bust of the Great Royal Wife of Pharaoh Akhenaten. It is a global icon of feminine beauty and power.

name: Winged Victory of Samothrace
highlights: A Hellenistic marble sculpture of Nike, the goddess of victory. Admired for the masterful rendering of motion and the wet drapery clinging to the body.

name: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa
highlights: A High Baroque masterpiece depicting the saint swooning in a state of religious ecstasy. It uses hidden windows to illuminate the bronze rays and marble figures.

name: Marilyn Diptych
highlights: Completed weeks after Marilyn Monroe's death. The contrast between the vivid colored panel and the fading black and white panel suggests her life and eventual death.

name: Composition VIII
highlights: A geometric abstract work that emphasizes the relationship between form and color. Kandinsky believed painting should evoke the same emotional resonance as music.

name: Apollo and Daphne
highlights: A life-sized Baroque marble sculpture showing the metamorphosis of Daphne into a laurel tree to escape the god Apollo. The texture of skin turning to bark is masterful.

name: Discobolus
highlights: Known as 'The Discus Thrower', this is a Roman copy of a lost Greek bronze original. It is the defining symbol of athletic energy and harmony.

name: Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss
highlights: A masterpiece of Neoclassical sculpture. It depicts the tender moment when the god Cupid awakens the lifeless Psyche with a kiss.

name: Laocoön and His Sons
highlights: A monumental marble sculpture depicting the Trojan priest Laocoön and his sons being attacked by sea serpents. It is famous for its agony and physical tension.

name: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
overview: An archaeologist tries to beat a band of Nazis to a unique religious relic which is central to their plans for world domination.
highlights: The ancient city stood in for the Canyon of the Crescent Moon, where Indiana Jones finds the Holy Grail.

name: The Sound of Music
overview: A young novice is sent by her convent in 1930s Austria to become a governess to the seven children of a widowed naval officer.
highlights: The 'Do-Re-Mi' song steps and the Pegasus Fountain are located here, tracing the footsteps of Maria von Trapp.

name: Inception
overview: A thief who steals corporate secrets through the use of dream-sharing technology is given the inverse task of planting an idea into the mind of a C.E.O.
highlights: The specific fortress design inspired the dream levels within the film.

name: The Grand Budapest Hotel
overview: A writer encounters the owner of an aging high-class hotel, who tells him of his early years serving as a lobby boy in the hotel's glorious years.
highlights: The stunning Art Nouveau interior of this department store was transformed into the hotel's lobby.

name: Star Wars: Attack of the Clones
overview: Ten years after meeting, Anakin Skywalker shares a forbidden romance with Padmé Amidala while Obi-Wan investigates an assassination attempt.
highlights: Anakin and Padmé's secret wedding was filmed at this villa overlooking Lake Como.

name: The Hunger Games
overview: Katniss Everdeen voluntarily takes her younger sister's place in the Hunger Games: a televised competition in which two teenagers from each of the twelve Districts of Panem are chosen at random to fight to the death.
highlights: The forest was used for the Arena scenes where Katniss hunts and hides.

name: Lost in Translation
overview: A faded movie star and a neglected young woman form an unlikely bond after crossing paths in Tokyo.
highlights: Bob and Charlotte meet at the New York Bar on the 52nd floor of this hotel.

name: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
overview: When their relationship turns sour, a couple undergoes a medical procedure to have each other erased from their memories.
highlights: The location associated with the famous whisper 'Meet me in Montauk' and the opening train scenes.

name: La La Land
overview: While navigating their careers in Los Angeles, a pianist and an actress fall in love while attempting to reconcile their aspirations for the future.
highlights: The famous jazz club where Sebastian introduces Mia to pure jazz.

name: Game of Thrones
overview: Political intrigue and supernatural threats collide as noble families fight for control of Westeros.
highlights: Thingvellir was used as the Bloody Gate and various scenes in the North, including Arya's journey.

name: Vikings
overview: The life and exploits of Ragnar Lothbrok across historic Scandinavia.
highlights: Lough Tay served as the iconic Viking village Kattegat.

name: Sherlock
overview: A modern interpretation of Sherlock Holmes solving cases in London.
highlights: Speedy's Café stands in for the exterior of 221B Baker Street.

name: Stranger Things
overview: A group of kids confront supernatural mysteries in Hawkins.
highlights: The exterior of Hawkins Lab was filmed at Emory University.

name: Breaking Bad
overview: A chemistry teacher turns into a drug kingpin.
highlights: The White family home became one of TV's most iconic locations.

name: Better Call Saul
overview: Jimmy McGill's journey into becoming Saul Goodman.
highlights: Loyola's is a recurring location for important conversations.

name: Crash Landing on You
overview: A South Korean heiress lands in North Korea, beginning an impossible romance.
highlights: Lucerne was used for key emotional scenes in the drama.

name: Goblin (Guardian: The Lonely and Great God)
overview: An immortal goblin searches for his destined bride.
highlights: The castle and old town were featured heavily in key scenes.

name: Narcos
overview: A gritty portrayal of the rise of Pablo Escobar.
highlights: Filmed in Medellín's real neighborhoods for authenticity.

name: Dark
overview: A time-loop mystery spanning generations.
highlights: Forest scenes around the caves were filmed in Grunewald.

name: Peaky Blinders
overview: A gangster family's rise in post-WWI Birmingham.
highlights: The museum's preserved streets were used extensively.

name: The Last of Us
overview: A hardened survivor escorts an immune girl through a devastated America.
highlights: The flyover was used for the Boston Quarantine Zone chase scene.

name: The Witcher
overview: Geralt of Rivia battles monsters and political forces.
highlights: The ruined castle was used in the epic Battle of Sodden.

name: Sense8
overview: Eight strangers across the world share a psychic connection.
highlights: Major crowd scenes and emotional sequences were filmed here.

name: Downton Abbey
overview: A British aristocratic family navigates social change.
highlights: Highclere Castle appears as the Crawley family's estate.

name: Lost
overview: Survivors of a plane crash encounter mysteries on a remote island.
highlights: Most jungle and beach scenes were filmed around Oahu's North Shore.

name: Chernobyl
overview: A dramatization of the 1986 nuclear disaster and the investigation that followed.
highlights: The Soviet-style district doubled as Pripyat.

name: Emily in Paris
overview: An American woman adjusts to life and work in Paris.
highlights: Emily's apartment square is one of the show's most recognizable spots.

name: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
overview: A daydreaming man escapes into grand fantasies while seeking a missing photograph.
highlights: The iconic longboard downhill scene was filmed on the winding roads of Seyðisfjörður.

name: The Crown
overview: Follows the political rivalries and romance of Queen Elizabeth II's reign and the events that shaped the second half of the twentieth century.
highlights: A lavish townhouse neighboring the real Queen's home, used to double for the interior of Buckingham Palace.

name: Avatar
overview: A paraplegic Marine dispatched to the moon Pandora on a unique mission becomes torn between following his orders and protecting the world he feels is his home.
highlights: Used for non-CGI scenes representing the lush jungles of Pandora.

name: Harry Potter (Oxford)
overview: An orphaned boy enrolls in a school of wizardry, where he learns the truth about himself, his family and the terrible evil that haunts the magical world.
highlights: Duke Humfrey's Library served as the Hogwarts Library, and the Divinity School served as the infirmary.

name: The Talented Mr. Ripley
overview: In late 1950s New York, Tom Ripley, a young underachiever, is sent to Italy to retrieve a rich and spoiled millionaire playboy, named Dickie Greenleaf.
highlights: The arrival point for Ripley in the fictional 'Mongibello' was filmed near this stunning 12th-century castle.

name: Slumdog Millionaire
overview: A Mumbai teenager reflects on his life after being accused of cheating on the Indian version of 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?'.
highlights: The memorable closing dance sequence 'Jai Ho' was filmed in this historic train station.

name: Harry Potter (Viaduct)
overview: The second installment of the boy wizard's adventures, featuring the flying car sequence.
highlights: Famous as the 'Harry Potter Bridge' where the Hogwarts Express travels.

name: The Avengers
overview: Earth's mightiest heroes must come together and learn to fight as a team if they are going to stop the mischievous Loki and his alien army from enslaving humanity.
highlights: The vast laboratory scenes were filmed in the Space Power Facility's vacuum chamber.

name: Green Book
overview: A working-class Italian-American bouncer becomes the driver of an African-American classical pianist on a tour of venues through the 1960s American South.
highlights: Home to the hot dog eating contest scene in the film.

name: Star Wars: A New Hope
overview: Luke Skywalker joins forces with a Jedi Knight, a cocky pilot, a Wookiee and two droids to save the galaxy from the Empire's world-destroying battle station.
highlights: Famous as the Lars homestead on Tatooine where Luke grew up.

name: X-Men
overview: In a world where mutants (evolved super-powered humans) exist and are discriminated against, two groups form for an inevitable clash.
highlights: The Gooderham and Worts Distillery was used to recreate the look of industrial 1940s Poland.

name: Mad Max: Fury Road
overview: In a post-apocalyptic wasteland, a woman rebels against a tyrannical ruler in search for her homeland with the aid of a group of female prisoners, a psychotic worshiper, and a drifter named Max.
highlights: The stark, dramatic dunes of Namibia replaced Australia to create the barren, post-apocalyptic landscape.

name: Black Panther
overview: T'Challa, heir to the hidden but advanced kingdom of Wakanda, must step forward to lead his people into a new future and must confront a challenger from his country's past.
highlights: Featured prominently in the high-speed car chase scene.

name: Star Wars: A New Hope (Yavin)
overview: The Rebel Alliance launches an attack on the Death Star from their hidden base.
highlights: The Mayan temple ruins served as the Massassi Outpost rebel base on Yavin IV.

name: Amélie
overview: Amélie is an innocent and naive girl in Paris with her own sense of justice. She decides to help those around her and, along the way, discovers love.
highlights: The famed café where Amélie worked in the film, located in Montmartre.

name: The Dark Knight Rises
overview: Eight years after the Joker's reign of anarchy, Batman, with the help of the enigmatic Catwoman, is forced from his exile to save Gotham City from the brutal guerrilla terrorist Bane.
highlights: The prison pit scenes where Bruce Wayne climbs out were filmed against the backdrop of this fort.

name: Mary Poppins Returns
overview: Decades after her original visit, the magical nanny returns to help the Banks siblings and Michael's children through a difficult time in their lives.
highlights: Filming locations included the Bank of England and Royal Exchange to capture Victorian detail.

name: Home Alone
overview: An eight-year-old troublemaker must protect his house from a pair of burglars when he is accidentally left home alone by his family during Christmas vacation.
highlights: The stunning red-brick family home that Kevin defends.

name: Mamma Mia!
overview: The story of a bride-to-be trying to find her real father told using hit songs by the popular 1970s group ABBA.
highlights: The outdoor beach scenes were filmed on this island, putting it on the map.

name: Gladiator
overview: A former Roman General sets out to exact vengeance against the corrupt emperor who murdered his family and sent him into slavery.
highlights: The mud-brick fortified city served as the slave-trading city of Zucchabar.

name: When Harry Met Sally
overview: Harry and Sally have known each other for years, and are very good friends, but they fear sex would ruin the friendship.
highlights: The location of the iconic 'I'll have what she's having' scene.

name: The King's Speech
overview: The story of King George VI, his impromptu ascension to the throne of the British Empire in 1936, and the speech therapist who helped the unsure monarch overcome his stammer.
highlights: Used to represent Westminster Abbey in preparation for the coronation.

name: The Godfather
overview: The aging patriarch of an organized crime dynasty transfers control of his clandestine empire to his reluctant son.
highlights: Stood in for the town of Corleone, featuring the bar where Michael Corleone asks for Apollonia's hand.

name: Notting Hill
overview: The life of a simple bookshop owner changes when he meets the most famous film star in the world.
highlights: The location of the famous Travel Book Shop.

name: Ghostbusters
overview: Three parapsychologists forced out of their university funding set up a unique ghost removal service in New York City.
highlights: The site of the first ghost encounter in the film.

name: Forrest Gump
overview: The presidencies of Kennedy and Johnson, the Vietnam War, the Watergate scandal and other historical events unfold from the perspective of an Alabama man with an IQ of 75.
highlights: The location where the famous park bench scenes were filmed (the bench is now in a museum).

name: Rain Man
overview: Selfish yuppie Charlie Babbitt's father leaves a fortune to his savant brother Raymond and a pittance to Charlie; they travel cross-country.
highlights: The 'Emperor's Suite' where the brothers stayed is still referred to as the Rain Man Suite.

name: Jurassic Park
overview: A pragmatic paleontologist touring an almost complete theme park on an island in Central America is tasked with protecting a couple of kids after a power failure causes the park's cloned dinosaurs to run loose.
highlights: The dramatic coastline seen when the cast first approaches Isla Nublar by helicopter.

name: Pirates of the Caribbean
overview: Blacksmith Will Turner teams up with eccentric pirate 'Captain' Jack Sparrow to save his love, the governor's daughter, from Jack's former pirate allies, who are now undead.
highlights: Served as the setting for Port Royal.

name: Les Misérables
overview: In 19th-century France, Jean Valjean, who for decades has been hunted by the ruthless policeman Javert after breaking parole, agrees to care for a factory worker's daughter.
highlights: While the story is set here and in Paris, the 2012 movie was primarily filmed in England (e.g., Winchester, Bath).

name: Django Unchained
overview: With the help of a German bounty-hunter, a freed slave sets out to rescue his wife from a brutal plantation-owner in Mississippi.
highlights: Many western town scenes were filmed at this historic ranch once owned by Gene Autry.

name: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider
overview: Video game adventurer Lara Croft comes to life in a movie where she races against time and villains to recover powerful ancient artifacts.
highlights: Famous for the massive trees growing out of the temple ruins.

name: In Bruges
overview: Guilt-stricken after a job gone wrong, hitman Ray and his partner await orders from their ruthless boss in Bruges, Belgium.
highlights: The medieval bell tower is a central location in the film's climax.

name: The Lord of the Rings
overview: A meek Hobbit from the Shire and eight companions set out on a journey to destroy the powerful One Ring and save Middle-earth from the Dark Lord Sauron.
highlights: The preserved set of the Shire, featuring the Hobbit holes.

name: Twilight
overview: A teenage girl risks everything when she falls in love with a vampire.
highlights: The actual house used as Charlie and Bella Swan's home.

name: Bridget Jones's Diary
overview: Bridget Jones is determined to improve herself while she looks for love in a year in which she keeps a personal diary.
highlights: The scene where Daniel Cleaver falls into the lake was filmed here.

name: Sex and the City
overview: A New York writer on sex and love is finally getting married to her Mr. Big. But her three best girlfriends must console her after one of them inadvertently leads Mr. Big to jilt her.
highlights: The famous front stoop used as the exterior for Carrie Bradshaw's apartment.

name: Silver Linings Playbook
overview: After a stint in a mental institution, former teacher Pat Solitano moves back in with his parents and tries to reconcile with his ex-wife.
highlights: Pat and Tiffany share a memorable scene in a specific booth at this diner.

name: Ocean's 8
overview: Debbie Ocean gathers an all-female crew to attempt an impossible heist at New York City's yearly Met Gala.
highlights: The glamorous jewelry heist takes place during the star-studded Met Gala.

name: Titanic
overview: A seventeen-year-old aristocrat falls in love with a kind but poor artist aboard the luxurious, ill-fated R.M.S. Titanic.
highlights: The massive Titanic replica was built in a giant water tank here.

name: Pretty Woman
overview: A man in a legal but hurtful business needs an escort for some social events, and hires a beautiful prostitute he meets... only to fall in love.
highlights: The luxury hotel where Edward and Vivian stay during the film.

name: Trinity College Library
overview: The largest library in Ireland, serving Trinity College and the University of Dublin. It houses the famous Book of Kells.
history_significance: Founded in 1592. The Old Library was built between 1712 and 1732. It is a legal deposit library for Ireland and the UK.
highlights:
The Long Room with its barrel-vaulted ceiling.
The Book of Kells.
The Brian Boru Harp.

name: New York Public Library (Main Branch)
overview: The Stephen A. Schwarzman Building is the flagship building of the NYPL system, a Beaux-Arts landmark.
history_significance: Dedicated in 1911. It was the largest marble structure in the US at the time of its construction.
highlights:
The Rose Main Reading Room with cloud murals.
The Patience and Fortitude lion statues outside.
The Gutenberg Bible.

name: Strahov Monastery Library
overview: A breathtaking library located inside the Strahov Monastery, featuring two magnificent baroque halls.
history_significance: The Theological Hall was completed in 1679, and the Philosophical Hall was built in the late 18th century to house growing collections.
highlights:
The ceiling frescoes depicting the struggle of mankind to know real wisdom.
The Curiosity Cabinet.
The ornate walnut shelving.

name: Clementinum National Library
overview: Often cited as one of the most beautiful libraries in the world, located in a historic complex of buildings.
history_significance: Established by Jesuits in 1622. The Baroque Library Hall was finished in 1722 and has remained untouched since.
highlights:
The collection of terrestrial globes.
The frescoes by Jan Hiebl.
The astronomical tower.

name: Admont Abbey Library
overview: The largest monastery library in the world, known for its dazzling white and gold Rococo architecture.
history_significance: Completed in 1776. The architecture represents the ideals of the Enlightenment, symbolizing light and knowledge.
highlights:
The 'Four Last Things' sculptures.
The seven ceiling frescoes depicting stages of human understanding.
The secret doors disguised as books.

name: Real Gabinete Português de Leitura
overview: A stunning library housing the largest collection of Portuguese literature outside of Portugal.
history_significance: Founded in 1837 by Portuguese immigrants. The building, completed in 1887, is a masterpiece of Neomanueline architecture.
highlights:
The limestone facade inspired by the Jerónimos Monastery.
The iron chandelier.
The three-story wooden bookshelves reaching the stained-glass skylight.

name: Bodleian Library
overview: The main research library of the University of Oxford and one of the oldest libraries in Europe.
history_significance: Opened to scholars in 1602. It holds a copy of every book published in the UK and Ireland.
highlights:
The Radcliffe Camera rotunda.
Duke Humfrey's Library (medieval section).
The Divinity School ceiling.

name: Austrian National Library
overview: Located in the Hofburg Palace, the State Hall (Prunksaal) is a jewel of Baroque architecture.
history_significance: Built in the 18th century under Emperor Charles VI. It served as the imperial court library.
highlights:
The central dome fresco by Daniel Gran.
The statues of Habsburg rulers.
The collection of Venetian globes.

name: Tianjin Binhai Library
overview: A futuristic library nicknamed 'The Eye', featuring a luminous spherical auditorium in the center.
history_significance: Opened in 2017. Designed by MVRDV, it became instantly famous for its terraced shelving that echoes the sphere.
highlights:
The 'Eye' auditorium.
The floor-to-ceiling terraced bookshelves.
The flowing, cavernous interior design.

name: Shakespeare and Company
overview: A legendary English-language bookstore on the Left Bank, serving as a haven for writers and readers.
history_significance: Opened in 1951 by George Whitman. It became a center for Beat Generation writers like Ginsberg and Burroughs.
highlights:
The 'Tumbleweeds' beds for aspiring writers.
The wishing well.
The chaotic, cozy stacks of books.

name: Daunt Books (Marylebone)
overview: An Edwardian bookshop famous for its long oak galleries and arrangement of books by country.
history_significance: Built in 1910 for antiquarian booksellers. It retains its original skylights and wooden interior.
highlights:
The long oak galleries.
The stained glass windows.
The travel section arranged geographically.

name: Boekhandel Dominicanen
overview: A spectacular bookstore located inside a 700-year-old converted Gothic church.
history_significance: The church was consecrated in 1294. It was repurposed into a bookstore in 2006, preserving the religious architecture.
highlights:
The multi-story black steel book stack.
The preserved ceiling frescoes.
The coffee shop in the former altar.

name: The Last Bookstore
overview: California's largest used and new book and record store, located in a former bank building.
history_significance: Founded in 2005. It is known for its whimsical art installations made of books.
highlights:
The tunnel made of books.
The hidden book vaults.
The mammoth head on the wall.

name: Cărturești Carusel
overview: Known as the 'Carousel of Light', this bookstore is housed in a restored 19th-century building.
history_significance: The building was confiscated by the communist regime and later restored by the grandson of the original owner in 2015.
highlights:
The spiraling white staircases.
The abundance of natural light.
The top floor bistro.

name: Zhongshuge Bookstore
overview: A visually stunning bookstore that uses mirrors to create an illusion of infinite books.
history_significance: Part of a modern chain of bookstores in China known for avant-garde interior design.
highlights:
The mirrored ceiling creating a tunnel effect.
The theatrical reading oval.
The kids' section designed like a forest.

name: Libreria Acqua Alta
overview: A whimsical 'bookstore of high water' where books are stored in bathtubs and boats to protect them from flooding.
history_significance: Created to adapt to Venice's periodic flooding (Acqua Alta), turning a problem into a unique feature.
highlights:
The full-sized gondola filled with books.
The staircase made of ruined encyclopedias.
The fire escape door opening directly to the canal.

name: George Peabody Library
overview: Part of Johns Hopkins University, described as a 'cathedral of books' due to its soaring atrium.
history_significance: Opened in 1878. It was a gift from philanthropist George Peabody to the citizens of Baltimore.
highlights:
The five tiers of ornamental cast-iron balconies.
The massive skylight.
The Neo-Greco interior design.

name: Wiblingen Monastery Library
overview: A masterpiece of Rococo architecture located in a former Benedictine abbey.
history_significance: Completed in 1744. The design was intended to awaken a desire for knowledge and spiritual devotion.
highlights:
The winding gallery supported by columns.
The statues representing virtues and disciplines.
The ceiling fresco depicting the Fall of Man.

name: Melk Abbey Library
overview: A world-famous high Baroque library overlooking the Danube river.
history_significance: Reconstructed in the early 18th century. It famously appears in Umberto Eco's novel 'The Name of the Rose'.
highlights:
The ceiling fresco by Paul Troger.
The spiral staircase connecting the library to the church.
The collection of medieval manuscripts.

name: Biblioteca Vasconcelos
overview: A 'megalibrary' known for its transparent walls and hanging bookshelves that look like a matrix.
history_significance: Inaugurated in 2006. Designed by Alberto Kalach to be an ark of knowledge in a botanical garden.
highlights:
The 'Matrix Mobile' whale skeleton sculpture.
The floating bookshelf illusion.
The surrounding botanical gardens.

name: Royal Library of Copenhagen (Black Diamond)
overview: A striking modern extension to the Royal Library, named for its polished black granite cladding.
history_significance: Completed in 1999. It serves as a cultural center as well as a library, bridging the harbor and the city.
highlights:
The tilting black granite facade.
The 200-square-meter ceiling painting by Per Kirkeby.
The harbor views.

name: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
overview: The rare book library of Yale University, one of the world's largest buildings dedicated entirely to rare books.
history_significance: Completed in 1963. Its unique design protects books from direct light while allowing a soft glow.
highlights:
The translucent Vermont marble panels.
The six-story glass tower of book stacks.
The Gutenberg Bible on display.

name: British Library
overview: The national library of the UK and one of the largest libraries in the world by number of items.
history_significance: Separated from the British Museum in 1973. The St Pancras building opened in 1998.
highlights:
The King's Library Tower.
The Treasures Gallery (Magna Carta, Beatles lyrics).
The massive brick architecture.

name: Boston Public Library
overview: The first large free municipal library in the US, known as a 'palace for the people'.
history_significance: The McKim building was built in 1895. It set the standard for American library architecture.
highlights:
Bates Hall with its green reading lamps.
The Sargent Gallery murals.
The Italian Renaissance-style courtyard.

name: Handelingenkamer
overview: The library of the Dutch House of Representatives, famous for its red cast-iron spiral stairs.
history_significance: Built in the late 19th century. It was designed to store the transcripts of parliamentary debates.
highlights:
The Dragon-style red ironwork.
The glass roof allowing natural light (originally for candles).
The towering walls of books.

name: National Library of France (Richelieu)
overview: The historic site of the BnF, recently renovated to reveal its full architectural splendor.
history_significance: Located in the former palace of Cardinal Mazarin. The Oval Room was designed in the late 19th century.
highlights:
The Oval Room (Salle Ovale).
The Labrouste Room with its iron domes.
The museum of precious coins and antiques.

name: Stockholm Public Library
overview: A quintessential example of Nordic Classicism designed by Erik Gunnar Asplund.
history_significance: Opened in 1928. It was the first library in Sweden with open shelves for direct public access.
highlights:
The massive central rotunda.
The textured orange facade.
The panoramic view of books surrounding the visitor.

name: Library of Parliament
overview: The main information repository for the Parliament of Canada, a High Victorian Gothic masterpiece.
history_significance: Completed in 1876. It is the only part of the original Centre Block to survive the fire of 1916.
highlights:
The flying buttresses and iron dome.
The white pine statue of Queen Victoria.
The intricate wood paneling.

name: Cafebrería El Péndulo
overview: A bookstore-cafe known for its lush greenery, with plants cascading over the balconies.
history_significance: Combines a bookstore with a cultural center and restaurant, creating a social hub for literature.
highlights:
The trees growing inside the store.
The winding staircases.
The live music and poetry readings.

name: Ler Devagar
overview: Located in the LX Factory arts complex, this bookstore occupies a former printing press space.
history_significance: The name means 'Read Slowly'. It preserved the original industrial machinery of the building.
highlights:
The flying bicycle sculpture suspended from the ceiling.
The massive original printing press.
The floor-to-ceiling book walls.

name: Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books)
overview: A modern architectural marvel dedicated to books, music, and movies, designed for a premium lifestyle.
history_significance: Designed by Klein Dytham Architecture. It redefined the bookstore experience in Japan as a curated cultural space.
highlights:
The facade made of interlocking 'T' shapes.
The magazine street.
The Anjin library lounge.

name: City Lights Booksellers
overview: A landmark independent bookstore and publisher that became the hub of the Beat Generation.
history_significance: Founded in 1953 by poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti. It is famous for publishing Allen Ginsberg's 'Howl'.
highlights:
The Poetry Room.
The politically progressive selection.
The historic signage.

name: Eslite Spectrum Songyan
overview: Part of the famous Eslite chain, located in a tobacco factory turned cultural park.
history_significance: Eslite is renowned for creating the 24-hour bookstore concept (originally at Dunnan). This branch focuses on lifestyle and design.
highlights:
The curved aesthetic and warm lighting.
The integration with artisan shops.
The tea rooms.

name: Atlantis Books
overview: A charming independent bookstore nestled into the basement of a traditional white-washed Cycladic house.
history_significance: Founded in 2004 by a group of friends from Cyprus, England, and the US who noticed the island lacked a bookstore.
highlights:
The terrace overlooking the Aegean Sea.
The hand-painted signs.
The cave-like interior.

name: Morgan Library & Museum
overview: A scholarly library and museum originally built as the private library of financier J. Pierpont Morgan.
history_significance: Built between 1902 and 1906. It houses an incredible collection of illuminated manuscripts and rare drawings.
highlights:
Pierpont Morgan's Study.
The East Room with triple-tier walnut bookcases.
The 16th-century tapestry.

name: Suzzallo Library
overview: The central library of the University of Washington, famous for its Collegiate Gothic architecture.
history_significance: Opened in 1926. The Graduate Reading Room is often compared to a cathedral or the Great Hall in Harry Potter.
highlights:
The Graduate Reading Room.
The 35-foot-high stained glass windows.
The terracotta figures on the facade.

name: Raza Library
overview: A repository of Indo-Islamic cultural heritage, housed in a magnificent palace.
history_significance: Founded in 1774 by Nawab Faizullah Khan. The current building was built in 1904.
highlights:
The vast collection of rare manuscripts and miniatures.
The Indo-Saracenic architecture.
The calligraphy specimens.

name: Chetham's Library
overview: The oldest public library in the English-speaking world, housed in a medieval sandstone building.
history_significance: Established in 1653. It was a meeting place for Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
highlights:
The desk where Marx and Engels worked.
The chained books.
The medieval timber roof.

name: Mafra Palace Library
overview: A monumental Rococo library located within the Palace of Mafra, containing over 36,000 leather-bound volumes.
history_significance: Built in the 18th century. It is known for the bats that live inside and eat insects that would damage the books.
highlights:
The Rococo shelving.
The marble floor.
The resident bats.

name: Vatican Apostolic Library
overview: The library of the Holy See, one of the oldest and most secret libraries in the world.
history_significance: Formally established in 1475, though its roots are older. It holds immense historical archives.
highlights:
The Sistine Hall.
The Codex Vaticanus (oldest Bible manuscript).
The frescoes depicting the history of the library.

name: Powell's City of Books
overview: The largest independent new and used bookstore in the world, occupying a full city block.
history_significance: Founded in 1971. It is a landmark of Portland, known for its color-coded rooms.
highlights:
The Rare Book Room.
The sheer scale of the inventory.
The color-coded navigation system.

name: Strand Bookstore
overview: A historic independent bookstore in the East Village, famous for its slogan '18 Miles of Books'.
history_significance: Founded in 1927. It is one of the survivors of the old 'Book Row' of NYC.
highlights:
The outdoor bargain bins.
The Rare Book Room on the top floor.
The '18 miles of books' signage.

name: Escorial Library
overview: Part of the Royal Site of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, a Renaissance masterpiece.
history_significance: Founded by Philip II in the 16th century. It was the first library to display books with their spines facing inward (gold edges out).
highlights:
The vaulted ceiling frescoes representing the seven liberal arts.
The globes and armillary spheres.
The walnut bookcases.

name: Vennesla Library
overview: A modern cultural center known for its unique rib-like wooden architecture.
history_significance: Opened in 2011. The 27 timber ribs serve as structure, lighting, and bookshelves all in one.
highlights:
The glue-laminated timber 'ribs'.
The cozy reading nooks inside the ribs.
The sustainable low-energy design.

name: British Museum Reading Room
overview: Located in the center of the British Museum's Great Court, famous for its magnificent domed ceiling.
history_significance: Historically the main reading room of the British Library before its move in 2000. Frequent visitors included Karl Marx, Oscar Wilde, and Lenin.
highlights:
The papier-mâché domed ceiling.
The Great Court architecture.
The curatorial exhibitions.

name: National Library of St. Mark's
overview: Biblioteca Marciana is a Renaissance masterpiece located in Piazza San Marco, holding one of the world's most important classical text collections.
history_significance: Construction began in 1537 by Jacopo Sansovino. It is one of the earliest surviving public manuscript depositories.
highlights:
The Renaissance architecture.
The ceiling roundels by Titian and Veronese.
The Grimani Breviary.

name: Thomas Fisher Rare Book Library
overview: Affiliated with the University of Toronto, this library houses the largest collection of rare books in Canada.
history_significance: Opened in 1973. It preserves significant works including Newton's Principia and Shakespeare's First Folio.
highlights:
The six tiers of book stacks visible from the lobby.
The Nuremberg Chronicle (1493).
The Babylonian cuneiform tablets.

name: National Library of Sweden
overview: Known as Kungliga biblioteket, located in Humlegården park. It preserves all Swedish printed materials.
history_significance: Its collection dates back to the 16th century. It famously houses the Codex Gigas (Devil's Bible).
highlights:
The Codex Gigas (Devil's Bible).
The Nelly Sachs room.
The underground annexation.

name: Jay Walker's Private Library
overview: A stunning private library owned by inventor Jay Walker, titled 'The Walker Library of the History of Human Imagination'.
history_significance: A contemporary private collection inspired by M.C. Escher's art, celebrating the history of invention and imagination.
highlights:
The Escher-inspired floating platforms.
The original Sputnik 1 backup.
The glass bridge.

name: Salt Lake City Public Library
overview: A modern architectural landmark designed by Moshe Safdie, featuring a massive curved glass wall.
history_significance: Opened in 2003. It was designed to be a 'walking library' with a spiral path ascending to the roof garden.
highlights:
The Urban Room (public piazza).
The rooftop garden with mountain views.
The five-story curved glass wall.

name: Château de Chantilly Library
overview: Part of the Musée Condé within the Chantilly estate, housing a precious collection of medieval manuscripts.
history_significance: The collection was amassed by Henri d'Orléans in the 19th century. It holds the famous 'Tres Riches Heures du Duc de Berry'.
highlights:
The Gutenberg Bible.
The illuminated manuscripts.
The 19th-century reading room decor.

name: Phillips Exeter Academy Library
overview: The largest secondary school library in the world, designed by renowned architect Louis Kahn.
history_significance: Completed in 1971. It is considered one of the finest examples of 20th-century architecture.
highlights:
The massive concrete circular voids.
The natural overhead lighting.
The individual wooden study carrels.

name: Herzog August Library
overview: Also known as Bibliotheca Augusta, it was once the largest library in Europe north of the Alps.
history_significance: Founded in 1572. It is internationally famous for its collection of medieval and early modern manuscripts.
highlights:
The Gospels of Henry the Lion.
The Augusteer hall.
The vast collection of incunabula.

name: Rijksmuseum Library
overview: The largest public art history research library in the Netherlands, located inside the Rijksmuseum.
history_significance: The reading room retains its 19th-century design by Pierre Cuypers, with a skylight and cast-iron decorations.
highlights:
The cast-iron spiral staircase.
The Cuypers Library reading room.
The art history collection.

name: National Library of Singapore
overview: A modern 16-story building featuring bioclimatic architecture and sky gardens.
history_significance: The new building opened in 2005. It replaces the historic red-brick library, symbolizing Singapore's modernization.
highlights:
The 'Pod' on the top floor with city views.
The sky gardens.
The comprehensive collection on Southeast Asia.

name: Cook & Book
overview: A unique combination of restaurant and bookstore divided into nine themed rooms.
history_significance: A modern concept store located near the metro, emphasizing the connection between food and reading.
highlights:
The books hanging from the ceiling in the fiction section.
The vintage car in the travel section.
The greenhouse room.

name: Bibliotheca Hertziana
overview: An art history library of the Max Planck Institute, featuring a striking modern interior within a historic facade.
history_significance: The new building by Juan Navarro Baldeweg (2012) was constructed on the site of a Roman villa, preserving the 'Mascherone' gate.
highlights:
The 'Mascherone' (Big Mask) entrance.
The light-filled central atrium.
The Roman ruins visible in the basement.

name: Kanazawa Umimirai Library
overview: A white box building punctuated by thousands of small round windows, creating a 'forest of books'.
history_significance: Opened in 2011. Designed to be a quiet, light-filled space for reading.
highlights:
The 6,000 circular windows.
The soaring open space.
The automated book retrieval system.

name: National Library of China
overview: One of the largest libraries in the world, with a modern northern extension housing a digital library.
history_significance: The new wing was completed in 2008. Its design symbolizes the importance of culture.
highlights:
The tiered reading area resembling a study canyon.
The glass roof.
The vast collection of Chinese historical documents.

name: Vienna State Opera
overview: One of the leading opera houses in the world, known for its busy schedule and the famous Vienna Opera Ball.
history_significance: Opened in 1869 with Mozart's Don Giovanni. Despite heavy bombing during WWII, it was rebuilt and reopened in 1955.
highlights:
The grand staircase and marble foyer.
The annual Vienna Opera Ball.
The expansive repertoire.

name: Royal Opera House
overview: A major performing arts venue in Covent Garden, home to The Royal Opera and The Royal Ballet.
history_significance: The current building is the third theatre on the site, opened in 1858. It has hosted premieres by Handel and is a cornerstone of British culture.
highlights:
The Paul Hamlyn Hall.
The classic horseshoe-shaped auditorium.
The statues of Melpomene and Thalia.

name: Bolshoi Theatre
overview: A historic theatre holding ballet and opera performances, synonymous with Russian artistic excellence.
history_significance: Established in 1776, the current Neoclassical building opened in 1856. It is the parent stage of the world-renowned Bolshoi Ballet.
highlights:
The Apollo quadriga sculpture.
The lavish gold and red velvet interior.
The six-tier auditorium.

name: Teatro La Fenice
overview: One of the most famous landmarks in the history of Italian theatre, known as 'The Phoenix'.
history_significance: True to its name, it has risen from the ashes of three fires, the latest in 1996. It hosted premieres of operas by Rossini and Verdi.
highlights:
The stunning reconstructed 19th-century interior.
The Sala Grande.
The Apollonian Rooms.

name: Teatro di San Carlo
overview: The oldest continuously active venue for public opera in the world, known for its perfect acoustics.
history_significance: Opened in 1737, decades before La Scala. It set the standard for subsequent European opera house architecture.
highlights:
The royal box.
The gold decorations and blue upholstery.
The ceiling fresco representing Apollo.

name: Metropolitan Opera House
overview: The largest classical music organization in North America, located at Lincoln Center.
