Best Dishes: Venison Meatball. Pickled Partridge.
highlights: Interprets the historical 'Memory of the Surroundings', focusing on game meat and river fish.

name: Cabaña Buenavista
history: Chef Pablo González serves whimsical dishes in a thatched hut surrounded by tropical gardens.
Best Dishes: The Sea (Seafood sequence). Tuna with Chocolate.
highlights: Known for its surprise appetizers served in the garden and a highly experimental tasting menu.

name: Les Cols
history: Fina Puigdevall cooks in the volcanic region of La Garrotxa, using buckwheat and local products.
Best Dishes: Buckwheat Spaghetti. Volcanic Egg.
highlights: Housed in a stunning golden farmhouse, celebrating the austere beauty of the volcanic landscape.

name: Culler de Pau
history: Chef Javier Olleros focuses on the 'Zero Mile' concept in the estuaries of Galicia.
Best Dishes: Spider Crab with Cauliflower. Green Peas with Hake Tripe.
highlights: A minimalist building overlooking the Ria de Arousa, emphasizing the connection between vegetable garden and sea.

name: Miramar
history: Paco Pérez turned a family hostel into a temple of avant-garde seafood cuisine.
Best Dishes: Sea Cucumber Carbonara. Freeze-dried Oyster.
highlights: Located on the promenade, famous for its technical mastery of gelatin and marine flavors.

name: BonAmb
history: Chef Alberto Ferruz explores the history and anthropology of the region through food.
Best Dishes: Cured Tuna Belly. Pickled Vegetables.
highlights: The menu is often divided into 'seasons' like the sun, salt, and time.

name: Ricard Camarena
history: Located in the Bombas Gens art center. Ricard Camarena is the master of vegetable broths and maximizing flavor.
Best Dishes: Roast Onion with Anchovy. Rice with Cow Heel.
highlights: Famous for cooking without water, using only the juices extracted from the ingredients themselves.

name: Retiro da Costiña
history: A family legacy in Galicia where hospitality is paramount. Chef Manuel Costiña leads the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Galician Lobster. Sea Urchin Toast.
highlights: The experience begins in the wine cellar and ends in a lounge with cigars and distillates.

name: Skina
history: Marcos Granda created one of the smallest Michelin-starred restaurants in the world (only four tables).
Best Dishes: Red Prawn Tartare. Suckling Pig.
highlights: Focuses on seasonal Andalusian ingredients with an exceptional wine list.

name: Coque
history: Run by the three Sandoval brothers (Mario, Diego, and Rafael). A sensory journey through different rooms.
Best Dishes: Suckling Pig (cooked in a wood-fired oven). Fermented Vegetables.
highlights: Guests move from the bar to the wine cellar, then the kitchen, and finally the dining room.

name: DSTAgE
history: Chef Diego Guerrero's industrial-chic space. The name stands for 'Days to Smell Taste Amaze Grow Enjoy'.
Best Dishes: Mochi of Huitlacoche. Garlic Prawn.
highlights: A relaxed fine dining atmosphere with no tablecloths and rock music, focusing on creativity.

name: Amelia by Paulo Airaudo
history: Argentinian Chef Paulo Airaudo mixes Italian roots with global influences. Located in the Hotel Villa Favorita.
Best Dishes: Caviar with Banana. Celeriac Cacio e Pepe.
highlights: Overlooks the famous La Concha bay, offering a highly personal tasting menu.

name: Voro
history: Chef Álvaro Salazar offers a free-spirited cuisine ('Voro' means 'devour' in Latin) in Mallorca.
Best Dishes: Mallorcan Suckling Pig. Amberjack with Gazpachuelo.
highlights: Focuses on the depth of Mediterranean flavors with a modern, artistic presentation.

name: El Rincón de Juan Carlos
history: The Padrón brothers elevate Canarian cuisine using local Atlantic products.
Best Dishes: Canarian Potato Mousse. Cherne with Mojo.
highlights: Located in the Royal Hideaway Corales Beach, offering views of the ocean and La Gomera.

name: Bardal
history: Benito Gómez champions the produce of the Serranía de Ronda with an honest, flavor-first approach.
Best Dishes: Rabbit with Snail Stew. Payoyo Cheese Soup.
highlights: A warm, sustainable restaurant that focuses on the distinct flavors of the Andalusian interior.

name: El Poblet
history: Directed by Luis Valls, a disciple of Quique Dacosta. It reinterprets Valencian traditions.
Best Dishes: Eel All i Pebre. Valencian Charcuterie.
highlights: Bold, powerful flavors that pay homage to the local Albufera region.

name: Molino de Urdániz
history: David Yárnoz transformed his family's mill into a minimalist gastronomic destination.
Best Dishes: Cucumber and Oyster. Smoked Trout.
highlights: Known for its silence, harmony, and delicate balance of textures.

name: Pepe Vieira
history: Xosé T. Cannas (Pepe Vieira) explores the 'last kitchen of the world' in Galicia.
Best Dishes: Kamae (Fishing Net) Fish. Spicy Galician Stew.
highlights: The architecture blends seamlessly with the surrounding forest and sea.

name: Paco Roncero
history: Located on the top floor of the Casino de Madrid. Chef Paco Roncero is a technique-driven master.
Best Dishes: The Olive Oil Tasting. Squid Risotto.
highlights: Offers one of the most beautiful dining rooms in Madrid and a famous terrace.

name: LÚ Cocina y Alma
history: Chef Juanlu Fernández combines classic French techniques with the folklore of Andalusia.
Best Dishes: Retinto Beef with Bearnaise. Red Tuna Stew.
highlights: Known for its 'Vanguardia de Retaguardia' (Rearguard Avant-Garde) style.

name: Mugaritz
history: Andoni Luis Aduriz creates a provocative dining experience that challenges the concept of deliciousness.
Best Dishes: Edible Stones. The Decay of a Leaf.
highlights: Often called the most adventurous restaurant in the world, prioritizing intellectual stimulation over comfort.

name: Cinc Sentits
history: Self-taught Chef Jordi Artal serves a modern interpretation of Catalan family recipes.
Best Dishes: Pork Trotters with Sea Cucumber. Sweet Potato and Chestnut.
highlights: Offers a sensory journey through Catalonia with a focus on small, artisan producers.

name: Enigma
history: Albert Adrià's labyrinthine space dedicated to culinary mystery and innovation.
Best Dishes: Spherical Olives. Earl Grey Tea Air.
highlights: A constantly evolving concept that continues the legacy of El Bulli in an urban setting.

name: Smoked Room
history: Dani García's exclusive fire-focused restaurant (Omakase style) with only 14 seats.
Best Dishes: Smoked Eel with Nitro Tomato. Wagyu A5 from Charcoal.
highlights: Everything is touched by smoke or fire, creating deep, primal flavors.

name: L'Escaleta
history: Chef Kiko Moya is famous for his 'Square Rice' and innovative use of local mountain ingredients.
Best Dishes: Rice cooked in a rectangular tin (Arròs al Quadrat). Mustard Ice Cream.
highlights: Located in the Alicante mountains, creating dishes that are visually stunning and deeply flavored.

name: Venta Moncalvillo
history: The Echapresto brothers run this restaurant in a tiny village (population 50).
Best Dishes: Seasonal Vegetable Menu. Cod with Rioja Peppers.
highlights: Famous for its biodynamic vegetable garden and an incredible cellar of Rioja wines.

name: Alevante
history: Chef Ángel León's outpost in the Gran Meliá Sancti Petri, bringing his 'Chef of the Sea' cuisine here.
Best Dishes: Sea Plankton Rice. Marine Charcuterie.
highlights: Offers the greatest hits of Aponiente in a luxurious resort setting.

name: Bo.TiC
history: Located in an old carriage factory. Chef Albert Sastregener offers refined, artistic Catalan cuisine.
Best Dishes: Goose Barnacles with Pumpkin. Oxtail Ravioli.
highlights: Known for impeccable presentation and a comprehensive tasting menu experience.

name: La Boscana
history: Chef Joel Castanyé focuses on fruit-based cuisine, highlighting the produce of the Lleida orchards.
Best Dishes: Pear from Lleida with Pork. Fruit-fed Duck.
highlights: A unique gastronomic concept where fruit is the protagonist in savory dishes.

name: Deessa
history: Located in the Mandarin Oriental Ritz, helmed by Quique Dacosta. It serves two distinct tasting menus: 'Historical' and 'Contemporary'.
Best Dishes: Denia Red Prawn. Caviar with Almond.
highlights: Set in the stunning Alfonso XIII room overlooking the hotel gardens.

name: Aleia
history: Located in the iconic Hotel Casa Fuster, Chef Rafa de Bedoya combines Andalusian flavors with French technique and Catalan produce.
Best Dishes: Sea Bream with 'Gazpachuelo'. Sherry-infused sauces.
highlights: An elegant, light-filled dining room in a Modernista landmark.

name: Mont Bar
history: Started as a high-end gastrobar by Ivan Castro. It proves that fine dining can happen in a relaxed, tapas-style setting.
Best Dishes: Sea Urchin Mochi. Ventresca (Tuna Belly) with Pine Nuts.
highlights: Offers a dizzying array of snacks and small plates with Michelin-star precision.

name: Maralba
history: Chef Fran Martínez focuses on 'La Mancha' cuisine, using game and fresh vegetables from the region.
Best Dishes: Pickled Partridge. Lamb with Honey and Rosemary.
highlights: Known for modernizing rustic Manchego recipes in a contemporary setting.

name: El Portal de Echaurren
history: Francis Paniego runs this family hotel restaurant, famous for mastering offal (casquería).
Best Dishes: Croquettes (Legendary). Lamb Sweetbreads on Dust.
highlights: Located in a small village, preserving the culinary heritage of La Rioja.

name: Enoteca Paco Pérez
history: Located in the Hotel Arts, Chef Paco Pérez brings the essence of the Costa Brava Mediterranean to the city.
Best Dishes: Sea Cucumber Carbonara. Peas with Sea Urchin.
highlights: Features an exceptional wine cellar with over 700 references.

name: M.B
history: Martín Berasategui's restaurant in the Ritz-Carlton Abama, Tenerife. Led by Chef Erlantz Gorostiza.
Best Dishes: Caramelized Millefeuille of Eel. Canary Island Black Pig.
highlights: Combines Berasategui's signature Basque style with local Canarian ingredients.

name: Glam Enrico Bartolini
history: Located in the Palazzo Venart on the Grand Canal. Chef Donato Ascani interprets Venetian flavors with modern flair.
Best Dishes: Cuttlefish with herbs. Smoked Eel.
highlights: A romantic setting with a hidden garden opening onto the Grand Canal.

name: Acquolina
history: Chef Daniele Lippi leads this seafood-focused restaurant inside The First Roma Arte hotel.
Best Dishes: Spaghetti with Sea Urchin and Peanuts. Red Mullet in bread crust.
highlights: Known for its 'Mediterraneo' menu which explores the history of the Mediterranean sea.

name: Seta by Antonio Guida
history: Inside the Mandarin Oriental Milan. Chef Antonio Guida brings his southern Italian roots to cosmopolitan Milan.
Best Dishes: Rice with Raspberry and Herb Cream. Teriyaki Eel.
highlights: Dining in the elegant courtyard is one of Milan's most exclusive experiences.

name: La Peca
history: Run by the Portinari brothers. 'La Peca' means 'the footprint' in local dialect.
Best Dishes: Bigoli with Duck Ragu. Risotto with Licorice.
highlights: Famous for its desserts and an elaborate centerpiece sculpture on each table.

name: La Madia
history: Chef Pino Cuttaia turns Sicilian home cooking memories into high art.
Best Dishes: Pine Cone of Smoked Fish. Egg of the Cuttlefish.
highlights: Celebrates the intense, sun-drenched flavors of southern Sicily.

name: Il Piccolo Principe
history: Located on the rooftop of the Grand Hotel Principe di Piemonte. Chef Giuseppe Mancino offers views of the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Best Dishes: Sushi Toscano. Calamarata Pasta.
highlights: Combines classic Tuscan ingredients with Asian influences and seafood.

name: Torre del Saracino
history: Chef Gennaro Esposito's fortress tower restaurant on the Sorrento coast.
Best Dishes: Soup of forgotten fish. Parmesan Risotto with Lemon.
highlights: Located in a 1,300-year-old watchtower right on the water's edge.

name: Agli Amici
history: The Scarello family has run this inn since 1887. Emanuele Scarello focuses on the herbs and produce of Friuli.
Best Dishes: Gnocchi with Sea Urchin. Deer with Lichen.
highlights: The menu bridges the gap between the Alps and the Adriatic Sea.

name: Harry's Piccolo
history: Located in the Grand Hotel Duchi d'Aosta on Piazza Unità d'Italia. Chefs Matteo Metullio and Davide De Pra.
Best Dishes: Sea Urchin Risotto. Bora (Local wind inspired dessert).
highlights: Offers a 'True Kilometer' philosophy, sourcing the best ingredients regardless of distance.

name: St. George by Heinz Beck
history: Heinz Beck's Sicilian outpost in The Ashbee Hotel, blending his healthy cooking philosophy with Sicilian zest.
Best Dishes: Fagottelli Carbonara (Beck classic). Amberjack with Tomato water.
highlights: Overlooks the Ionian Sea with a terrace dining experience.

name: Il Pagliaccio
history: Chef Anthony Genovese draws heavily on his time in Asia, creating a fusion unique in Rome.
Best Dishes: The Journey (Snack sequence). Char with Coconut and Curry.
highlights: An intimate, sophisticated space known for its 'Circus' of flavors.

name: Locanda Sant'Uffizio Enrico Bartolini
history: Chef Gabriele Boffa leads this kitchen in a former monastery, under the mentorship of Enrico Bartolini.
Best Dishes: Agnolotti del Plin. Piedmontese Beef Tartare.
highlights: Set in the rolling vineyards of Monferrato, specializing in truffle and wine pairing.

name: Castel fine dining
history: Chef Gerhard Wieser has led the kitchen for over 20 years, creating 'Alpine-Mediterranean' cuisine.
Best Dishes: Smoke soup. Venison from South Tyrol.
highlights: Located in the Hotel Castel with breathtaking views of the Merano valley.

name: Enoteca La Torre
history: Located in the luxurious Villa Laetitia (owned by the Fendi family). Chef Domenico Stile blends Neapolitan roots with Roman tradition.
Best Dishes: Lemon Risotto with Clams. Pigeon with Cocoa.
highlights: Dining in a historic Liberty-style hall with immense windows.

name: Duomo
history: Chef Ciccio Sultano is the master of modern Sicilian cuisine, embracing the island's complex history.
Best Dishes: Spaghetti with Taratata Sauce. Stuffed Pig Trotter.
highlights: Located near the Cathedral of San Giorgio in Ragusa Ibla, reflecting the baroque opulence of the city.

name: Caino
history: Valeria Piccini focuses on the 'Cucina Povera' of Maremma, elevating peasant dishes to 2-star status.
Best Dishes: Tortelli Cacio e Pepe. Tripe and Lampredotto.
highlights: Situated in a medieval stone village, famous for its deep, comforting flavors.

name: Krèsios
history: Chef Giuseppe Iannotti runs a highly experimental kitchen. There is no menu, only a blind tasting journey.
Best Dishes: Spaghetto allo Zafferano (Saffron Spaghetti). Chicken Skin.
highlights: Known for its minimalist design and provocative dishes that challenge texture and temperature.

name: Madonnina del Pescatore
history: Moreno Cedroni creates 'Susci' (his Italian version of Sushi), blending raw fish with experimental aging techniques.
Best Dishes: The Tunnel (Seafood structure). Cutlet of Amberjack.
highlights: A modern glass structure directly on the Adriatic beach.

name: Terra The Magic Place
history: Heinrich Schneider forages for wild herbs in the Dolomites daily. It is the highest 2-star restaurant in Italy.
Best Dishes: Pine Needle Risotto. Hay Soup.
highlights: Located at 1,600 meters altitude in the Auener Hof hotel, focusing on wild Alpine botany.

name: Campo del Drago
history: Located in the Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco. Chef Matteo Temperini highlights the produce of the Val d'Orcia.
Best Dishes: Tortelli with Genovese Ragout. Local Boar.
highlights: Surrounded by Brunello di Montalcino vineyards in a historic borgo.

name: San Domenico
history: Founded in 1970, it introduced the concept of 'Home Cooking' for nobles. Chef Max Mascia continues the legacy.
Best Dishes: Uovo in Raviolo (Egg Yolk Raviolo with Truffle).
highlights: A temple of classic Italian gastronomy, famous for its unbroken history of excellence.

name: Arnolfo
history: Chef Gaetano Trovato is a mentor to many Italian chefs. The restaurant recently moved to a new architectural space.
Best Dishes: Pigeon with Foie Gras. Langoustine with Passion Fruit.
highlights: Offers panoramic views of the Tuscan hills from a modern, custom-built venue.

name: D'O
history: Chef Davide Oldani invented 'Pop Cuisine' (accessible fine dining).
Best Dishes: Caramelized Onion with Grana Padano ice cream.
highlights: Known for its custom-designed furniture and utensils by the chef.

name: L'Olivo
history: The flagship of the Capri Palace Jumeirah. Chef Andrea Migliaccio brings Ischian innovation to Capri.
Best Dishes: Lemon Tagliolini with Burrata and Red Prawns.
highlights: The dining room is designed like a luxurious living room with cashmere and art.

name: Andrea Aprea
history: Located on the top floor of the Luigi Rovati Foundation. Chef Aprea explores the relationship between memory and taste.
Best Dishes: Caprese Dolce Salato (Sweet and Salty Caprese).
highlights: A stunning space with panoramic views, connected to an Etruscan art museum.

name: Villa Feltrinelli
history: Chef Stefano Baiocco is famous for his greenhouse and herb garden, using over 100 varieties of plants.
Best Dishes: A simple salad (with dozens of rare herbs). Lake Fish variations.
highlights: Housed in a historic villa on Lake Garda, offering extreme exclusivity.

name: Santa Elisabetta
history: Located in the Byzantine Pagliazza Tower (one of the oldest buildings in Florence). Chef Rocco De Santis.
Best Dishes: Red Prawn with Almond and Cherry. Cappelletti.
highlights: An intimate circular dining room with only 7 tables inside the ancient tower.

name: Antica Corona Reale
history: The Vivalda family has run this restaurant since 1815. Renzo Vivalda serves the pinnacle of traditional Piedmont cuisine.
Best Dishes: Snails with Leeks. Tajarin with White Truffle.
highlights: Famous for its garden where vegetables are grown and its massive wine cellar.

name: Antica Osteria Cera
history: Lionello Cera transformed a countryside bar into one of Italy's best seafood restaurants.
Best Dishes: Colors of the Sea (Raw fish platter). Spider Crab.
highlights: Unusual for a 2-star seafood restaurant to be located inland, proving the quality of their sourcing.

name: Verso Capitaneo
history: Brothers Mario and Remo Capitaneo run this open-kitchen concept in Piazza Duomo.
Best Dishes: Sweetbreads with Sea Urchin. Pasta with Yeast.
highlights: A barrier-free environment where chefs serve guests directly across the counter.

name: daní maison
history: Nino Di Costanzo's restaurant is set in his family home's garden. A fairytale atmosphere.
Best Dishes: Pasta and Potatoes with 25 types of pasta. Scampi cocktail.
highlights: The garden is filled with art and sculptures, creating a magical dining setting.

name: Piazzetta Milù
history: Chef Maicol Izzo was named Best Young Chef by Michelin. A family-run modern bistro.
Best Dishes: Artichoke and Coffee. Genovese Pasta.
highlights: Known for a dynamic tasting menu that starts with a cocktail pairing.

name: Taverna Estia
history: Francesco Sposito leads the kitchen while his brother Mario manages the wine. Located near Vesuvius.
Best Dishes: Fettuccine with Pink Shrimp and Truffle. Lemon Risotto.
highlights: Elevates the humble ingredients of the Campania countryside.

name: Villa Elena
history: Part of Enrico Bartolini's constellation. Chef Marco Galtarossa interprets the Bergamo territory.
Best Dishes: Pigeon with Grape and Liver. Casoncelli.
highlights: Located in a historic villa in the Upper Town (Città Alta) of Bergamo.

name: Magnolia
history: Chef Alberto Faccani creates playful, technically precise dishes in the hills of Romagna.
Best Dishes: Squid Tagliatelle. Eel with Green Apple.
highlights: Vibrant, colorful dishes that match the modern art on the walls.

name: I Tenerumi
history: Chef Davide Guidara champions 'Vegetal Cuisine' on a volcanic island.
Best Dishes: Lentils and Garlic. Tomato variations.
highlights: Guests sit on pillows (tatami style) overlooking the sea. The menu is almost entirely plant-based.

name: Famiglia Rana
history: Created by the famous Rana pasta family. Chef Francesco Sodano brings avant-garde techniques.
Best Dishes: Tortelli of Artichoke. Fermented Pasta.
highlights: Located inside the pasta factory complex but offers a serene, nature-filled sanctuary.

name: George Restaurant
history: Chef Domenico Candela brings his French training back to Naples. Located in the Grand Hotel Parker's.
Best Dishes: Spaghettone with Tomato Water. Blue Lobster.
highlights: Offers one of the best panoramic views of the Bay of Naples.

name: Jônt
history: Ryan Ratino's intimate chef's counter. Focuses on dry-aging and fermentation.
Best Dishes: Dungeness Crab with Kani Miso. Dry-aged Duck.
highlights: A hidden, 14-seat tasting counter offering a highly interactive experience.

name: minibar
history: José Andrés's temple of avant-garde molecular gastronomy. One of the most difficult reservations in the US.
Best Dishes: Rubber Ducky Meringue. Olive Spheres.
highlights: A theatrical meal where science meets art in bite-sized courses.

name: The Inn at Little Washington
history: Chef Patrick O'Connell (the 'Pope of American Cuisine') founded this inn in 1978.
Best Dishes: Carpaccio of Herb-Crusted Lamb. Tuna and Foie Gras Confetti.
highlights: The longest-tenured 3-star restaurant in the US, known for its opulent maximalist decor and cheese trolley.

name: Blue Hill at Stone Barns
history: Chef Dan Barber's farm-to-table icon located on a working four-season farm and educational center.
Best Dishes: Vegetables from the farm. Rotation Risotto.
highlights: There are no menus; guests receive a multi-course feast featuring the day's harvest from the surrounding fields.

name: Aska
history: Chef Fredrik Berselius runs this warehouse-style restaurant in Williamsburg, blending Nordic flavors with New York attitude.
Best Dishes: Bladderwrack Seaweed and Blue Mussels. Birch Ice Cream.
highlights: Includes a garden, a cellar bar, and a dining room with a distinct, dark, moody aesthetic.

name: Aquavit
history: A midtown institution since 1987. Chef Emma Bengtsson transformed it into a 2-star destination.
Best Dishes: Arctic Bird's Nest. Swedish Meatballs (Lunch).
highlights: Instrumental in introducing Nordic cuisine to America long before the Noma trend.

name: Jean-Georges
history: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's flagship at the Trump International Hotel, blending French technique with Asian herbalism.
Best Dishes: Egg Caviar. Sea Scallops with Caper-Raisin Emulsion.
highlights: Defined fine dining in New York for decades with its table-side service and light, broth-based sauces.

name: Atera
history: A sensory kitchen counter in Tribeca led by Chef Ronny Emborg.
Best Dishes: Waffles with Kalix Roe. Razor Clam with Almond.
highlights: Offers an immersive sensory experience where guests watch the chefs work in silence.

name: Gabriel Kreuther
history: Chef Gabriel Kreuther brings his Alsatian heritage to Bryant Park.
Best Dishes: Sturgeon and Sauerkraut Tart. Foie Gras Terrine.
highlights: Famous for its stork-themed decor and delivering high-end Alsatian hospitality.

name: Saga
history: Located on the 63rd floor of a Art Deco skyscraper. Chef James Kent (late) created a dining experience on top of the world.
Best Dishes: Dry Aged Duck. Fluke with Green Tomato.
highlights: Features panoramic balconies and a tagine-style serving format.

name: Masa
history: Chef Masa Takayama established the first ultra-luxury sushi counter in the US.
Best Dishes: Ohmi Beef Tataki with Truffle. Uni Risotto.
highlights: Known for being one of the most expensive restaurants in the world, flying fish directly from Japan.

name: Joo Ok
history: Originally a starred venue in Seoul, Chef Shin Chang-ho relocated the restaurant to NYC to showcase his fermentation mastery.
Best Dishes: Perilla Oil Noodles. Vinegar Tasting.
highlights: Specializes in using 30 different types of house-fermented vinegars.

name: César
history: César Ramirez returned to the scene with this stone-counter restaurant, focusing on extreme precision.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Kaffir Lime. Frozen Soufflé.
highlights: A strict no-photo policy (usually) and an intense focus on the chef's hand-crafted seafood dishes.

name: odo
history: Chef Hiroki Odo runs this speakeasy-style Kaiseki counter hidden behind a bar.
Best Dishes: Seasonal Kaiseki Soup. Wagyu Shabu Shabu.
highlights: Offers a modern interpretation of Kaiseki with a focus on US seasonal produce.

name: Sushi Noz
history: Modeled after a Kyoto temple, Chef Nozomu Abe serves Edomae sushi with ancient aging techniques.
Best Dishes: Iwashi (Sardine). Aged Tuna.
highlights: The interior was constructed in Japan and reassembled in NYC without nails.

name: Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare
history: Now led by chefs Max Natmessnig and Marco Prins, continuing the legacy of one of NYC's most acclaimed counters.
Best Dishes: Hokkaido Sea Urchin with Truffle. Frozen Cosmo.
highlights: Located inside a grocery store, transforming into a sleek fine dining theater.

name: The Modern
history: Danny Meyer's restaurant inside the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), overlooking the Sculpture Garden.
Best Dishes: Eggs on Eggs on Eggs. Roast Duck.
highlights: Chef Thomas Allan delivers artful cuisine that complements the museum setting.

name: Atomix
history: Chef JP Park and Ellia Park redefined Korean fine dining with this counter-only tasting menu.
Best Dishes: Sea Cucumber with Shrimp. Langoustine with Doenjang.
highlights: Guests receive cards explaining the ingredients and philosophy of every dish.

name: Oriole
history: Chef Noah Sandoval's hidden gem in the West Loop, accessible via a freight elevator.
Best Dishes: Hamachi with Truffle and Puffed Rice. Capellini with Rye and Yeast.
highlights: Known for a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere despite the high-level cooking.

name: Alinea
history: Grant Achatz's temple of molecular gastronomy, famous for deconstructing food.
Best Dishes: Edible Helium Balloon. Dessert painted on the table.
highlights: Constantly reinventing itself, offering one of the most theatrical dining experiences in the world.

name: Ever
history: Chef Curtis Duffy (formerly of Grace) returned with this ambitious project focusing on proteins.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Citrus. Frozen Celery Root.
highlights: The dining room is designed to be soundproof and distraction-free, focusing solely on the plate.

name: Kasama
history: Tim Flores and Genie Kwon run this bakery by day and fine dining destination by night.
Best Dishes: Mushroom Adobo. Truffle Croissant.
highlights: The first Filipino restaurant in the world to be awarded a Michelin star.

name: Dewakan
history: Chef Darren Teoh explores indigenous ingredients from Malaysia's seas, farms, and jungles.
Best Dishes: Black Banana Porridge. Goat Tartare.
highlights: The name combines 'Dewa' (God) and 'Makan' (Food), emphasizing the sacredness of local produce.

name: Emeril's
history: The flagship of Emeril Lagasse, recently renovated and led by his son EJ Lagasse.
Best Dishes: Potato Alexa. Barbecue Shrimp.
highlights: Combines classic New Orleans hospitality with a modern, refined tasting menu approach.

name: Helm
history: Chef Josh Boutwood's intimate theater of dining, where the menu changes theme regularly.
Best Dishes: Mussel and Duck. Adlai Porridge.
highlights: A minimalist black-and-white space where the chef interacts directly with every guest.

name: Jingji
history: A high-end restaurant focusing on the Imperial cuisine of Beijing (Jingji).
Best Dishes: Braised Sea Cucumber with Scallion. Traditional Peking Duck.
highlights: Located in the SKP mall, offering a luxurious modern interpretation of capital cuisine.

name: King's Joy
history: Located near the Lama Temple, Chef Pan Jianjun uses ingredients to mimic meat textures.
Best Dishes: Sweet and Sour Monkey's Head Mushroom. Fox Nut Soup.
highlights: The first vegetarian restaurant to receive three Michelin stars in China, emphasizing health and mindfulness.

name: Shanghai Cuisine
history: Also known as Wulixiang, bringing authentic Shanghai flavors to the capital.
Best Dishes: Braised Pork Belly. Hairy Crab (Seasonal).
highlights: Located in a renovated courtyard house, offering a nostalgic and elegant atmosphere.

name: Blackswan
history: A visually stunning restaurant created by the Holiland bakery founders, focusing on art and food.
Best Dishes: Caviar Tart. Black Swan Dessert.
highlights: Famous for its ethereal, white landscape design and impeccable service aesthetics.

name: Lamdre
history: A plant-based fine dining destination inspired by Tibetan philosophy.
Best Dishes: Tofu with Truffle. Seasonal Mushroom Hotpot.
highlights: Focuses on the purity of ingredients and sustainability, earning a Green Star.

name: Lu Shang Lu
history: Dedicated to Lu cuisine (Shandong), the oldest of the major Chinese culinary traditions.
Best Dishes: Braised Intestine. Sea Cucumber with Leek.
highlights: Celebrates Confucian culinary philosophy and the rich seafood traditions of Shandong.

name: L'Atelier Robuchon
history: Located in The Woodward hotel. Chef Olivier Jean maintains the Robuchon legacy of counter dining.
Best Dishes: Imperial Caviar and King Crab. Quail with Foie Gras.
highlights: The first L'Atelier in Switzerland, offering the iconic red-and-black aesthetic.

name: La Table du Lausanne Palace
history: Chef Franck Pelux (Top Chef finalist) brings a fresh, emotional approach to the palace hotel.
Best Dishes: The Potato (Signature). Lake Geneva Fera.
highlights: Offers stunning views of Lake Geneva and the Alps.

name: Da Vittorio - St. Moritz
history: The Alpine outpost of the Cerea family (Da Vittorio Brusaporto). Located in the Carlton Hotel.
Best Dishes: Paccheri alla Vittorio. Elephant Ear Cutlet.
highlights: Brings the warmth and abundance of Italian hospitality to the snowy peaks.

name: Einstein Gourmet
history: Chefs Sebastian Zier and Richard Schmidtkow produce elaborate French-based cuisine overlooking the city.
Best Dishes: Breton Lobster. Pigeon from Miéral.
highlights: Located in the Hotel Einstein, offering panoramic views of the Old Town and the Abbey.

name: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada, Bad Ragaz
history: The first IGNIV ('Nest' in Romansh) by Andreas Caminada, focusing on a fine dining sharing concept.
Best Dishes: Chicken Nuggets (Gourmet version). Sharing Starters.
highlights: Breaks the traditional course structure, encouraging social dining.

name: The Japanese Restaurant
history: Located in The Chedi Andermatt. Chef Dominik Sato and Fabio Toffolon create modern Japanese dishes.
Best Dishes: Black Cod Miso. Sushi Omakase.
highlights: Features a tempura and sushi bar at 1,444 meters above sea level.

name: Gilles Varone
history: Chef Gilles Varone operates this eco-friendly restaurant in a modern wooden structure.
Best Dishes: Vegetable tasting menu. Local Lamb.
highlights: Highly sustainable, using solar energy and local Valais produce.

name: The Counter
history: Chef Mitja Birlo creates a unique interaction at a long wooden counter in the main station area.
Best Dishes: Fish cooked in beeswax. Forest floor dessert.
highlights: Guests sit at a counter watching the preparation of complex, nature-inspired dishes.

name: La Brezza, Ascona
history: Chef Marco Campanella cooks light, fresh Mediterranean cuisine at the Hotel Eden Roc.
Best Dishes: Tagliolini with Lemon and Scampi. Pike Perch.
highlights: Located right on the shores of Lake Maggiore with a beautiful garden terrace.

name: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada, Andermatt
history: Another 'Nest' in the Swiss Alps. Chef Valentin Röttgeber executes the sharing philosophy.
Best Dishes: Egg Royal. Beef Tartare.
highlights: Designed by Patricia Urquiola, offering a cozy, living-room atmosphere.

name: Maison Wenger
history: Jérémy Desbraux (formerly of Crissier) runs this historic house in the Jura mountains.
Best Dishes: Venison from the Jura. Absinthe Soufflé.
highlights: A destination restaurant in a quiet railway station building.

name: Magdalena
history: Dominik Hartmann focuses on vegetable-based fine dining, though not exclusively vegetarian.
Best Dishes: Beetroot Steak. Fermented Carrot.
highlights: Offers views of Lake Lucerne and the mountains with a casual, bakery-attached vibe.

name: focus ATELIER
history: Chef Patrick Mahler serves avant-garde cuisine in the Park Hotel Vitznau.
Best Dishes: Duck Liver with Apple. Wagyu with Onions.
highlights: Set in a glass pavilion within the hotel, emphasizing transparency and nature.

name: Taverne zum Schäfli
history: Chef Christian Kuchler took over his parents' tavern, turning it into a top gastronomic address.
Best Dishes: Ravioli with Truffle. Venison Wellington.
highlights: Combines a rustic timber-framed exterior with world-class modern cooking.

name: Ecco St. Moritz
history: Chef Rolf Fliegauf's winter residence in the Hotel Giardino Mountain.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Dashi. Pigeon with Beetroot.
highlights: Fliegauf was one of the youngest chefs to be awarded 2 stars in Switzerland.

name: Stucki - Tanja Grandits
history: Tanja Grandits is famous for her monochromatic menus where every dish is based on a single color.
Best Dishes: The 'Green' Menu. Salmon with Matcha.
highlights: Located in a patrician villa, celebrating the harmony of color and spices.

name: Ecco
history: Rolf Fliegauf's summer residence in the Hotel Giardino Ascona.
Best Dishes: Raw marinated seafood. Citrus aromatics.
highlights: Focuses on 'aroma cuisine', keeping the original flavors of ingredients intact.

name: Skin's - the restaurant
history: Chef Kevin Romes offers a global menu in a former industrial site (Hero factory).
Best Dishes: Short Rib with Kimchi. Tuna with Jalapeno.
highlights: The architecture retains the industrial brick charm contrasted with modern luxury.

name: Colonnade
history: Chef Gilad Peled runs this restaurant in the Mandarin Oriental Palace.
Best Dishes: Sole with Champagne Sauce. Lamb with Artichoke.
highlights: The dining room features grand columns and Belle Époque elegance.

name: La Brezza, Arosa
history: Chef Marco Campanella moves his team between Ascona in summer and the Tschuggen Grand Hotel in Arosa for the winter.
Best Dishes: Pike Perch with Sauerkraut. Vegan Tasting Menu.
highlights: Offers a plant-based 'Moving Mountains' menu alongside traditional options in a stunning Alpine setting.

name: IGNIV Zürich by Andreas Caminada
history: Located in the Hotel Marktgasse, bringing Caminada's fine dining sharing concept to Zurich's old town.
Best Dishes: Egg Royal. Beef Tartare with Truffle.
highlights: Focuses on a relaxed, social dining experience with many small plates shared in the center of the table.

name: The Restaurant
history: Heiko Nieder has led this restaurant in The Dolder Grand since 2008, earning 2 stars and high GaultMillau points.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Strawberry and Tomato. Rabbit with Curry.
highlights: Situated in a castle-like hotel overlooking the lake and city, offering an extensive vegetarian menu.

name: 7132 Silver
history: Head Chef Marcel Koolen serves avant-garde cuisine in the architecturally famous 7132 Hotel (designed by Peter Zumthor).
Best Dishes: Valser Lamb. Trout from the Rhine.
highlights: Uses ingredients foraged from the surrounding Vals valley, emphasizing extreme locality.

name: Mammertsberg
history: Silvio Germann (formerly at IGNIV) took over this historic chateau in 2022 and quickly earned 2 stars.
Best Dishes: Char with Cucumber. Venison with Elderberry.
highlights: Located in a picturesque Swiss half-timbered castle with views of Lake Constance.

name: Pic Beau-Rivage Palace
history: Anne-Sophie Pic's Swiss outpost in the legendary Beau-Rivage Palace hotel.
Best Dishes: Berlingots with Gruyère. Wild Sea Bass with Caviar.
highlights: Combines French elegance with Swiss ingredients, overlooking Lake Geneva and the Alps.

name: roots
history: Chef Pascal Steffen focuses on vegetables as the main event, with meat and fish playing supporting roles.
Best Dishes: Celeriac with Truffle. Pike Perch with Fennel.
highlights: Situated directly on the Rhine river with a terrace offering beautiful water views.

name: Stand
history: Chefs Szabina Szulló and Tamás Széll interpret classic Hungarian dishes with modern French techniques.
Best Dishes: Goulash Soup. Somlói Galuska (Dessert).
highlights: The leading light of Hungarian gastronomy, showcasing local terroir and traditions.

name: Platán Gourmet
history: Chef István Pesti moved to the countryside to create Hungary's first rural 2-star restaurant.
Best Dishes: Trout with Kohlrabi. Venison with Pine.
highlights: Located in the castle district of Tata, near the Old Lake, offering a highly artistic presentation.

name: Create by Guido Braeken
history: Chef Guido Braeken (formerly of Julemont) opened this new venue in the Van Oys Maastricht Retreat.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Pumpkin. Wagyu with Onion.
highlights: Awarded 2 stars almost immediately after opening, known for intense sauces and perfectionism.

name: GEM. by Soenil Bahadoer
history: Soenil Bahadoer (of De Lindehof fame) opened this new flagship in Gemert Castle, blending Surinamese roots with haute cuisine.
Best Dishes: Roti with Crab and Curry. Spicy Rendang.
highlights: A unique fusion of Hindustani flavors and French technique set in a historic castle.

name: Fred
history: Chef Fred Mustert runs this sleek, modern restaurant known for its consistency and luxury ingredients.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Curry. Wagyu Beef.
highlights: Features a stunning cheese trolley and an interior designed with warm, golden tones.

name: Tribeca
history: Chef Jan Sobecki took over the former Boreas restaurant, transforming it into a relaxed, top-tier destination.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Truffle. Sweetbreads with Laksa.
highlights: Combines a living-room atmosphere with highly technical, flavor-focused cooking.

name: 't Nonnetje
history: Chef Michel van der Kroft is famous for his 'Portuguese' influences, inspired by his wife's heritage.
Best Dishes: Carabineiro with Risotto. Pastel de Nata (Dessert interpretation).
highlights: Located on the historic Vischmarkt square, blending Dutch produce with Iberian flair.

name: Brut172
history: Hans van Wolde (formerly of Beluga) renovated a farmhouse to create this immersive culinary destination.
Best Dishes: Local Pork with Hay. Fermented Vegetables.
highlights: A complete experience where guests move through different rooms (barn, kitchen, loft) during the meal.

name: De Treeswijkhoeve
history: Dick Middelweerd creates dishes inspired by his travels and the surrounding Brabant forests.
Best Dishes: Indonesian Rendang (Modern take). Brabant Asparagus.
highlights: Located in a thatched farmhouse, offering a warm, family-run atmosphere.

name: FG - François Geurds
history: Chef François Geurds (formerly of The Fat Duck) is known for his flavor laboratory and obsession with ingredients.
Best Dishes: Bonbon of Foie Gras. 50-item Taste Laboratory.
highlights: Famous for allowing guests to choose their own knife and the extreme customization of the menu.

name: De Lindenhof
history: Martin Kruithof runs this idyllic restaurant in the 'Venice of the North', often picking up guests by boat.
Best Dishes: Eel from the canals. Wagyu Beef.
highlights: Set in a thatched house surrounded by water, offering a quintessentially Dutch experience.

name: Aan de Poel
history: Chef Stefan van Sprang serves internationally inspired dishes with spectacular views of 'De Poel' lake.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Curry. Strawberries with Basil.
highlights: Known for its large terrace and cosmopolitan, relaxed vibe.

name: Ciel Bleu
history: Located on the 23rd floor of the Hotel Okura. Chefs Onno Kokmeijer and Arjan Speelman focus on international excellence.
Best Dishes: King Crab with Baeri Caviar. Pigeon with Truffle.
highlights: Offers the best panoramic views of Amsterdam from a high-rise setting.

name: De Nieuwe Winkel
history: Chef Emile van der Staak pioneered 'Botanical Gastronomy', focusing on local plants and food forests.
Best Dishes: Tempeh of Local Beans. Chestnut Mousse.
highlights: A meat-free (or near meat-free) menu that explores the potential of Dutch terroir and botany.

name: Spectrum
history: Chef Sidney Schutte (formerly of Librije) brings bold, Asian-influenced flavors to the Waldorf Astoria.
Best Dishes: Crispy Duck Tongue. Blue Lobster with X.O. sauce.
highlights: Known for using unexpected ingredient combinations and a powerful vegetarian menu.

name: Inter Scaldes
history: Previously a 3-star legend under Jannis Brevet, now led by Chef Jeroen Achtien, who maintained its elite status.
Best Dishes: Oosterschelde Lobster. Sea Bass with Oyster.
highlights: Nestled in the Zeeland polders, focusing heavily on local seafood and herbs.

name: Restaurant 212
history: Chefs Richard van Oostenbrugge and Thomas Groot created Amsterdam's first 'no-table' restaurant.
Best Dishes: Potato with Caviar (Signature). Lobster with Vin Jaune.
highlights: Guests sit at a continuous counter surrounding the kitchen, watching every step of the process.

name: De Groene Lantaarn
history: Jarno Eggen creates refined dishes in a historic windmill in the village of Staphorst.
Best Dishes: Roe Deer with Red Cabbage. Langoustine with Pumpkin.
highlights: Located in a beautifully restored windmill, offering a romantic and historic setting.

name: Vinkeles
history: Located in a former 18th-century bakery within the Dylan Hotel. Chef Jurgen van der Zalm leads the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Imperial Caviar with Scallop. Bresse Pigeon.
highlights: Dining in the sunken ovens of the old bakery provides a unique historical atmosphere.

name: Parkheuvel
history: Erik van Loo (the 'Sauce Master') and his son Juliën run this classic restaurant in the park.
Best Dishes: Bresse Chicken Ravioli. Turbot with Truffle.
highlights: Famous for its sweeping views of the Maas river and shipping traffic.

name: De Bokkedoorns
history: Nestled in the dunes near Haarlem, this restaurant has held 2 stars for decades. Chef Roy Eijkelkamp leads it now.
Best Dishes: North Sea Crab. Dunes Rabbit.
highlights: A tranquil escape in nature, focusing on seasonal and local game.

name: Flore
history: Chef Bas van Kranen replaced the classic Bord'Eau with Flore, focusing on 'Conscious Fine Dining'.
Best Dishes: Vegetable Charcuterie. North Sea Sepia.
highlights: Dairy-free and sustainably focused, sourcing ingredients from biodynamic farms.

name: PRISMA
history: Chef Ilha Saito is the only Italian chef in Tokyo to hold 2 stars. He works alone in the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Cavatelli with Truffle. Warm Carpaccio.
highlights: A minimalist, serene space where the chef prepares everything from scratch, including the bread and pasta.

name: Tempura Motoyoshi
history: Chef Kazuhito Motoyoshi treats tempura as a form of molecular gastronomy, manipulating moisture and texture.
Best Dishes: Uni (Sea Urchin) wrapped in Shiso Leaf tempura. Sweet Potato.
highlights: Known for his 'liquid nitrogen' batter technique for the vegetable tempura.

name: Tempura Kondo
history: Chef Fumio Kondo revolutionized tempura by focusing on vegetables, which were previously ignored in high-end tempura.
Best Dishes: Sweet Potato (7cm thick). Carrot Julienne.
highlights: A legendary institution in Ginza where the vegetable tempura is as prized as the seafood.

name: Seizan
history: Chef Haruhiko Yamamoto serves kaiseki that is both traditional and accessible, famous for his desserts.
Best Dishes: Wagyu Beef Hotpot. Mont Blanc Dessert.
highlights: Known for the chef's warm hospitality and the famous pudding served at the end.

name: Kohaku
history: Led by Chef Koji Koizumi (Ishikawa group), Kohaku earned 3 stars for its fusion of traditional kaiseki with innovative ingredients.
Best Dishes: Truffle and Foie Gras Chawanmushi. Fried Soft Shell Turtle.
highlights: Combines the purity of dashi with bold, non-traditional luxury ingredients.

name: HOMMAGE
history: Chef Noboru Arai brings French fine dining to the historic Asakusa district.
Best Dishes: Foie Gras with Narazuke (Pickles). Asakusa Nori Bread.
highlights: A unique blend of classic French technique with the traditional 'Edo' spirit of Asakusa.

name: MAZ
history: Virgilio Martínez (Central, Peru) opened this Tokyo outpost to explore Japan's nature through Peruvian biodiversity.
Best Dishes: Vertical World (Tasting menu based on altitude). Sea Urchin with Cacao.
highlights: Explores the concept of 'Mater Iniciativa', connecting the ecosystems of Peru and Japan.

name: ASAHINA Gastronome
history: Chef Satoru Asahina (formerly of Joel Robuchon) creates classic, heavy French cuisine with modern precision.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Vanilla. Beef Rossini.
highlights: Known for its table-side carving and classic, opulent sauces.

name: Hakuun
history: Chef Shingo Sakamoto (formerly of RyuGin) offers a modern kaiseki experience in Minamiaoyama.
Best Dishes: Charcoal-grilled Bonito. Soft-shelled Turtle Chawanmushi.
highlights: Focuses on 'Aroma and Temperature', cooking ingredients live in front of guests.

name: Crony
history: Led by Chef Michihiro Haruta and Sommelier Kazuyoshi Ozawa, focusing on sustainable, Nordic-influenced French cuisine.
Best Dishes: Tea Pairing Menu. Sourdough with Sake Lees.
highlights: Famous for its expertly curated tea pairing and relaxed, Scandinavian-style interior.

name: Den
history: Zaiyu Hasegawa created 'Den' to make kaiseki fun and approachable, focusing on hospitality and humor.
Best Dishes: Dentucky Fried Chicken (Stuffed wing). Garden Salad with Smiley Face carrot.
highlights: Voted the Best Restaurant in Asia (2022), known for the chef's dog Puchi and the fun atmosphere.

name: Nishiazabu Sushi Shin
history: A hidden gem in Nishiazabu where Chef Shintaro Suzuki focuses on the purity of ingredients.
Best Dishes: Steamed Abalone. Kohada (Gizzard Shad).
highlights: Offers a quiet, traditional atmosphere favored by locals and connoisseurs.

name: Florilège
history: Chef Hiroyasu Kawate moved his restaurant to Azabudai Hills, focusing on a plant-based ('Vegetable') theme.
Best Dishes: Carpaccio of Sustainable Beef (Classic). Roasted Vegetables.
highlights: A large U-shaped counter surrounds the kitchen, creating a theatrical 'stadium' feel.

name: Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongiten
history: Run by Takashi Ono, the younger son of Jiro Ono. It is more relaxed than the (now unlisted) Ginza original.
Best Dishes: Omakase Nigiri. Egg Custard (Tamago).
highlights: Offers the legendary 'Jiro' style of sushi in a slightly more approachable setting for foreigners.

name: Ginza Fukuju
history: Chef Katsuhiro Onodera creates robust, flavorful kaiseki dishes, emphasizing the dashi.
Best Dishes: Stewed Shark Fin. Soft-shelled Turtle Hotpot.
highlights: A small counter restaurant known for powerful flavors that pair well with sake.

name: ESqUISSE
history: Chef Lionel Beccat brings a philosophical and artistic approach to French cuisine in Ginza.
Best Dishes: Amadai with scales. Foie Gras with Citrus.
highlights: Known for the chef's poetic menus and the light, airy atmosphere of the dining room.

name: Kioicho Fukudaya
history: A historic ryotei founded in 1939, serving as a gathering place for politicians and artists (like Rosanjin).
Best Dishes: Seasonal Kaiseki. Sea Bream with Shark Fin.
highlights: Guests dine in private tatami rooms surrounded by exquisite Japanese gardens and art.

name: Ginza Kojyu
history: Chef Toru Okuda is a master of charcoal grilling and one of Japan's most famous kaiseki chefs.
Best Dishes: Charcoal Grilled Unagi (Eel). Seasonal Sashimi.
highlights: Celebrated for its wine list and the chef's dedication to perfecting the art of grilling.

name: Ryuzu
history: Chef Ryuta Iizuka, formerly of Joël Robuchon, creates elegant French cuisine with a Japanese touch.
Best Dishes: Shiitake Mushroom Tart. Niigata Rice Soufflé.
highlights: Offers a counter-style French dining experience in Roppongi with heavy emphasis on seasonal Japanese ingredients.

name: Ensui
history: Chef Koji Hayashi focuses on the purity of water ('Ensui' means salt water/brine) and dashi.
Best Dishes: Dashi Soup. Seasonal Hassun.
highlights: A minimalist kaiseki experience where the quality of the water is as important as the ingredients.

name: NARISAWA
history: Yoshihiro Narisawa pioneered 'Innovative Satoyama' cuisine, focusing on sustainability and the forest.
Best Dishes: Bread of the Forest. Soil Soup.
highlights: Consistently ranked among the best in Asia, known for bringing the Japanese landscape to the plate.

name: Sushi Kanesaka
history: Chef Shinji Kanesaka is a master of Edomae sushi, located in the Palace Hotel Tokyo.
Best Dishes: Kuruma Ebi (Prawn). Marinated Tuna.
highlights: Known for the perfect temperature and balance of the shari (rice) and neta (topping).

name: Ginza Shinohara
history: Chef Takemasa Shinohara brought his rural Shiga cuisine to the heart of Ginza.
Best Dishes: Foie Gras Monaka. Nabe (Hot Pot).
highlights: Famous for its 'Hassun' course which depicts the seasons of the Japanese countryside.

name: Akasaka Kikunoi
history: The Tokyo outpost of the legendary Kyoto kaiseki restaurant Kikunoi, led by Yoshihiro Murata.
Best Dishes: Sea Bream Sashimi. Turtle Soup.
highlights: Brings the authentic atmosphere and water (shipped from Kyoto) of the original Ryotei to Tokyo.

name: Kutan
history: Chef Kotaro Nutahara offers a high-end kaiseki experience in the Shintomicho area.
Best Dishes: Charcoal Grilled Nodoguro. Crab dishes.
highlights: Known for sourcing the absolute highest quality ingredients from Toyosu market nearby.

name: Restaurant Pearl Morissette
history: Located at the Pearl Morissette winery, focusing on French techniques applied to Niagara region produce.
Best Dishes: Duck aged in Beeswax. Seasonal Vegetable Tart.
highlights: Offers a blind tasting menu that changes daily, paired with their own low-intervention wines.

name: The Wolf's Tailor
history: Chef Kelly Whitaker's zero-waste kitchen that fuses Colorado ingredients with Asian techniques.
Best Dishes: Skewers from the Binchotan grill. Sourdough Bread.
highlights: Focuses heavily on fermentation and grain milling in-house.

name: Xin Rong Ji
history: The Chengdu branch of the famous Taizhou seafood brand, adapting slightly to local tastes.
Best Dishes: Wild Yellow Croaker. Braised Sea Anemone.
highlights: Brings high-end coastal cuisine to the heart of the Sichuan basin.

name: Yu Zhi Lan
history: Chef Lan Guijun, a master of Sichuan cuisine, runs this intimate 18-seat private kitchen.
Best Dishes: Golden Thread Noodles (cut by hand with a cleaver). Abalone.
highlights: Famous for the 'Golden Thread Noodles' which are so thin they can be threaded through a needle.

name: Eika
history: Chef Izumi utilizes dry-aging techniques for fish to concentrate umami.
Best Dishes: Aged Sashimi. Grilled Fish.
highlights: A minimalist space focusing entirely on the texture and depth of aged seafood.

name: A
history: Chef Alain Huang (formerly of RAW) opened this sleek, all-white restaurant in the Diamond Towers.
Best Dishes: The White Menu. Scallop variations.
highlights: Everything from the decor to the plating is designed in shades of white.

name: Yu Kapo
history: A kappo-style restaurant where the chef prepares dishes directly in front of the diners.
Best Dishes: Wagyu Beef Cutlet. Seasonal Clay Pot Rice.
highlights: Known for its intimate atmosphere and high-quality Japanese ingredients.

name: logy
history: Chef Ryogo Tahara (formerly of Florilège) combines French technique with Taiwanese flavors.
Best Dishes: Chawanmushi with Crab and Beef Consommé. Ayu with Liver Sauce.
highlights: The name stands for geology, biology, and the environment, reflected in the earthy flavors.

name: Mudan
history: A high-end tempura restaurant using premium ingredients and light batter.
Best Dishes: Sea Urchin Tempura wrapped in Shiso. Shark Fin Tempura.
highlights: One of the few Michelin-starred tempura specialists in Taiwan.

name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon
history: The Taipei branch of the legendary French chef, featuring the signature open kitchen.
Best Dishes: Quail with Foie Gras. Le Caviar Imperial.
highlights: Located in the Bellavita mall, offering a consistent world-class French dining experience.

name: Molino de Urdániz, Taipei
history: The overseas branch of the 2-star Spanish restaurant, located in Hotel MVSA.
Best Dishes: The Cucumber and Oyster. Smoked Trout.
highlights: Replicates the minimalist, nature-inspired cuisine of the Navarra original.

name: Cloudstreet
history: Chef Rishi Naleendra blends his Sri Lankan heritage with Australian culinary training.
Best Dishes: Grilled Oyster with Betel Leaf. Stout and Liquorice Bread.
highlights: Features a chef's counter and a distinct focus on bold, spicy, and smoky flavors.

name: Sushi Sakuta
history: Chef Yoshio Sakuta delivers a sublime omakase experience in the Capitol Kempinski Hotel.
Best Dishes: Aburi Toro with Truffle. Uni and Caviar.
highlights: Known for a luxurious setting and the use of gold leaf and caviar on sushi.

name: Thevar
history: Chef Mano Thevar creates 'Indian cuisine with a European backbone' in Keong Saik.
Best Dishes: Chettinad Chicken Roti. Crab Curry Rice.
highlights: A modern grill restaurant that redefines Indian flavors with contemporary techniques.

name: Jaan by Kirk Westaway
history: Chef Kirk Westaway reinvented the menu to focus on 'Reinventing British' cuisine.
Best Dishes: English Garden (Vegetable arrangement). Hens Egg with Caviar.
highlights: Located on the 70th floor of Swissôtel The Stamford with iconic skyline views.

name: Saint Pierre
history: Chef Emmanuel Stroobant focuses on 'Essence' - French techniques with Asian ingredients.
Best Dishes: Kegani Crab with Corn. Omi Beef.
highlights: Overlooks Marina Bay Sands, known for its impeccable, ceremonial service.

name: Meta
history: Chef Sun Kim combines his Korean heritage with French and Japanese techniques.
Best Dishes: Abalone with Liver Sauce. BBQ Wagyu Beef.
highlights: A sophisticated open-kitchen restaurant that moved to a larger, stunning venue in 2023.

name: Shoukouwa
history: A collaboration with the 3-star Sushi Shikon, offering strict Edomae sushi.
Best Dishes: Steamed Abalone. Castella Egg.
highlights: Fish is flown in daily from Toyosu Market to ensure absolute freshness.

name: Jiang by Chef Fei
history: Chef Fei is one of the most celebrated Cantonese chefs, modernizing traditional recipes.
Best Dishes: Flaxseed Crispy Chicken. Dim Sum specialties.
highlights: Located in the Mandarin Oriental, setting the standard for Cantonese fine dining.

name: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine, Guangzhou
history: Part of the Singapore-based group, known for reliability and high standards.
Best Dishes: Crispy Roasted Pork. Shark Fin Soup.
highlights: Famous for its impeccable roasting techniques and consistent quality.

name: Taian Table, GuangZhou
history: Stefan Stiller's Guangzhou outpost, following the successful interactive counter concept of Shanghai.
Best Dishes: Sea Urchin with Brown Butter. Smoked Eel.
highlights: Guests sit around a large open kitchen, watching the 8-course menu preparation.

name: Agli Amici Rovinj
history: A collaboration between the Scarello family (from Italy) and the Maistra Hospitality Group.
Best Dishes: Istrian Lamb. Kvarner Scampi.
highlights: Located in the Grand Park Hotel with stunning views of the old town and the Adriatic.

name: Vespertine
history: Chef Jordan Kahn created a gastronomic experience housed in a twisting steel tower (The Waffle).
Best Dishes: Dishes are conceptual and change completely, often resembling sculptures.
highlights: A multi-sensory, atmospheric experience with a custom soundtrack and monolithic architecture.

name: Aubergine
history: Chef Justin Cogley creates a menu inspired by the coastline of Carmel and Monterey Bay.
Best Dishes: Red Abalone with Seaweeds. Roasted Duck.
highlights: Located in L'Auberge Carmel, offering elegant cuisine with a deep sense of place.

name: Birdsong
history: Chef Chris Bleidorn focuses on heritage ingredients and open-fire cooking.
Best Dishes: Cornbread with Trout Roe. Creek-raised Trout.
highlights: Known for utilizing the whole animal and ancient cooking techniques.

name: Cyrus
history: Chef Douglas Keane returned with this reinvented classic in Sonoma wine country. (Note: Listed as 'Enclos' in prompt).
Best Dishes: Canapés in the Bubbling Room. Chocolate Room desserts.
highlights: A progressive dining journey moving guests through multiple rooms (Lounge, Kitchen, Dining Room).

name: Commis
history: Chef James Syhabout was the first to bring Michelin stars to Oakland. His cuisine is slow-paced and elemental.
Best Dishes: Slow-poached Egg Yolk with Dates. Caramelized Bread Soup.
highlights: A serene, minimalist counter-dining spot in the Piedmont Avenue neighborhood.

name: Acquerello
history: Suzette Gresham has run this fine dining institution for decades, elevating Italian cuisine to high art.
Best Dishes: Ridged Pasta with Foie Gras and Truffle. Bourbon-Caramel Semifreddo.
highlights: Housed in a converted chapel, offering old-school luxury and hospitality.

name: Hayato
history: Chef Brandon Go serves a traditional kaiseki meal to only 7 guests per seating.
Best Dishes: Bento Box (Lunch). Owalo with Dashi.
highlights: Located in the ROW DTLA, known for being one of the hardest reservations to get in LA.

name: Sons & Daughters
history: Chef Harrison Cheney brings a New Nordic influence to California produce.
Best Dishes: Cured Trout. Fermented Vegetables.
highlights: Promoted to 2 stars in 2024, focusing on acidity, fermentation, and herbaceous flavors.

name: Saison
history: Founded by Joshua Skenes, now led by Richard Lee. Famous for open hearth cooking.
Best Dishes: Uni Toast. Radish with Clarified Butter.
highlights: The kitchen has no gas stoves; everything is cooked with wood fire.

name: Californios
history: Chef Val M. Cantu reinvented Mexican cuisine as fine dining tasting menus.
Best Dishes: Tres Frijoles. Squab Tacos.
highlights: The only 2-star Mexican restaurant in the US, located in the Mission District.

name: Lazy Bear
history: Started as a pop-up dinner party by David Barzelay. It retains the communal, social atmosphere.
Best Dishes: Whipped Scrambled Eggs. Smokey BBQ flavors.
highlights: Guests sit at long communal tables and chefs explain each course to the whole room.

name: Harbor House
history: Chef Matthew Kammerer forages ingredients from the inn's own cove and gardens.
Best Dishes: Seaweed Sourdough. Abalone cooked in kelp.
highlights: Located on a remote cliff on the Mendocino coast, offering breathtaking ocean views.

name: Mélisse
history: Josiah Citrin's 14-seat intimate dining room hidden inside the larger Citrin restaurant.
Best Dishes: Egg Caviar. Lobster Bolognese.
highlights: A legendary LA establishment that reinvented itself into a more exclusive experience.

name: Kiln
history: Chef John Wesley focuses on simplicity and technique in an industrial-chic space.
Best Dishes: Glazed Squab. Cured Fish.
highlights: Known for its stark, minimalist warehouse aesthetic and powerful, stripped-back flavors.

name: 180° by Matthias Diether
history: Chef Matthias Diether brought Michelin-level dining to Estonia. The restaurant has an open kitchen in the center.
Best Dishes: Cucumber with Dill and Buttermilk. Pigeon.
highlights: The first 2-star restaurant in Estonia, offering views of the Port Noblessner.

name: ATAMA by Martin Stopp
history: A new concept focusing on 'Omakase' style service with German precision.
Best Dishes: Binchotan grilled seafood. Seasonal game.
highlights: A small, intimate venue that blends Japanese philosophy with European ingredients.

name: IKIGAI
history: Located in Schloss Elmau. The kitchen focuses on the Japanese concept of 'reason for being'.
Best Dishes: Chawanmushi with Lobster. Wagyu Beef.
highlights: A meditative dining experience in a luxury spa retreat in the Bavarian Alps.

name: Ox & Klee
history: Chef Daniel Gottschlich structures his menus around the six taste qualities: sour, bitter, salty, sweet, umami, and fat.
Best Dishes: The 'Experience Taste' Menu. Magpie Goose.
highlights: Located in the Crane Houses (Kranhäuser) with views of the Rhine river.

name: Gotthardt's by Yannick Noack
history: Yannick Noack took over the iconic establishment, quickly earning accolades for his refined modern cooking.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Pumpkin. Venison with Red Cabbage.
highlights: Located in the historic center of Koblenz, blending tradition with youthful energy.

name: OPUS V
history: Located above the Engelhorn fashion house, Chef Dominik Paul creates avant-garde cuisine with a Nordic touch.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Pumpkin. Saddle of Venison.
highlights: Offers a spectacular view over the rooftops of Mannheim from its minimalist, glass-walled dining room.

name: Tantris
history: A temple of German gastronomy since the 1970s. Chef Benjamin Chmura continues the legacy of this Bauhaus-style icon.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Vin Jaune. Veal Sweetbreads 'Rumohr'.
highlights: Famous for its vibrant orange retro interior and its status as the cradle of Michelin-starred cooking in Germany.

name: Alois - Dallmayr Fine Dining
history: Located inside the famous Dallmayr Delicatessen. Recently taken over by Chef Rosina Ostler, continuing its reputation for lightness and product quality.
Best Dishes: Breton Lobster with Koshihikari Rice. Mieral Pigeon.
highlights: An intimate, luxurious atmosphere on the first floor of one of the world's most famous food halls.

name: sein
history: Chef Thorsten Bender serves minimalist, Asian-inspired cuisine in a sleek, modern setting.
Best Dishes: Chawanmushi with Dashi. Wagyu with Kimchi.
highlights: Known for its 'less is more' philosophy, focusing on clarity and precision on the plate.

name: Intense
history: Chef Benjamin Peifer calls his style 'Pfälzer' (Palatinate) cuisine meets Japan. He uses local ingredients with Japanese techniques.
Best Dishes: Palatinate Bread with Ham. Dry Aged Carp.
highlights: An immersive dining experience where guests move through different stations, including a bakery.

name: Jante
history: Tony Hohlfeld and sommelier Mona Schrader transformed a former public toilet into one of Germany's most exciting restaurants.
Best Dishes: Char with Cucumber and Dill. Deer with Elderberry.
highlights: Celebrated for its fermentation techniques and relaxed, young atmosphere.

name: Votum
history: Located in the Leineschloss (state parliament building). Chef Benjamin Gallein serves complex, texture-rich dishes.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Pumpkin. Pigeon with Beetroot.
highlights: Offers a sophisticated dining room with high ceilings within a historic political landmark.

name: 100/200 Kitchen
history: Chef Thomas Imbusch cooks in an open kitchen surrounding a Molteni stove (100 and 200 degrees).
Best Dishes: The 'Water & Salt' Menu. Whole animal usage dishes.
highlights: Located in an industrial warehouse in Veddel, offering a view of the Elbbrücken and a unique 'no-menu' concept.

name: Le Cerf
history: Chef Boris Rommel brings a modern touch to classic French haute cuisine in the Wald & Schlosshotel Friedrichsruhe.
Best Dishes: Goose Liver with Truffle. Saddle of Venison.
highlights: A grand dining room adorned with paintings and chandeliers, representing classic luxury.

name: Hirschen
history: Douce Steiner, one of Germany's most famous female chefs, runs this family hotel restaurant.
Best Dishes: Red Mullet with Fennel. Variations of Rabbit.
highlights: Known for its warm hospitality and Douce Steiner's light, aromatic cuisine.

name: LOUIS restaurant
history: Chef Sebastian Sandor focuses on 'Political' cuisine, often using ingredients to make statements about sustainability.
Best Dishes: Vegetable Charcuterie. Game from local forests.
highlights: Located in a former court building, offering a modern and thoughtful gastronomic concept.

name: Oswald's Gourmetstube
history: Chef Michael Ammon creates unpretentious but high-level cuisine in the Bavarian Forest.
Best Dishes: Bavarian Shrimp. Venison with Celery.
highlights: Part of the Landromantik Hotel Oswald, focusing on regional ingredients with French technique.

name: Gourmetrestaurant Dichter
history: Chef Thomas Kellermann cooks in the Parkhotel Egerner Höfe. The restaurant features huge glass windows opening to the park.
Best Dishes: Fennel cooked in Salt Dough. Phlox with Trout.
highlights: A modern, airy space that connects the diner with the Bavarian nature outside.

name: Le Pavillon
history: Martin Herrmann has held 2 stars for years, cooking in the Relais & Châteaux Hotel Dollenberg.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Champagne Sauce. Black Forest Venison.
highlights: Offers panoramic views of the Black Forest and classic, opulent French service.

name: Ösch Noir
history: Chef Manuel Ulrich returned to his home region to lead this restaurant in the Öschberghof resort.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Dashi. Lamb with Artichoke.
highlights: A dark, stylish, and mysterious interior design ('Noir') that puts the spotlight on the food.

name: Coeur D'Artichaut
history: Chef Frédéric Morel combines his Breton roots with Westphalian ingredients.
Best Dishes: Breton Lobster with Grapefruit. Sweetbreads with Peas.
highlights: Located in a historic building in Münster, offering a relaxed but refined atmosphere.

name: Pietsch
history: Chef Robin Pietsch runs this intimate counter restaurant (only 14 seats) focusing on childhood memories and Harz regional cuisine.
Best Dishes: Potato Soup with Marjoram. Harz Cheese creations.
highlights: Guests sit at a U-shaped counter and watch the team prepare dishes with a personal narrative.

name: PUR
history: Chef Ulrich Heimann focuses on 'Alpine Purity' at the Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden.
Best Dishes: Arctic Char with Buttermilk. Venison from local hunt.
highlights: Offers breathtaking views of the Bavarian Alps from a high-altitude location.

name: AURA by Alexander Herrmann & Tobias Bätz
history: TV Chef Alexander Herrmann and Tobias Bätz run this 'Future Lab' of gastronomy.
Best Dishes: Franconian Soul Menu. Umami bombs using local ferments.
highlights: The restaurant includes a food scout who sources unique ingredients from the surrounding Frankenwald.

name: ammolite - The Lighthouse Restaurant
history: Located inside the lighthouse of the Europa-Park Hotel Bell Rock. Chef Peter Hagen-Wiest creates cosmopolitan cuisine.
Best Dishes: Goose Liver with Passion Fruit. Balfego Tuna.
highlights: The only Michelin-starred restaurant located within a theme park resort in the world.

name: GästeHaus Klaus Erfort
history: Klaus Erfort creates timeless, product-focused French cuisine in a white villa surrounded by a park.
Best Dishes: Langoustine Royale with Sea Urchin. Tartare of Beef with Caviar.
highlights: Renowned for its 'Truth on the Plate' philosophy—minimalist perfection.

name: Esplanade
history: Chef Silio Del Fabro serves modern classic cuisine in the Max-Ophüls-Platz district.
Best Dishes: Sole with Truffle. Pigeon with Cabbage.
highlights: Known for its elegance and a very strong classical foundation inspired by French neighbors.

name: Essigbrätlein
history: Andree Köthe and Yves Ollech are pioneers of 'Spice Cuisine' (Gewürzküche) and vegetable-focused dining.
Best Dishes: Vegetables with unusual spices. Fruit acidity in savory dishes.
highlights: Located in one of Nuremberg's oldest townhouses, offering a unique, quiet culinary philosophy.

name: Lakeside
history: Julian Stowasser cooks on the top floor of The Fontenay hotel with views of the Alster lake.
Best Dishes: Hamachi with Radish. Saddle of Venison with Quince.
highlights: The light-filled, airy dining room perfectly complements the modern, approachable cuisine.

name: Lafleur
history: Located in the Palmengarten. Chef Andreas Krolik is famous for creating a fully vegan menu that matches his meat menu in complexity.
Best Dishes: Vegan Macarons with Carrot. Venison with Wild Berries.
highlights: A pioneer in high-end vegan gastronomy in Germany.

name: Söl'ring Hof
history: Chef Jan-Philipp Berner focuses on the products of the island of Sylt (North Frisian cuisine).
Best Dishes: Sylt Oysters with Sauerkraut. Salt Marsh Lamb.
highlights: Located on the dunes under a thatched roof, offering a complete island experience.

name: Speisemeisterei
history: Located in the baroque Hohenheim Palace. Chef Stefan Gschwendtner blends history with modern techniques.
Best Dishes: Salmon with Cucumber and Dill. Beef with Onion variations.
highlights: Dining in a grandiose palace hall with high ceilings and stucco details.

name: Steinheuers Restaurant
history: Hans Stefan Steinheuer and his son-in-law Christian Binder run this institution of classic German fine dining.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Beurre Blanc. Pigeon from the Ahr valley.
highlights: Located in the wine region of Ahr, famous for its extensive wine list and family hospitality.

name: Obendorfers Eisvogel
history: Hubert Obendorfer created a culinary destination in the Upper Palatinate Lake District.
Best Dishes: Duck Liver with Apple. Lake Fish.
highlights: Offers panoramic views of the lake in a modern, elegant setting.

name: Meierei Dirk Luther
history: Chef Dirk Luther serves classic French cuisine with a modern twist at the Alter Meierhof Vitalhotel.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Coral Sauce. Turbot with Mustard.
highlights: Located directly on the Flensburg Fjord, offering views of the Danish coast.

name: CODA Dessert Dining
history: René Frank redefined dinner by serving a tasting menu consisting entirely of dessert-style techniques (though not all sweet).
Best Dishes: Caviar with Pecan and Jerusalem Artichoke. Parsley Root with Garlic.
highlights: The world's first 2-star 'Dessert Restaurant', blurring the line between savory and sweet.

name: Tim Raue
history: Tim Raue's flagship serves Asian-inspired cuisine free of white sugar, dairy, and gluten.
Best Dishes: Wasabi Langoustine. Peking Duck Interpretation.
highlights: Famous for its bold, punchy flavors (spicy, sour, sweet) and casual but high-energy vibe.

name: Vendôme
history: Joachim Wissler is one of the founders of 'New German School' cooking. Located in the Grandhotel Schloss Bensberg.
Best Dishes: Suckling Pig with Bean Stew. Foie Gras 'Toffifee'.
highlights: Consistently ranked among the best in the world, known for intellectual and technical masterpieces.

name: bianc
history: Matteo Ferrantino brings the warmth and flavors of his native Puglia to Hamburg's HafenCity.
Best Dishes: Red Prawn with Burrata. Risotto with Amalfi Lemon.
highlights: Designed like a Mediterranean piazza with an olive tree in the center and light, bright decor.

name: L.A. Jordan
history: Chef Daniel Schimkowitsch creates bold, contrasting flavors in the Ketschauer Hof hotel.
Best Dishes: Kobe Beef with Onions. Ray Wing with XO Sauce.
highlights: Located in a renowned wine village, offering extensive pairings with local Rieslings.

name: Horváth
history: Sebastian Frank transforms humble Austrian peasant ingredients (celery, kohlrabi) into world-class dishes.
Best Dishes: Salt-baked Celeriac (Aged 12 months). Langos.
highlights: Famous for its 'emancipatory' vegetable cuisine, elevating simple roots to luxury status.

name: FACIL
history: Michael Kempf serves elegant, light cuisine in a glass pavilion on the rooftop of The Mandala Hotel.
Best Dishes: Tea-smoked Duck. Char with Cucumber.
highlights: A green oasis in the middle of Potsdamer Platz, filled with bamboo and light.

name: AUGUST
history: Christian Grünwald creates an avant-garde dining experience in the Villa Haag.
Best Dishes: Menu usually consists of many small, conceptual courses.
highlights: Known for its theatrical presentation, scents, and artistic plating that engages all senses.

name: KOMU
history: Christoph Kunz (formerly of Alois) opened this restaurant to immediate acclaim, focusing on top-tier products.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Melon. Pigeon with Cherry.
highlights: Located in the heart of Munich, offering a relaxed but highly precise fine dining experience.

name: Atelier
history: The flagship restaurant of the Hotel Bayerischer Hof, designed by Axel Vervoordt. Chef Anton Gschwendtner leads the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Vendée Pigeon. Breton Turbot.
highlights: A stylish, intimate space hidden behind a mobile wall in the hotel, known for its art-gallery aesthetic.

name: etz
history: Felix Schneider focuses on hyper-local ingredients, often curing and fermenting them in his glass-walled lab.
Best Dishes: Carp Ham. Local Wagyu.
highlights: Dishes are explained in detail, focusing on the agricultural cycle of the region.

name: PAZ
history: Opened by Chef Poul Andrias Ziska (famous for KOKS), this restaurant continues to explore the unique Faroese terroir.
Best Dishes: Fermented Lamb (Ræst). Sea Urchin.
highlights: Serves cuisine rooted in the harsh, windswept nature of the Faroe Islands, utilizing ancient fermentation techniques.

name: Alchemist
history: Rasmus Munk's 'Holistic Cuisine' experience features 50 courses served under a massive planetarium dome.
Best Dishes: Plastic Fantastic (Edible plastic). Andy Warhol's Banana.
highlights: More than a restaurant, it is a theatrical performance commenting on social and political issues.

name: a|o|c
history: Located in the vaulted cellars of a 17th-century mansion. Søren Selin creates sensory Nordic cuisine.
Best Dishes: Mushroom Ice Cream. Juniper-smoked Scallop.
highlights: Known for its 'New Nordic' approach focusing on local nature and artistic presentation.

name: Signum
history: Chef Thomas Sjögren creates a seafood-focused menu on the shores of Lake Landvetter.
Best Dishes: Langoustine from the West Coast. Hällsnäs Vegetables.
highlights: A picturesque setting where the menu is dictated by the daily catch and the restaurant's garden.

name: Koan
history: Kristian Baumann (born in Korea, raised in Denmark) explores his heritage through a Nordic lens.
Best Dishes: White Kimchi. Mandu with Langoustine.
highlights: Beautiful minimalist design with Korean ceramics, offering a personal journey of identity.

name: AIRA
history: Tommy Myllymäki's purpose-built restaurant on the water in Djurgården.
Best Dishes: Quail cooked over Charcoal. Nordic Seafood platter.
highlights: A stunning architectural building by the sea, serving highly polished, ambitious Nordic gastronomy.

name: Frederikshøj
history: Chef Wassim Hallal is known as the 'King of Jutland', creating technically perfect, flamboyant dishes.
Best Dishes: Caviar and White Asparagus. Pigeon en Croûte.
highlights: Located in a lodge overlooking the forest and the Bay of Aarhus, offering ultra-luxurious dining.

name: Kadeau Copenhagen
history: Nicolai Nørregaard brings the terroir of the Baltic island of Bornholm to the city, preserving ingredients for winter.
Best Dishes: Preserved Berries and Pine. Cold-smoked Salmon.
highlights: Features a massive open kitchen with a wood-fire oven, creating a cozy, cabin-like atmosphere.

name: Kong Hans Kælder
history: The first restaurant in Denmark to receive a Michelin star (1983). Chef Mark Lundgaard respects this legacy with rich, classic French flavors.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Truffle Sauce. Signature Cheese Wagon.
highlights: Located in the oldest building in Copenhagen (a Gothic cellar), offering regal, old-school hospitality.

name: Vollmers
history: Brothers Mats and Ebbe Vollmer highlight the produce of the Scania region in Southern Sweden.
Best Dishes: Scanian Eel. Beetroot and Liquorice.
highlights: Located in a historic townhouse, the cooking emphasizes their personal family history and local terroir.

name: Kontrast
history: Chef Mikael Svensson champions 'Brutalist Nordic' cuisine, using only organic, wild-caught, and ethically sourced ingredients.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Spruce. Dry-aged Dairy Cow.
highlights: A sleek, industrial-style venue in the Vulkan neighborhood with a strong focus on sustainability.

name: Palace
history: Located in a historic 1952 building constructed for the Olympics. Chef Eero Vottonen revived this Finnish icon.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Brown Butter. Whitefish Roe tart.
highlights: Offers panoramic views of Helsinki's harbor and is considered the pinnacle of Finnish gastronomy.

name: Henne Kirkeby Kro
history: British Chef Paul Cunningham cooks in this historic thatched inn on the Danish west coast.
Best Dishes: Garden Turbot. Roast Duck with Honey and Lavender.
highlights: Possesses the largest kitchen garden in Denmark, which dictates the daily menu.

name: Milka
history: Chef David Žefran leads this Alpine destination overlooking Lake Jasna, earning 2 stars quickly after opening.
Best Dishes: Bear Salami. Trout from the lake.
highlights: Modern Alpine cuisine that reflects the rugged biodiversity of the Julian Alps.

name: Bottiglieria 1881
history: Chef Przemysław Klima created the first 2-star restaurant in Poland, focusing on simple Polish ingredients elevated to art.
Best Dishes: Mangalica Pork with Cabbage. Pierogi interpretation.
highlights: A small, intimate venue with a wine cellar atmosphere in the Kazimierz district.

name: Pujol
history: Enrique Olvera transformed Mexican street food and indigenous ingredients into world-class fine dining.
Best Dishes: Mole Madre, Mole Nuevo (Aged over 2500 days). Baby Corn with Chicatana Ant Mayonnaise.
highlights: The most famous restaurant in Mexico, honoring the roots of Aztec and Mayan cooking.

name: Quintonil
history: Chef Jorge Vallejo (a Pujol alumnus) and Alejandra Flores focus on fresh greens ('Quelites') and herbs.
Best Dishes: Charred Avocado Tartare with Escamoles (Ant Larvae). Cactus Sorbet.
highlights: Known for a lighter, vegetable-forward approach to Mexican flavor profiles.

name: STAY by Yannick Alléno
history: Located in the One&Only The Palm. Yannick Alléno brings his mastery of sauces and extraction to Dubai.
Best Dishes: Langoustine Tart with Caviar. Wagyu Beef with 12-spice sauce.
highlights: Features a unique 'Pastry Library' where guests can customize their desserts.

name: Il Ristorante-Niko Romito
history: Niko Romito (of Reale) curated this menu for the Bulgari Hotel, focusing on the essence of Made in Italy.
Best Dishes: Spaghetti e Pomodoro (Technical perfection). Veal Milanese.
highlights: Minimalist Italian cooking where simple titles hide complex preparation methods.

name: Row on 45
history: Chef Jason Atherton's 'penthouse' concept in the Grosvenor House, serving a 17-course tasting journey.
Best Dishes: Brioche with Chicken Butter. Saroma Wagyu.
highlights: Divided into three acts (Champagne lounge, Main dining, Library), offering extreme exclusivity.

name: Tanière³
history: Chef François-Emmanuel Nicol creates an immersive dining experience in the stone vaults of Québec City.
Best Dishes: Deer Moss. Labrador Tea sorbet.
highlights: A blind tasting menu focused on the boreal forest and history of Québec, served in a windowless, theatrical setting.

name: akordu
history: Chef Hiroshi Kawashima (formerly of Mugaritz) creates modern Spanish-influenced cuisine using Nara's ancient ingredients.
Best Dishes: Yamato Pork with Narazuke. Liquid Gnocchi.
highlights: Located in Todaiji Temple park, the name means 'memory' in Basque.

name: Oryori Hanagaki
history: A traditional kaiseki restaurant located within the historic Hotel Musashino.
Best Dishes: Seasonal Kaiseki Course. Venison dishes.
highlights: Guests wear yukata and dine in tatami rooms, experiencing the atmosphere of old Nara.

name: NARA NIKON
history: Chef Shojiro Nikon runs this intimate counter-style Kappo restaurant, focusing on the essence of ingredients.
