Best Dishes: Dashi soup with seasonal fish. Charcoal grilled beef.
highlights: A minimalist setting where the chef's knife skills and conversation take center stage.

name: Tsukumo
history: Chef Masato Nishihara spent years in New York (Kajitsu) mastering Shojin Ryori before opening this modern kaiseki spot.
Best Dishes: Vegetable-forward Kaiseki. Sesame Tofu.
highlights: Blends the precision of Buddhist vegetarian cooking with modern Japanese fine dining.

name: Oro
history: Chef Felipe Bronze is the master of fire. Almost every dish touches the embers or the grill.
Best Dishes: Oyster with Caipirinha Sorbet. Ox Rib cooked for 48 hours.
highlights: Brazilian avant-garde cuisine focusing on native ingredients cooked over fire.

name: Evvai
history: Chef Luiz Filipe Souza defines his style as 'Oriundi'—the fusion of Italian immigrants and Brazilian terroir.
Best Dishes: Mini Pizza (Signature snack). Tortellini with Brazilian cheese.
highlights: A colorful, modern space celebrating the cultural exchange between Italy and Brazil.

name: D.O.M.
history: Alex Atala put Brazilian cuisine on the global map by discovering Amazonian ingredients.
Best Dishes: Amazonian Ant with Pineapple. Fettuccine of Palm Heart.
highlights: Famous for introducing ingredients like Tucupi, Jambu, and ants to fine dining.

name: Lasai
history: Rafa Costa e Silva and Malena Cardiel run this farm-to-table restaurant. 'Lasai' means 'Tranquility' in Basque.
Best Dishes: Vegetable snacks from their own gardens. Fish with Coconut.
highlights: The menu is dictated entirely by the two gardens the chef maintains in Rio.

name: Tuju
history: Chef Ivan Ralston reopened Tuju in a new location, focusing on the weather and seasons of São Paulo.
Best Dishes: Sea Urchin with Corn. Rabbit with Jabuticaba.
highlights: A vertical restaurant structure with a research lab, garden, and dining room.

name: Ru Yuan
history: Chef Fu Yue Liang, a master of Hangzhou cuisine, serves refined local classics in a zen-like setting.
Best Dishes: Braised Pork Belly. Longjing Shrimp.
highlights: Located in the dreamy scenery of the Xixi Wetlands, elevating traditional Zhejiang flavors.

name: Maison Colette
history: Thijs Vervloet dedicated this restaurant to his grandmother. It serves classic French cuisine with aristocratic finesse.
Best Dishes: Vol-au-vent (Luxury version). Dame Blanche.
highlights: A tribute to the golden age of French gastronomy, prioritizing sauces and perfect cooking.

name: Hertog Jan at Botanic
history: Gert De Mangeleer and Joachim Boudens revived their legendary 3-star brand in the Botanic Sanctuary Hotel.
Best Dishes: Tomato Collection. Dim Sum of Langoustine.
highlights: An exclusive, intimate dining experience focusing on produce from their own farm.

name: La Table de Maxime
history: Maxime Collard returned to his native village to create a gastronomic destination in the Ardennes forest.
Best Dishes: Game from the Ardennes. Trout with Sorrel.
highlights: A modern glass extension to an old house, immersing diners in the surrounding nature.

name: L'air du temps
history: Sang-Hoon Degeimbre, a Korean-born Belgian chef, is a pioneer of fermentation and garden-based cooking.
Best Dishes: Vegetables from the 5-hectare garden. Lacto-fermented juices.
highlights: Located in a stunning white square farmhouse, with a philosophy deeply rooted in nature and time.

name: L'Eau Vive
history: Pierre Résimont cooks in a beautifully restored 17th-century watermill.
Best Dishes: Crab with Caviar. Sweetbreads.
highlights: The dining room is located by the stream, offering a picturesque and romantic setting.

name: Sir Kwinten
history: Glenn Verhasselt (chef) and Yanick Dehandschutter (sommelier) transformed a former village tavern into a star destination.
Best Dishes: Hare à la Royale. Hop Shoots (seasonal).
highlights: Known for impeccable sauce work and one of the best wine programs in Belgium.

name: Slagmolen
history: Bert Meewis is a guardian of classical cuisine, refusing to follow trends. Located in a watermill.
Best Dishes: Lady Clementine (Scallops with Truffle). Turbot with Mousseline.
highlights: A bastion of classical French cooking with rich sauces and generous portions.

name: d'Eugénie à Emilie
history: Eric Fernez celebrates the opulence of French gastronomy. Named after his mother and daughter.
Best Dishes: Whole Roasted Poultry. Sea Bass in Salt Crust.
highlights: A place of generosity and classic luxury, famous for table-side carving.

name: De Jonkman
history: Filip Claeys founded the 'North Sea Chefs' collective to promote sustainable, lesser-known local fish.
Best Dishes: North Sea Fish Soup. By-catch fish specials.
highlights: A strong commitment to sustainability and the local maritime heritage of Bruges.

name: Cuchara
history: Jan Tournier created a sleek, black interior to focus senses on the texture and flavor of the food.
Best Dishes: Oyster with Kohlrabi. Eel with Green Herbs.
highlights: Minimalist art-gallery atmosphere with highly conceptual, visually striking dishes.

name: Ma Langue Sourit
history: Cyril Molard brings creativity and playfulness to the Luxembourg dining scene.
Best Dishes: Trout with Wasabi. Crunchy-soft textures.
highlights: Luxembourg's only 2-star restaurant, known for its impeccable service and detail.

name: Léa Linster
history: Founded by Léa Linster (the only woman to win Bocuse d'Or). Her son Louis Linster now leads the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Saddle of Lamb in Potato Crust (Bocuse d'Or dish). Madeleines.
highlights: Successfully transitioned to the next generation while maintaining its legendary status.

name: Vrijmoed
history: Michaël Vrijmoed (former sous-chef of Hof van Cleve) runs this townhouse restaurant.
Best Dishes: The Tomato (Signature vegetarian dish). BBQ Pigeon.
highlights: Famous for making vegetables the star of the show without being strictly vegetarian.

name: Bozar Restaurant
history: Karen Torosyan is a craftsman known for his pastry work. Located in the Centre for Fine Arts.
Best Dishes: Pâté en Croûte. Pithiviers.
highlights: Torosyan is a World Champion of Pâté en Croûte, celebrated for his crust work.

name: Nuance
history: Thierry Theys creates dishes with intricate layers of flavor and contrast.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Vadouvan. Beef with Pickles.
highlights: A chic, banking-district style interior serving highly sophisticated, complex plates.

name: Castor
history: Maarten Bouckaert focuses on the essence of the product in a modern concrete building.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Oxtail. Rabbit.
highlights: The open kitchen is the heart of the restaurant, showcasing disciplined, product-first cooking.

name: Bartholomeus
history: Chef Bart Desmidt renovated his restaurant to a counter-dining concept facing the sea.
Best Dishes: Wagyu Beef. Turbot.
highlights: Offers an intimate connection between the chef, the guest, and the North Sea view.

name: Hof van Cleve - Floris Van Der Veken
history: Formerly Peter Goossens' 3-star temple. Floris Van Der Veken took over in 2024, continuing the legacy of perfection.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Oxtail. Belgian Caviar dishes.
highlights: Remains the gold standard for Belgian hospitality and culinary excellence in a rural farmhouse.

name: Le Chalet de la Forêt
history: Pascal Devalkeneer's sanctuary on the edge of the Sonian Forest.
Best Dishes: Venison with Chocolate. Sea Bass with Truffle.
highlights: A luxurious glass-walled chalet surrounded by trees, offering an escape from Brussels.

name: La Paix
history: David Martin runs this brasserie opposite the Anderlecht abattoirs, fusing French technique with Japanese obsession.
Best Dishes: Live King Crab. Dry Aged Beef.
highlights: Features an origami-inspired ceiling and a tank for live crabs, blending bistro roots with high art.

name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon Miami
history: The Florida outpost of the Robuchon empire, located in the Design District.
Best Dishes: Le Burger (Foie Gras and Beef). Pommes Purée.
highlights: The signature red and black counter seating offers a view of the precise French brigade at work.

name: Sorekara
history: Chef William Shen created a hidden, philosophical dining journey in Baldwin Park.
Best Dishes: Aged Fish Sashimi. Seasonal Hassun.
highlights: Orlando's new fine dining star, focusing on the Japanese concept of 'Sorekara' (and then...).

name: Aramburu
history: Gonzalo Aramburu's restaurant in Recoleta is a pioneer of modern Argentine gastronomy.
Best Dishes: Black Hake. Suckling Pig.
highlights: The first restaurant in Argentina to receive 2 Michelin stars (2024), known for its moody, elegant atmosphere.

name: Rozó
history: Chef Diego Delbecq and pastry chef Camille Pailleau moved their acclaimed restaurant to a former printing house.
Best Dishes: Smoked Eel with Licorice. Mushrooms with Coffee.
highlights: A bright, industrial-chic space featuring a playful and technically precise cuisine.

name: Villa René Lalique
history: Housed in the former home of René Lalique. Chef Paul Stradner leads the kitchen, succeeding Jean-Georges Klein.
Best Dishes: Roebuck with Red Cabbage. Lalique Signature Dessert.
highlights: A glass pavilion designed by Mario Botta, showcasing the crystal artwork of Lalique.

name: Le Jules Verne
history: Chef Frédéric Anton took over this iconic venue on the second floor of the Eiffel Tower, elevating it to gastronomic heights.
Best Dishes: Crab with Zest of Grapefruit. Langoustine Ravioli with Truffle.
highlights: Offers unrivaled views of Paris from 125 meters above ground inside the Iron Lady.

name: Marsan par Hélène Darroze
history: Hélène Darroze pays tribute to her roots in the Landes region (Marsan is her family's territory).
Best Dishes: Tandoori Lobster. Baba with Armagnac (Signature of the Darroze family).
highlights: The dining room features a chef's table and decor inspired by the southwest of France.

name: David Toutain
history: Chef David Toutain is known for his vegetable-forward, textural cuisine and earthy aesthetics.
Best Dishes: Smoked Eel with Black Sesame. Cauliflower with Coconut and White Chocolate.
highlights: A minimalist, zen-like space where the menu is a surprise journey of textures.

name: L'Abysse Monte-Carlo
history: Yannick Alléno expands his sushi temple concept to the Hôtel Hermitage, blending French extraction sauces with Japanese precision.
Best Dishes: Nigiri of Red Mullet. Extraction of Fish Soup.
highlights: A sleek, modern counter offering one of the most refined Japanese experiences on the Riviera.

name: Le Taillevent
history: A legendary institution of French gastronomy. Chef Giuliano Sperandio revitalized the menu while respecting its heritage.
Best Dishes: Spelt Risotto with Frog Legs. Boudin of Lobster.
highlights: Famous for its unparalleled wine service and pairings, boasting one of the best cellars in Paris.

name: Maison Aribert
history: Christophe Aribert created an eco-responsible destination in a 19th-century chalet, focusing on local plants and wellness.
Best Dishes: Trout from the Vercors. Antésite Ice Cream.
highlights: No plastic is used in the kitchen, and the menu is deeply rooted in the Alpine terroir.

name: Table - Bruno Verjus
history: Food critic turned chef Bruno Verjus lets the ingredient dictate the dish. 'The way you treat the product is the way you treat yourself.'
Best Dishes: Colors of the Day (Vegetable tart). Lobster with Clarified Butter.
highlights: Features a long, serpentine counter where diners watch the minimal-intervention cooking.

name: Blue Bay Marcel Ravin
history: Chef Marcel Ravin blends his Caribbean heritage (Martinique) with Mediterranean produce.
Best Dishes: Organic Egg with Cassava and Truffle. Green Papaya Spaghetti.
highlights: Located in the Monte-Carlo Bay Hotel, offering a unique fusion of Creole and French flavors.

name: L'Orangerie
history: Chef Alan Taudon creates a light, feminine cuisine focusing on fish and vegetables in the Four Seasons George V.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Tahitensis Vanilla. Sea Urchin with Cabbage.
highlights: Set in a glass-and-steel conservatory overlooking the hotel's famous marble courtyard.

name: Le Grand Restaurant - Jean-François Piège
history: Jean-François Piège's flagship, featuring his concept of 'Mijotés Modernes' (Modern Stews).
Best Dishes: Sweetbreads on Walnut Shells. Blanc-Manger.
highlights: The dining room features a spectacular glass roof and an intimate, club-like atmosphere.

name: Guy Savoy
history: Located in the Monnaie de Paris, Guy Savoy offers one of the most acclaimed dining experiences in the world.
Best Dishes: Artichoke Soup with Black Truffle. Brioche with Mushrooms.
highlights: Offers views of the Seine and the Louvre, combining grandeur with warm hospitality.

name: Restaurant Le Meurice Alain Ducasse
history: Amaury Bouhours interprets Alain Ducasse's philosophy of 'Naturalness' in a setting inspired by the Chateau de Versailles.
Best Dishes: Noirmoutier Potatoes with Seaweed. Smoked Beef.
highlights: The dining room, designed by Philippe Starck, is a masterpiece of gold, crystal, and mirrors.

name: Relais de la Poste
history: The Coussau family has run this inn for generations. Jean Coussau is a master of Landes cuisine.
Best Dishes: Foie Gras with Grapes. Adour Salmon.
highlights: A temple of traditional southwestern French gastronomy, serving the best products of the region.

name: Paul Bocuse
history: The historic home of Chef Paul Bocuse. Chefs Gilles Reinhardt and Olivier Couvin maintain the legend.
Best Dishes: VGE Black Truffle Soup. Red Mullet with Potato Scales.
highlights: The colorful, baroque building is a pilgrimage site for chefs and food lovers worldwide.

name: Takao Takano
history: Chef Takao Takano (a disciple of Nicolas Le Bec) creates subtle, restrained dishes that bridge Japan and France.
Best Dishes: Deer with Salsify. Scallop with Hazelnut.
highlights: Known for elegance and silence in flavors, letting the main ingredient speak.

name: Mère Brazier
history: Founded by Eugénie Brazier, the first person to hold 6 Michelin stars. Chef Mathieu Viannay modernized the institution.
Best Dishes: Poularde de Bresse Demi-Deuil. Artichoke with Foie Gras.
highlights: Revives the classics of Lyonnaise 'Mère' cooking with contemporary finesse.

name: Le Pré - Xavier Beaudiment
history: Xavier Beaudiment offers a surprise menu that changes daily, focusing on the volcanic terroir of Auvergne.
Best Dishes: Vegetable & Herb Composition. Auvergne Cheese Cart.
highlights: A creative, spontaneous kitchen that refuses to have a set menu.

name: JY'S
history: Jean-Yves Schillinger's cosmopolitan restaurant located in the 'Little Venice' of Colmar.
Best Dishes: King Crab with Yuzu. Pigeon with Cocoa.
highlights: Set in a historic building by the canal, but with a thoroughly modern interior.

name: Serge Vieira
history: Founded by the late Serge Vieira (Bocuse d'Or winner). His wife Marie-Aude and the team continue his legacy.
Best Dishes: Sodalite (Signature appetizer). Turbot with Verbena.
highlights: A stunning architectural fortress built into the landscape of the Cantal mountains.

name: Sushi Yoshinaga
history: Tomoyuki Yoshinaga serves an authentic Edomae sushi omakase behind the Opera Garnier.
Best Dishes: Otoro Nigiri. Steamed Abalone.
highlights: An intimate wooden counter experience relying on fish caught in French waters but treated with Japanese technique.

name: Le Neuvième Art
history: Chef Christophe Roure (MOF) treats the plate as a canvas for his artistic, precise cuisine.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Truffle. Hare à la Royale.
highlights: The interior is minimalist and gallery-like, focusing all attention on the colorful dishes.

name: Le Sarkara
history: Sébastien Vauxion created the world's first gastronomic restaurant dedicated entirely to dessert.
Best Dishes: Celery Root with Vanilla. Mushroom and Chocolate.
highlights: Located in the Hotel K2 Palace, it reimagines dessert as a full meal with savory elements.

name: Le Suquet - Sébastien Bras
history: Sébastien Bras continues the work of his father Michel, inventor of the 'Gargouillou'. Famous for returning his stars in 2018 but now listed again.
Best Dishes: Gargouillou of Young Vegetables. Chocolate Coulant (The original).
highlights: A glass structure floating over the Aubrac plateau, celebrating the wild herbs and light of the region.

name: Le Skiff Club
history: Chef Stéphane Carrade calls his cuisine 'Terroir Progressif', rooted in the Gascony region.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Pine. Lamb of the Pyrenees.
highlights: Located in the Hotel Ha(a)ïtza designed by Philippe Starck, with a yacht club aesthetic.

name: La Table des Amis
history: Christophe Bacquié, formerly a 3-star chef, opened this intimate guest house restaurant in the Luberon.
Best Dishes: Modern Aioli. Stuffed Zucchini Flower.
highlights: A very exclusive venue (Mas Les Eydins) where the chef cooks for a handful of friends and guests.

name: Maison Benoît Vidal
history: Chef Benoît Vidal moved his restaurant from the high mountains of Val d'Isère to the valley of Annecy, maintaining his Alpine soul.
Best Dishes: Arctic Char with Pine. Hay-smoked meats.
highlights: Focuses on the connection between the raw nature of the Alps and human craftsmanship.

name: Jean Sulpice
history: Jean Sulpice revitalized the legendary Auberge du Père Bise on the banks of Lake Annecy.
Best Dishes: Fera Fish with Pistachio. Crayfish from the lake.
highlights: Located literally on the water's edge, creating a cuisine that reflects the lake and the mountains.

name: Duende
history: Pierre Gagnaire's outpost in Nîmes, led by Nicolas Fontaine. Located in the Hotel Imperator.
Best Dishes: Gambero Rosso with Chorizo. Veal with Olives.
highlights: Blends Gagnaire's avant-garde style with the sunny, bold flavors of the Occitanie region.

name: Py-r
history: Chef Pierre Lambinon serves innovative cuisine in the vaulted brick cellars of Toulouse.
Best Dishes: Cassoulet (Modern interpretation). Trout with Verjuice.
highlights: Known for its white minimalist decor contrasted against ancient pink brick arches.

name: La Scène
history: Stéphanie Le Quellec's independent restaurant after leaving the Prince de Galles. 'The Scene' puts the open kitchen center stage.
Best Dishes: Caviar on Toast. Sweetbreads 'Pomme de Ris'.
highlights: A chic, energetic atmosphere where the kitchen is the theater of the dining room.

name: Les Ambassadeurs by Christophe Cussac
history: Christophe Cussac (a disciple of Robuchon) revived this historic dining room in the Hotel Metropole.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Maltaise Sauce. Lamb Chops with Thyme.
highlights: Offers refined, classic Mediterranean cuisine in a Jacques Garcia-designed setting.

name: Les Morainières
history: Ingrid and Michaël Arnoult run this restaurant in the middle of the Marestel vineyards.
Best Dishes: Crayfish with Bisque. Pigeon from Flanders.
highlights: Offers spectacular views of the Rhône valley and vineyards.

name: La Pyramide - Maison Henriroux
history: A legendary address formerly run by Fernand Point. Patrick Henriroux has maintained its prestige for decades.
Best Dishes: Bresse Chicken in Bladder (Homage). Chartreuse Soufflé.
highlights: A historic pillar of French gastronomy, blending museum-like history with modern luxury.

name: Cédric Burtin
history: Formerly known as L'Amaryllis. Cédric Burtin showcases the terroir of Burgundy with a modern touch.
Best Dishes: Snails from Burgundy. Charolais Beef.
highlights: Located in a renovated mill, offering a refined country dining experience.

name: La Merise
history: Christelle and Cedric Deckert built this half-timbered Alsatian house using traditional methods.
Best Dishes: Venison with Spätzle. Sauerkraut variation.
highlights: A perfect example of Alsatian warmth combined with high-level gastronomy.

name: L'Abysse Paris
history: Located in the Pavillon Ledoyen. Chef Yasunari Okazaki collaborates with Yannick Alléno.
Best Dishes: Nigiri with Extraction Jelly. Sea Urchin Toast.
highlights: Focuses on the interaction between French extraction techniques and Japanese sushi mastery.

name: Racine
history: Kazuyuki Tanaka blends Japanese precision with French produce in a tiny open-kitchen restaurant.
Best Dishes: The 'Tanaka' Salad. Pigeon with Miso.
highlights: Known for the extreme beauty and complexity of the plating.

name: Michel Kayser - Restaurant Alexandre
history: Michel Kayser serves cuisine deeply rooted in the Nîmes and Camargue region.
Best Dishes: Truffle Surprise. Camargue Rice and Bull.
highlights: Set in a beautiful park with century-old trees, offering a true escape in the Gard.

name: L'Oiseau Blanc
history: Chef David Bizet leads this rooftop restaurant at The Peninsula, themed around early aviation.
Best Dishes: Lièvre à la Royale. Blue Lobster.
highlights: Features a replica of the L'Oiseau Blanc biplane and stunning views of the Eiffel Tower.

name: Maison Nouvelle
history: Celebrity Chef Philippe Etchebest returned to Bordeaux to open this intimate, personal restaurant.
Best Dishes: Ravioli of Mushrooms. The 'Maison' Dessert.
highlights: Located in the Chartrons district, designed like a private home.

name: La Côte Saint-Jacques
history: Jean-Michel Lorain continues the legacy of his family at this riverside institution.
Best Dishes: Oysters in Sea Water Jelly. Blood Sausage Terrine.
highlights: Situated on the banks of the Yonne river, famous for its exceptional hospitality.

name: La Table de Pavie
history: Yannick Alléno creates a menu that dialogues with the prestigious wines of Saint-Emilion.
Best Dishes: Modern Pot-au-Feu. Mushrooms from the vineyards.
highlights: Located in the Hotel de Pavie, offering views over the historic village rooftops and vineyards.

name: Blanc
history: Chef Shinichi Sato (formerly of Passage 53) returns with a minimalist, ingredient-obsessed venue.
Best Dishes: Abalone with Liver Sauce. Grilled Beef.
highlights: A discreet, luxurious space in the 16th arrondissement focusing on purity and perfection.

name: La Table de Franck Putelat
history: Franck Putelat describes his cooking as 'Classical-Fiction', twisting classics with emotion.
Best Dishes: Cassoulet of the Sea. Tartare 'F&P'.
highlights: Located at the foot of the medieval Cité of Carcassonne.

name: La Table de Yoann Conte
history: Yoann Conte took over Marc Veyrat's 'Blue House', cooking with Alpine herbs and fire.
Best Dishes: Carrot cooked in earth. Fera from the lake.
highlights: A rustic yet luxurious lakeside chalet with a private pontoon.

name: Auberge de l'Ill
history: The Haeberlin family has run this Alsatian legend for over 50 years (formerly 3 stars).
Best Dishes: Salmon Soufflé Auberge de l'Ill. Mousseline of Frogs.
highlights: Located in a willow-shaded garden by the river Ill, it is the definition of Alsatian warmth.

name: La Table d'Olivier Nasti
history: Chef Olivier Nasti is an avid hunter and forager, bringing the essence of the Alsatian forest to the Hotel Le Chambard.
Best Dishes: Smoked Eel from the Rhine. Venison with Chocolate.
highlights: Located in a picturesque Alsatian village, blending rustic hunting lodge aesthetics with modern precision.

name: Anne de Bretagne
history: Mathieu Guibert took over this institution facing the Atlantic, continuing a legacy of seafood excellence.
Best Dishes: Iodized compositions. Blue Lobster.
highlights: Offers panoramic views of the ocean, focusing on the salty terroir of the Retz region.

name: L'Auberge des Glazicks
history: Olivier Bellin transformed his family's village inn into a temple of Breton cuisine, championing buckwheat.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Pork. Buckwheat Ice Cream.
highlights: Famous for the 'Mar et Moun' (Surf and Turf) concept, blending local seafood with earthy meats.

name: Ekaitza
history: Guillaume Roget, a former sommelier turned chef, explores the richness of the Basque Country.
Best Dishes: Line-caught Hake. Sweetbreads with Basque spices.
highlights: A welcoming atmosphere near the port of Saint-Jean-de-Luz, focusing on local fishermen's catch.

name: L'Auberge de Saint-Rémy - Fanny Rey & Jonathan Wahid
history: Chef Fanny Rey and Pastry Chef Jonathan Wahid run this charming inn in the heart of Provence.
Best Dishes: Saint-Pierre with Shellfish. Signature Millefeuille.
highlights: A place of light and sun, celebrating the Mediterranean market produce.

name: René et Maxime Meilleur
history: A father and son duo who built their chalet 'La Bouitte' by hand. They cook a pure Alpine cuisine.
Best Dishes: Polenta with Beaufort Cheese. Milk in all its forms (Dessert).
highlights: Located at high altitude, offering an authentic and rustic yet incredibly refined Savoyard experience.

name: Cyril Attrazic
history: Cyril Attrazic embodies the rugged terroir of Aubrac in his family's hotel-restaurant.
Best Dishes: Aubrac Beef. Aligot (Traditional cheese mash).
highlights: Focuses on the 'ecosystem' of the Aubrac plateau, working closely with local breeders.

name: La Villa Archange
history: Chef Bruno Oger offers a cuisine of the senses in a private Bastide near Cannes.
Best Dishes: Abalone from Groix. Lemon from the garden.
highlights: A discreet and luxurious setting with a beautiful shaded courtyard.

name: L'Auberge de Montmin
history: Florian Favario settled in this mountain pass to cook closer to nature and his own vegetable garden.
Best Dishes: Snail Tart. Arctic Char.
highlights: Situated at Col de la Forclaz with stunning views, prioritizing hyper-local sourcing.

name: Maison Rostang
history: Founded by Michel Rostang, now led by Nicolas Beaumann. A bastion of classic gastronomy and wine.
Best Dishes: Truffle Sandwich (Legendary). Pike Quenelles.
highlights: Famous for its wood-paneled decor, extensive wine collection, and truffle obsession.

name: Lalique
history: Chef Jérôme Schilling integrates the world of Sauternes wine into his cuisine at Château Lafaurie-Peyraguey.
Best Dishes: Mackerel marinated in Sauternes. Crystal-inspired desserts.
highlights: Dining amidst Lalique crystal in a Premier Grand Cru Classé vineyard.

name: Christophe Hay - Fleur de Loire
history: Christophe Hay celebrates the Loire river fish and vegetables from his own massive permaculture garden.
Best Dishes: Carp à la Chambord. Garden Vegetables.
highlights: A luxurious eco-resort focused on sustainability and the heritage of the Loire Valley.

name: La Grand'Vigne - Les Sources de Caudalie
history: Chef Nicolas Masse draws inspiration from the surrounding vineyards of Château Smith Haut Lafitte.
Best Dishes: Grape marc-fed Beef. Aquitaine Caviar.
highlights: Located in a vinotherapy spa resort, the menu is deeply connected to the grapevine cycle.

name: L'Observatoire du Gabriel
history: Alexandre Baumard brings precision to the Place de la Bourse.
Best Dishes: Turbot with Artichoke. Breton Lobster.
highlights: Offers views of the Garonne river and the Miroir d'eau from an 18th-century landmark.

name: Maison Ronan Kervarrec
history: Ronan Kervarrec returned to Brittany to share his childhood memories through food.
Best Dishes: Buckwheat Galette with Caviar. Shellfish stew.
highlights: A personal, emotional cuisine housed in a refined setting near Rennes.

name: La Voile - La Réserve Ramatuelle
history: Chef Eric Canino pioneered 'wellness gastronomy', focusing on lightness without sacrificing flavor.
Best Dishes: Red Mullet with Basil. Vegetable Garden Menu.
highlights: Overlooks the Mediterranean with a menu that balances health and hedonism.

name: La Grenouillère
history: Alexandre Gauthier runs this radical, avant-garde restaurant in a metal structure resembling blacksmith huts.
Best Dishes: Smoked Eel. Herbs from the marshes.
highlights: A raw, immersive experience where the kitchen is completely open and the food is provocative.

name: La Table de Christophe Dufossé
history: Christophe Dufossé revitalized the Château de Beaulieu, adding a strong focus on nature and eco-responsibility.
Best Dishes: Scallops from the Opal Coast. Garden Vegetables.
highlights: Located in a stunning brick château with its own vegetable gardens and orchard.

name: Le Pressoir d'Argent - Gordon Ramsay
history: Gordon Ramsay's presence in Bordeaux, centered around a legendary solid silver lobster press.
Best Dishes: Pressed Lobster (Tableside service). Gironde Beef.
highlights: Located in the InterContinental Bordeaux, celebrating local products with British flair.

name: Le Parc Les Crayères
history: Christophe Moret (formerly of Shangri-La) leads this iconic Champagne château kitchen.
Best Dishes: Scallop and Caviar. Venison with Grand Veneur sauce.
highlights: Set in a magnificent park, offering one of the most comprehensive Champagne lists in the world.

name: Georges Blanc
history: Georges Blanc has held 3 stars since 1981, transforming his village into a culinary destination.
Best Dishes: Bresse Chicken with Morels. Vonnas Crepes.
highlights: The definitive temple of Bresse poultry and classic French sauces.

name: Sylvestre Wahid - Les Grandes Alpes
history: Sylvestre Wahid creates a bespoke dining experience with only 4 tables.
Best Dishes: Roscoff Crab. Lemon from Menton dessert.
highlights: An ultra-exclusive, intimate setting where the chef cooks tailored dishes for guests.

name: Le Clarence
history: Chef Christophe Pelé combines classical French bases with wild creativity in a mansion owned by the Prince of Luxembourg.
Best Dishes: Red Mullet with Lardo. Pigeon.
highlights: The interior mimics a 19th-century château, contrasting with the modern, spontaneous cooking.

name: Flaveur
history: Brothers Gaël and Mickaël Tourteaux create a four-handed cuisine inspired by their travels.
Best Dishes: Mediterranean Fish with Exotic Spices. Nice Vegetables.
highlights: A fusion of Niçoise tradition with flavors from the West Indies and Asia.

name: La Table Lionel Giraud
history: Lionel Giraud took over the Maison Saint Crescent, focusing on short circuits and the Occitan terroir.
Best Dishes: Cassoulet Deconstructed. Gruissan Oysters.
highlights: Located in a former oratory, celebrating the rugged landscape of the Languedoc.

name: La Côte d'Or
history: Patrick Bertron continues the legacy of the legendary Bernard Loiseau.
Best Dishes: Frog Legs with Garlic Purée. Pike Perch.
highlights: Maintains the spirit of 'Goût du Terroir' in a historic burgundy inn.

name: William Frachot
history: Chef William Frachot redefined Burgundian cuisine with a lighter, modern touch.
Best Dishes: Eggs Meurette (Modern). Charolais Beef.
highlights: Located in the Hostellerie du Chapeau Rouge, blending colorful design with deep flavors.

name: La Fourchette des Ducs
history: Nicolas Stamm and Serge Schaal run this sophisticated Alsatian establishment.
Best Dishes: Duck Foie Gras. Game dishes in season.
highlights: Decorated by Baccarat crystal and Lalique, representing the height of Alsatian elegance.

name: Baumanière 1850
history: Chef Thomas Prod'homme brings the Mediterranean spirit of Baumanière (Provence) to the snowy Alps.
Best Dishes: Black Truffle Gnocchi. Sisteron Lamb.
highlights: Located in the Hotel Strato, offering a unique blend of Provençal flavors in a ski resort.

name: Casadelmar
history: Chef Fabio Bragagnolo blends Corsican ingredients with Italian techniques.
Best Dishes: Cannelloni with Spider Crab. Dentex fish.
highlights: Offers stunning views of the bay of Porto-Vecchio, emphasizing seafood and Mediterranean herbs.

name: Le Chabichou by Stéphane Buron
history: Stéphane Buron (MOF) creates refined cuisine in one of Courchevel's most historic white chalets.
Best Dishes: Pig Trotter (Homage). Truffle Fondue.
highlights: A symbol of Courchevel luxury, focusing on precision and noble ingredients.

name: La Chèvre d'Or
history: Chef Tom Meyer creates sunny, complex dishes in this eagle's nest overlooking the Mediterranean.
Best Dishes: Rabbit with Octopus. Lemon from Menton.
highlights: Offers one of the most breathtaking views on the French Riviera.

name: La Cime
history: Chef Yusuke Takada connects French technique with Japanese ingredients. 'La Cime' means 'The Peak'.
Best Dishes: Boudin Dog (Signature snack). Seasonal Fish with Citrus.
highlights: Known for the famous black 'Boudin Dog' and highly artistic, modern plating.

name: Miyamoto
history: A kaiseki restaurant focusing deeply on the soup (Wanmono) and the purity of dashi.
Best Dishes: Seasonal Wanmono (Soup). Grilled Fish.
highlights: A quiet, counter-style restaurant that emphasizes the subtle changing of seasons.

name: Fujiya 1935
history: Chef Tetsuya Fujiwara is the 4th generation chef. He blends Spanish influence with Japanese sensibility.
Best Dishes: Bread of the Forest. Ayu Confit.
highlights: Known for the incredible texture of its homemade bread and a nature-inspired aesthetic.

name: Koryu
history: Chef Osamu Matsuo serves bold, flavorful kaiseki dishes that pair well with alcohol.
Best Dishes: Nimonowan (Simmered Bowl). Sashimi with unique garnishes.
highlights: A lively counter experience where the chef's personality shines through the food.

name: Yugen
history: Focuses on the beauty of subtlety ('Yugen'). A refined kaiseki experience.
Best Dishes: Hassun. Rice cooked in clay pot.
highlights: A minimalist space dedicated to the Tea Ceremony spirit of hospitality.

name: Shunsaiten Tsuchiya
history: Located in a renovated traditional house. Chef Yukihiko Tsuchiya elevates tempura to an art form.
Best Dishes: Prawn Tempura. Seasonal Vegetable Tempura.
highlights: Combines the lightness of tempura with the structure of a kaiseki meal.

name: Sushi Harasho
history: A reservation-only sushi counter known for high-quality neta and perfect rice temperature.
Best Dishes: Steamed Abalone. Sea Urchin Nigiri.
highlights: Considered one of the pinnacles of Edomae sushi in the Kansai region.

name: Yusokuryori Mankamero
history: Founded in 1716. Specializes in Yusoku Ryori (Imperial Court Cuisine) and ceremonial knife rituals (Shikibocho).
Best Dishes: Imperial style Sea Bream. Turtle Soup.
highlights: A living museum of Japanese culinary history, serving food fit for the Emperor.

name: Sanso Kyoyamato
history: A historic Ryotei located in the grounds of a temple, offering views of the Yasaka Pagoda.
Best Dishes: Seasonal Kaiseki. Bamboo Shoot Rice.
highlights: The setting is historically significant, having been a meeting place for samurai in the Edo period.

name: Ogata
history: Chef Toshiro Ogata is legendary for his obsession with the absolute best seasonal ingredients.
Best Dishes: Taiza Crab (Winter). Bamboo Shoots (Spring).
highlights: One of the most difficult reservations in Japan. The cuisine is deceptively simple but profound.

name: Kyokaiseki Kichisen
history: Chef Yoshimi Tanigawa beat Morimoto on Iron Chef. He serves energetic, elaborate Kaiseki.
Best Dishes: Hassun (Elaborate presentation). Clear Soup.
highlights: Located in the Shimogamo Shrine forest, known for strict discipline and high energy.

name: Gion Nishikawa
history: Chef Masayoshi Nishikawa offers a welcoming, educational kaiseki experience in Gion.
Best Dishes: Sabazushi (Mackerel Sushi). Egg Tofu.
highlights: Famous for the chef's friendly explanations and the beautiful counter made of hinoki wood.

name: Otagi
history: Chef Mamoru Baba serves a freer, more innovative style of Japanese cuisine.
Best Dishes: Wagyu Beef Cutlet Sandwich. Seasonal Pot Rice.
highlights: Located a bit far from the center, offering a relaxed and creative dining atmosphere.

name: Numata
history: Chef Kazuya Numata is a tempura specialist known for his precise frying and ingredient selection.
Best Dishes: Amadai Tempura. Sweet Potato.
highlights: Famous for serving 'Kumamoto Aka-Ushi' beef as tempura.

name: KAHALA
history: Chef Yoshiharu Moris created his own genre of cuisine in 1971. It is neither purely French nor Japanese.
Best Dishes: Kahala's signature beef millefeuille. Coffee oil and salt.
highlights: An intimate 8-seat counter where the chef has been serving creative fusion for over 50 years.

name: Oimatsu Hisano
history: Specializes in traditional Naniwa (Osaka) cuisine, focusing on wild vegetables and fish.
Best Dishes: Simmered dishes using Osaka greens. Yodogawa natural eel.
highlights: A place to experience the authentic, historical flavors of Osaka's culinary heritage.

name: Restaurant Story
history: Chef Tom Sellers tells his personal life story through food. The restaurant is housed in a former Victorian toilet block.
Best Dishes: Beef Fat Candle (Bread course). Paddington Bear (Marmalade sandwich).
highlights: Guests leave a book behind, creating a library. The menu is a narrative journey.

name: Restaurant Andrew Fairlie
history: Located in the Gleneagles Hotel. It is the only 2-star restaurant in Scotland, founded by the late Andrew Fairlie.
Best Dishes: Home-Smoked Scottish Lobster. Highland Lamb.
highlights: A dining room hidden within the hotel, offering the absolute pinnacle of Scottish produce.

name: Alex Dilling at Hotel Café Royal
history: Alex Dilling brings technical precision and classic French elegance to Regent Street.
Best Dishes: Hunter Chicken (Pollo alla Cacciatora technical rework). Clam Chowder.
highlights: An intimate, bright dining room overlooking the curve of Regent Street.

name: Patrick Guilbaud
history: Founded in 1981, it is Ireland's most renowned restaurant, holding 2 stars for decades.
Best Dishes: Blue Lobster Ravioli. Wicklow Lamb.
highlights: Located in the Merrion Hotel, featuring a significant collection of Irish art.

name: Ynyshir
history: Gareth Ward runs this destination restaurant with a DJ, disco ball, and a heavy focus on aged meat.
Best Dishes: Salt-Aged Wagyu. Char Siu Pork.
highlights: An intense, fun, and uncompromising experience known as 'Ingredient led, flavor driven, fat fueled, meat obsessed'.

name: Restaurant Sat Bains
history: Sat Bains turned a venue under electric pylons near a flyover into a world-class gastronomic destination.
Best Dishes: The Ng7 (Foraged herbs from the postcode). Scallop with Pumpkin.
highlights: Features an urban garden and a 'Nucleus' chef's table.

name: Opheem
history: Aktar Islam became the first chef outside London to win 2 stars for Indian cuisine in the UK.
Best Dishes: Aloo Tuk (Potato chaat). Soft Shell Crab.
highlights: Progressive Indian cooking that deconstructs traditional recipes using seasonal British produce.

name: Ikoyi
history: Jeremy Chan and Iré Hassan-Odukale explore spices from sub-Saharan West Africa with hyper-modern technique.
Best Dishes: Smoked Jollof Rice. Plantain with Raspberry Salt.
highlights: Located at 180 The Strand, known for bold, heat-driven flavors never seen before in fine dining.

name: Dinner by Heston Blumenthal
history: Heston Blumenthal and Chef Ashley Palmer-Watts research British culinary history dating back to the 1300s.
Best Dishes: Meat Fruit (c.1500). Tipsy Cake (c.1810).
highlights: Located in the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, famous for reviving historic recipes with modern science.

name: The Clove Club
history: Isaac McHale's restaurant in the Shoreditch Town Hall started the modern British supper club movement.
Best Dishes: Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Pine Salt. Raw Orkney Scallop.
highlights: A relaxed atmosphere with high-end cooking, prioritizing Scottish produce.

name: Kitchen Table
history: James Knappett (Chef) and Sandia Chang (Sommelier) run this 19-seat counter behind a curtain.
Best Dishes: Daily changing tasting menu (often 20 courses).
highlights: Interaction is key; the chefs cook and serve everything directly to the guests.

name: Terre
history: Chef Vincent Crepel combines his French training and time in Asia with the terroir of County Cork.
Best Dishes: Cod with Caviar. Chawanmushi with Otter Shell Clam.
highlights: Located in the Castlemartyr Resort, offering a dynamic dining experience that moves through different rooms.

name: Le Manoir aux Quat' Saisons, a Belmond Hotel
history: Raymond Blanc's legendary hotel and restaurant, holding 2 stars since 1984.
Best Dishes: Crab Bisque. Garden Vegetable Risotto.
highlights: Set in extensive organic gardens which supply the kitchen, defining the English country house hotel.

name: A. Wong
history: Andrew Wong studies the 3,000-year culinary history of China. It is the first Chinese restaurant outside Asia to hold 2 stars.
Best Dishes: Shanghai Steamed Dumplings (Xiao Long Bao). Peking Duck.
highlights: Famous for its intricate dim sum lunch and the 'Taste of China' tasting menu at dinner.

name: The Ritz Restaurant
history: Chef John Williams MBE preserves the Escoffier tradition in one of the world's most beautiful dining rooms.
Best Dishes: Bresse Duck. Langoustine à la Nage.
highlights: Features chandeliers, marble columns, and a live pianist. Tableside service (guéridon) is a specialty.

name: Brooklands by Claude Bosi
history: Located on the rooftop of The Peninsula London, Claude Bosi pays homage to British aviation and motorsport.
Best Dishes: Exmoor Caviar with Roscoff Onion. Racan Guinea Fowl.
highlights: Features a scale model of the Concorde on the ceiling and a terrace overlooking Hyde Park.

name: Landhaus Bacher
history: A Wachau valley institution. Thomas Dorfer continues the legacy of Lisl Wagner-Bacher.
Best Dishes: Marinated Goose Liver. Wachau Apricot Dumplings.
highlights: Combines Austrian tradition with modern lightness, set in the heart of wine country.

name: Döllerer
history: Andreas Döllerer invented 'Alpine Cuisine' (Cuisine Alpine), using ingredients from the nearby Bluntautal valley.
Best Dishes: Bluntau Char. Alpine Scallops (Bone Marrow).
highlights: Showcases the distinct flavors of the Salzburg Alps, from rocks to lichens.

name: Ois
history: Philip Rachinger (Mühltalhof) represents the new generation of Austrian chefs, blending tradition with punk energy.
Best Dishes: Mühlviertel Sushi. Bread Soup.
highlights: Located in a remote hotel by the river, offering a highly creative and personal menu.

name: Taubenkobel
history: Founded by the Eselböck family. Alain Weissgerber focuses on the wild herbs and ingredients of the Pannonian plain.
Best Dishes: Pannonian Bouillabaisse. Duck Heart.
highlights: A romantic, boho-chic farm complex near Lake Neusiedl.

name: Obauer
history: Brothers Karl and Rudi Obauer have maintained world-class standards for decades in the mountains.
Best Dishes: Trout Strudel. Werfen Lamb.
highlights: Known for 'Werfen Cooking'—regional, grounded, yet open to the world.

name: SENNS.Restaurant
history: Andreas Senn cooks in a former bell foundry (Gusswerk), creating a dark, industrial, atmospheric space.
Best Dishes: Char with Kimchi. Goose Liver with Popcorn.
highlights: A trendy, club-like atmosphere serving technically brilliant dishes.

name: Silvio Nickol Gourmet Restaurant
history: Located in the Palais Coburg. Silvio Nickol is known for his elaborate, multi-component dishes.
Best Dishes: Duck Liver with Popcorn and Corn. Venison.
highlights: The hotel sits above six centuries of wine cellars containing 60,000 bottles.

name: Stüva
history: Benjamin Parth is one of the youngest top chefs in Austria, following the philosophy 'Keep it simple'.
Best Dishes: Arctic Char with Gentian. Turbot.
highlights: Offers cosmopolitan fine dining in the heart of the Ischgl ski resort.

name: Restaurant 141 by Joachim Jaud
history: Located at a golf course, Chef Joachim Jaud surprises guests with ambitious gourmet cuisine.
Best Dishes: Tyrolean Grey Cattle. Crayfish.
highlights: Combines a casual setting with unexpectedly high-level gastronomy.

name: Doubek
history: Stefan Doubek focuses on fire and craftsmanship in a dark, moody, architecturally striking space.
Best Dishes: Grilled Pigeon. Goat Cheese matured in ash.
highlights: Everything is cooked over open fire; the atmosphere is intense and focused.

name: Ikarus
history: Located in Red Bull's Hangar-7. The executive chef (Martin Klein) implements a different guest chef's menu every month.
Best Dishes: Changes monthly based on the guest chef.
highlights: The most unique dining concept in the world, surrounded by historical airplanes and Formula 1 cars.

name: Mraz & Sohn
history: Lukas and Manuel Mraz (and father Markus) run this unconventional, fun, family restaurant.
Best Dishes: Often finger food. Cheese trolley.
highlights: Known for breaking fine dining rules, casual service, and a highly creative tasting menu.

name: Griggeler Stuba
history: Thorsten Probost and his team focus strictly on herbs and products from the Vorarlberg mountains.
Best Dishes: Mountain Herbs Salad. Venison.
highlights: Located in the Burg Vital Resort, emphasizing health and alpine purity.

name: Kräuterreich by Vitus Winkler
history: Vitus Winkler tells stories of the mountains through wild herbs (Kräuterreich means Herb Kingdom).
Best Dishes: The Forest Floor. River Stones.
highlights: Each dish relates to a specific hiking trail or mountain memory.

name: Gourmetrestaurant Tannenhof
history: Chef Gustav Jantscher creates Alpine haute cuisine in a 5-star superior hotel.
Best Dishes: Tyrolean Speck Dumpling (Deconstructed). Venison.
highlights: An intimate dining room with only a few tables, offering highly personalized service.

name: Schwarzer Adler
history: Chef Johannes Nuding (formerly of Sketch London) returned home to take over this historic inn.
Best Dishes: Spinach with Truffle. Glazed Veal Sweetbread.
highlights: Located in a 700-year-old building, blending immense history with world-class cooking.

name: Rote Wand Chef's Table
history: Located in the 'Schualhus' (old schoolhouse). Chef Julian Stieger serves a menu centered on fermentation and local products.
Best Dishes: Koji-aged Beef. Fermented Vegetables.
highlights: Guests sit around an open kitchen counter in a historic wooden building.

name: Konstantin Filippou
history: Konstantin Filippou blends his Austrian upbringing with his Greek heritage.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Calf's Tongue. Brandade with Caviar.
highlights: A minimalist, dark dining room that focuses entirely on the contrast of land and sea.

name: Delta
history: Located in the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. Chefs George Papazacharias and Thanos Feskos focus on sustainability.
Best Dishes: Potato millefeuille. Fermented fruits.
highlights: Greece's only 2-star restaurant, famous for its visually stunning, nature-inspired dishes.

name: Bao Li Xuan
history: The Chinese restaurant of the Bulgari Hotel Shanghai. Chef Fu Man Biao serves refined Cantonese classics.
Best Dishes: Crispy Suckling Pig. Abalone Puff.
highlights: Located in the restored Chamber of Commerce Shanghai building, blending history with luxury.

name: Canton 8 (Huangpu)
history: Famous for being one of the world's cheapest 2-star restaurants.
Best Dishes: Char Siu (BBQ Pork). Shrimp Dumplings.
highlights: Offers high-quality Cantonese dim sum and roast meats at extremely affordable prices.

name: Da Vittorio - Shanghai
history: The first outpost of the legendary Cerea family outside Europe, bringing authentic Italian hospitality to the Bund.
Best Dishes: Paccheri alla Vittorio. Egg à la Egg.
highlights: Offers views of the Pudong skyline and the same level of family-style luxury as the original.

name: The House of Rong
history: A brand under the Xin Rong Ji group, focusing on the cuisine of Linhai (Taizhou).
Best Dishes: Yellow Croaker. Sea Anemone.
highlights: Located in a historic villa, serving refined coastal cuisine with exceptional ingredients.

name: Fu He Hui
history: Chef Tony Lu elevates vegetarian cuisine to fine dining heights using rare fungi and seasonal vegetables.
Best Dishes: Porcini smoked in a jar. Braised Tofu.
highlights: A zen-like sanctuary offering a set menu that changes with the seasons.

name: 8 ½ Otto e Mezzo Bombana
history: Umberto Bombana's Shanghai branch, located in the Rockbund development.
Best Dishes: Truffle Pasta. Lobster Salad.
highlights: Known for its white truffle season and elegant, sophisticated Italian cooking.

name: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine, Shanghai
history: Part of the Singaporean group known for consistency and excellence in Cantonese cooking.
Best Dishes: Peking Duck. Steamed Fish.
highlights: Located in Yi Feng Galleria, celebrated for its impeccably executed traditional dishes.

name: Ji Pin Court
history: Chef Yat Fung Cheung (formerly of Fook Lam Moon) serves high-end Cantonese cuisine.
Best Dishes: Crispy Chicken. Abalone.
highlights: Located in a French concession villa, offering a discreet and luxurious dining environment.

name: 102 House
history: Originally from Foshan, Chef Xu Jingye brings refined 'fucai' (official banquet cuisine) to Shanghai.
Best Dishes: Sweet and Sour Pork with Fruit. Crystal King Prawn.
highlights: Combines traditional Cantonese techniques with modern aesthetics.

name: VYN
history: Daniel Berlin returned to the dining scene with VYN, located in a former farm in Österlen.
Best Dishes: Celeriac cooked in open fire. Game birds.
highlights: Offers sweeping views of the Baltic Sea and a hyper-seasonal menu focused on Skåne's terroir.

name: Miyamaso
history: A legendary ryokan located in the mountains north of Kyoto. Chef Hisato Nakahigashi serves 'Souan' (grass-thatched hut) cuisine, focusing on foraging.
Best Dishes: Grilled Ayu (Sweetfish). Wild Boar Hot Pot.
highlights: Guests dine in a secluded mountain setting, eating ingredients gathered from the surrounding forests and streams.

name: Sumibi Kappo Ifuki
history: Chef Norio Yamamoto specializes in charcoal-grilled (Sumibi) kaiseki cuisine in the heart of Gion.
Best Dishes: Charcoal Grilled Spanish Mackerel. Bear Meat.
highlights: The open kitchen centers around a charcoal grill where guests watch the chef masterfully control the fire.

name: Kenninji Gion Maruyama
history: Yoshio Maruyama established this kaiseki institution near Kennin-ji Temple. It is the main branch of the Maruyama brand.
Best Dishes: Bamboo Shoot Kaiseki (Spring). Matsutake Mushroom (Autumn).
highlights: Emphasizes the 'Kyoto aesthetic', offering a complete cultural experience with seasonal interior decorations.

name: Kodaiji Wakuden
history: Originally an inn in Tango (northern Kyoto), it moved to the city to serve refined kaiseki. It has produced many famous chefs.
Best Dishes: Taiza Crab (Winter). Dai-gokujo (Top grade) Rice.
highlights: Known for sourcing the absolute best crab in Japan during winter from their origins in Tango.

name: Kikunoi Roan
history: The casual 'counter-style' sister to the main Kikunoi ryotei. Led by Yoshihiro Murata's philosophy.
Best Dishes: Seasonal Hassun. Sea Bream Sushi.
highlights: Offers a more lively and accessible atmosphere than the main branch, allowing interaction with the chefs.

name: Tenjimbashi Aoki
history: Chef Machiaki Aoki serves quiet, dignified kaiseki cuisine in a discreet location.
Best Dishes: Sea Eel and Egg Tofu. Seasonal Sashimi.
highlights: A favorite of locals for its understated elegance and flawless execution of dashi.

name: Sojiki Nakahigashi
history: Chef Hisao Nakahigashi (brother of Miyamaso's chef) creates 'grass-eating' cuisine, elevating vegetables and herbs.
Best Dishes: Mezashi (Dried Sardine) breakfast. Kamado-cooked Rice.
highlights: The climax of the meal is the rice, cooked in a traditional stove and served in three stages of doneness (Al dente to crispy).

name: Kodaiji Jugyuan
history: Located in a historic garden villa built in 1908. It was originally a private retreat for a shipping magnate.
Best Dishes: Kyoto Beef. Seasonal Kaiseki.
highlights: Offers one of the most spectacular garden views in Kyoto, overlooking the city from the Higashiyama hills.

name: Gion Matayoshi
history: Chef Kazuyoshi Matayoshi brings the spirit of 'Cha-kaiseki' (Tea ceremony cuisine) to Gion's Hanamikoji street.
Best Dishes: Hand-kneaded Soba. Hassun.
highlights: Known for the chef's friendly hospitality and the incorporation of Okinawan influences (his heritage).

name: Gion Maruyama
history: Another establishment by Yoshio Maruyama, distinct from the Kenninji branch, offering a quintessential Kyoto Ryotei experience.
Best Dishes: Charcoal grilled bamboo shoots. Hamo (Pike Conger).
highlights: Features private tatami rooms and a dedication to highlighting the changing seasons.

name: Ryō-shō
history: Chef Makoto Fujiwara blends classic technique with modern architectural aesthetics in Gion.
Best Dishes: Crab covered in its own roe. Tilefish.
highlights: The building is a modern architectural marvel designed by an architect, standing out in the traditional district.

name: Rùn
history: Led by Chef Hung Chi-Kwong in the St. Regis Hong Kong, known for refining traditional recipes.
Best Dishes: Deep-fried diced oyster. Barbecued Iberian Pork.
highlights: Designed like a contemporary tea pavilion, offering elegant interpretations of classic Cantonese dishes.

name: The Eight
history: The flagship Chinese restaurant of the Grand Lisboa Hotel. It is famous for its lavish interior featuring the number 8.
Best Dishes: Goldfish Dumpling (Dim Sum). Suckling Pig stuffed with Fried Rice.
highlights: Renowned for having one of the most creative dim sum menus in the world.

name: Octavium
history: A project by Chef Umberto Bombana, intended to be his 'private dining room' laboratory.
Best Dishes: Tagliolini with Truffle. Te Mana Lamb.
highlights: An intimate venue serving highly personal, ingredient-driven Italian cuisine.

name: L'Envol
history: Chef Olivier Elzer creates sophisticated French cuisine in the St. Regis, focusing on seasonal ingredients from France.
Best Dishes: Hokkaido Sea Urchin Box. Brittany Lobster.
highlights: Features an open kitchen and a dedicated cheese cave.

name: Wing Lei
history: Chef Chan Tak Kwong serves classic Cantonese in a dramatic room at the Wynn Macau.
Best Dishes: Tea-smoked Crispy Chicken. Steamed Cod with preserved olive.
highlights: Famous for its flying dragon sculpture made of 90,000 Swarovski crystals.

name: Lai Ching Heen
history: Formerly known as Yan Toh Heen. Located in the Regent Hotel, it is famous for its jade place settings.
Best Dishes: Golden Lobster with Spicy Salt. Wok-seared Kagoshima Wagyu.
highlights: Offers spectacular views of Victoria Harbour along with museum-quality jade decor.

name: Arbor
history: Chef Eric Räty combines French technique with Nordic and Japanese ingredients.
Best Dishes: Langoustine with Tomato and Candy. Soy Milk Ice Cream.
highlights: Known for its minimalist, pink-hued interior and light, sharp flavors.

name: Noi by Paulo Airaudo
history: Chef Paulo Airaudo brings his globally influenced Italian style to the Four Seasons Hong Kong.
Best Dishes: Tuna with Caviar. Cappelletti.
highlights: Features a playlist curated by the chef and pop-culture inspired decor.

name: Tin Lung Heen
history: Chef Paul Lau Ping Lui runs this restaurant on the 102nd floor of the Ritz-Carlton.
Best Dishes: Barbecued Iberian Pork with Honey. Double-boiled Chicken Soup with Fish Maw.
highlights: One of the highest restaurants in the world, offering sweeping views of the skyline.

name: Feng Wei Ju
history: Located in the StarWorld Hotel, specializing in spicy Hunan and Sichuan cuisines.
Best Dishes: Boiled Mandarin Fish in Chili Oil. Carp Fillet.
highlights: Considered the best place for spicy, authentic Hunanese flavors in Macau.

name: Alain Ducasse at Morpheus
history: Ducasse's outpost in the Zaha Hadid-designed Morpheus hotel. It focuses on the essential taste of ingredients.
Best Dishes: Mediterranean Gamberoni. Farm Hen with Truffle.
highlights: A stunning, futuristic dining room filled with glass and light.

name: Tate
history: Chef Vicky Lau creates 'Edible Stories', blending French technique with Chinese heritage.
Best Dishes: Ode to Tofu. Ode to Scallop.
highlights: The menu is structured as a series of 'Odes' to specific ingredients, plated with feminine elegance.

name: Ying Jee Club
history: Chef Siu Hin Chi is a master of Cantonese cooking, known for his lightness of touch.
Best Dishes: Crispy Salted Chicken. Pan-fried Crab Claw.
highlights: A refined, club-like atmosphere serving high-end business lunches and dinners.

name: Lung King Heen
history: The first Chinese restaurant in the world to be awarded 3 Michelin stars. Chef Chan Yan Tak is a legend.
Best Dishes: Baked Barbecued Pork Buns. Lobster and Scallop Dumpling.
highlights: Located in the Four Seasons, known for consistency and excellence in dim sum and seafood.

name: Bo Innovation
history: Alvin Leung (The Demon Chef) deconstructs Chinese food in his style known as 'X-treme Chinese'.
Best Dishes: Molecular Xiao Long Bao. Sex on the Beach (Charity dish).
highlights: A playful, sometimes shocking, menu that challenges traditional perceptions of Chinese food.

name: The Huaiyang Garden
history: Chef Zhou Xiaoyan, the 'Godfather of Huaiyang Cuisine', brings the delicate flavors of Yangzhou to The Londoner.
Best Dishes: Stewed Meatball with Crab Roe. Shredded Tofu Soup.
highlights: Showcases incredible knife skills, particularly in the tofu dishes.

name: Chef Tam's Seasons
history: Chef Tam Kwok Fung creates a menu based on the 24 solar terms of the traditional Chinese calendar.
Best Dishes: Double-boiled soups. Seasonal delicacies.
highlights: Focuses on the concept of 'tonic food' and seasonality in Chinese medicine and gastronomy.

name: Il Gallo d'Oro
history: Chef Benoît Sinthon uses ingredients from the island of Madeira to create vibrant, colorful dishes.
Best Dishes: Scarlet Shrimp. Madeira Banana dessert.
highlights: The first restaurant in Madeira to receive 2 Michelin stars, located in the Cliff Bay Hotel.

name: Casa de Chá da Boa Nova
history: Located in a national monument designed by architect Álvaro Siza Vieira. Chef Rui Paula leads the kitchen.
Best Dishes: Squid with Fennel. Matosinhos Fish.
highlights: Dining literally on the rocks above the Atlantic Ocean, harmonizing architecture and gastronomy.

name: Antiqvvm
history: Chef Vitor Matos cooks in the gardens of the Crystal Palace, blending history with modern flavors.
Best Dishes: Beetroot and Foie Gras. Codfish variation.
highlights: Offers one of the most romantic views of the Douro River in Porto.

name: The Yeatman
history: Ricardo Costa's restaurant focuses on the harmony between food and the immense wine collection of the hotel.
Best Dishes: Suckling Pig. Scarlet Shrimp.
highlights: Offers the definitive panoramic view of the historic center of Porto.

name: Vila Joya
history: Chef Dieter Koschina has held 2 stars for over two decades, putting the Algarve on the culinary map.
Best Dishes: Guinea Fowl with Truffle. Algarve Seafood.
highlights: A boutique hotel restaurant located directly on the cliffs overlooking the sea.

name: Ocean
history: Austrian Chef Hans Neuner explores the history of Portuguese maritime discoveries through food.
Best Dishes: The 'Route to India' Menu. Violet Prawns.
highlights: The dining room offers a seamless view of the Atlantic, matching the oceanic theme of the menu.

name: Alma
history: Henrique Sá Pessoa's flagship in Chiado, focusing on Portuguese taste and Asian influences.
Best Dishes: Confited Suckling Pig. Salted Cod with Coriander.
highlights: Housed in an 18th-century warehouse for a sophisticated, moody atmosphere.

name: Belcanto
history: José Avillez reinvented this historic restaurant (open since 1958) to tell the story of Portuguese cuisine.
Best Dishes: The Garden of the Goose that laid the Golden Eggs. Dip in the Sea (Sea Bass).
highlights: The most famous fine dining restaurant in Portugal, blending history, theater, and flavor.

name: ION Harbour by Simon Rogan
history: British Chef Simon Rogan took over this rooftop venue, bringing his farm-to-table philosophy to Malta.
Best Dishes: Truffle Pudding. Local Maltese Prawns.
highlights: Offers spectacular views of the Grand Harbour from the rooftop of the Iniala Harbour House.

name: Chapter One by Mickael Viljanen
history: Chef Mickael Viljanen took over the iconic Chapter One, transforming it into a world-class destination.
Best Dishes: Lobster with Cocoa Butter. Foie Gras with Walnut.
highlights: Located in the basement of the Dublin Writers Museum, serving technically flawless cuisine.

name: The Glenturret Lalique
history: Mark Donald cooks inside Scotland's oldest working whisky distillery.
Best Dishes: Tattie Scone. Highland Wagyu.
highlights: A unique collaboration between Lalique crystal and whisky heritage, featuring world-class food.

name: hide and fox
history: Chef Allister Barsby and manager Alice Bussi run this intimate restaurant in a small village shop.
Best Dishes: Lamb with Anchovy. Seasonal Fruit Soufflé.
highlights: A hidden gem proving that exceptional fine dining can exist in quiet, rural locations.

name: Humble Chicken
history: Angelo Sato's counter restaurant evolved from a yakitori bar into a sophisticated 'Combat' tasting menu.
Best Dishes: Mussel Citrus. Chicken Liver Pâté.
highlights: A lively, jazz-filled Soho counter where the chef combines European training with Japanese roots.

name: dede
history: Chef Ahmet Dede fuses his Turkish heritage with the hyper-local produce of West Cork.
Best Dishes: Spiced Lobster. Manti Dumplings.
highlights: A relaxed, joyous atmosphere where Turkish spices meet the best Irish seafood.

name: Trivet
history: Jonny Lake (Chef) and Isa Bal (Sommelier), both Fat Duck alumni, focus on the interplay of food and wine.
Best Dishes: Hokkaido Potato with Roe. Drunken Lobster.
highlights: A restaurant designed around the wine list, offering a relaxed and unpretentious experience.

name: Da Terra
history: Rafael Cagali blends his Brazilian heritage with Italian roots in the historic Bethnal Green Town Hall.
Best Dishes: Moqueca (Brazilian Fish Stew) interpretation. Pork belly.
highlights: A blind tasting menu served in a grand Edwardian room.

name: Liath
history: Damien Grey runs this tiny restaurant in a market in suburban Dublin. 'Liath' means Grey in Irish.
Best Dishes: Five Tastes Menu (Sweet, Sour, Salty, Bitter, Umami).
highlights: An intimate, personal experience where the chef explains the philosophy of flavor to every guest.

name: Midsummer House
history: Daniel Clifford has maintained 2 stars here for nearly 20 years in a Victorian villa on the River Cam.
Best Dishes: Scallop with Truffle and Apple. Celeriac baked on open fire.
highlights: A Cambridge institution known for bold flavors and impeccable consistency.

name: Hand and Flowers
history: Tom Kerridge's pub is the first and only pub in the UK to hold 2 Michelin stars.
Best Dishes: Essex Lamb Bun. The Hand and Flowers Chips.
highlights: Refined, robust cooking served in a cozy, unpretentious traditional pub setting.

name: Gymkhana
history: Inspired by the colonial gymkhana clubs of India. It was the first Indian restaurant to win 2 stars in London.
Best Dishes: Muntjac Biryani. Kid Goat Methi Keema.
highlights: Famous for its rich, spicy flavors and club-like decor with dark wood and leather.

name: Gion Matsuri
history: Originating in 869 as a religious ceremony to appease the gods during an epidemic, it is one of Japan's most famous festivals.
highlights: The grand procession of Yamaboko Junko, featuring massive, elaborate floats adorned with tapestries, moving through the streets.

name: Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras
history: Began in 1978 as a protest march for LGBTQ+ rights, evolving into one of the world's largest pride parades.
highlights: A spectacular night parade with vibrant floats, costumes, and satire, celebrating diversity and equality.

name: Songkran Festival
history: Traditional Thai New Year celebration, historically involving gentle water pouring for purification and respect.
highlights: Massive public water fights using cannons and buckets across major city streets like Khao San Road.

name: Saint Patrick's Festival
history: A cultural and religious celebration of the patron saint of Ireland, dating back to the 17th century.
highlights: A grand parade featuring marching bands, theatrical troupes, and everything turning green to celebrate Irish heritage.

name: Montreux Jazz Festival
history: Founded in 1967, it is the second-largest jazz festival in the world, held on the shoreline of Lake Geneva.
highlights: World-class performances ranging from jazz and blues to rock and pop in an idyllic lakeside setting.

name: Mevlana Festival
history: Commemorates the death of the Sufi poet Rumi (Mevlana), celebrating his union with the divine.
highlights: The mesmerizing Whirling Dervishes ceremony (Sema), representing a mystical journey of spiritual ascent.

name: Semana Santa
history: Holy Week processions dating back to the 16th century, organized by religious brotherhoods.
highlights: Solemn processions of elaborate 'pasos' (floats) carrying lifelike wooden sculptures of biblical scenes, accompanied by brass bands.

name: Cannes Film Festival
history: Founded in 1946, it is the most prestigious film festival in the world, previewing new films of all genres.
highlights: The red carpet arrivals of global movie stars and the awarding of the Palme d'Or.

name: Edinburgh Festival Fringe
history: Established in 1947 as an alternative to the official International Festival, now the world's largest arts festival.
highlights: Thousands of shows including comedy, theater, and street performances taking over the entire city.

name: Rio Carnival
history: Dating back to 1723, it is the world's biggest carnival, rooted in Portuguese traditions mixed with African rhythms.
highlights: The Sambadrome parade featuring Samba schools with colossal floats and thousands of dancers in flamboyant costumes.

name: Burning Man
history: An experiment in community and art that began in 1986, creating a temporary metropolis in the desert.
highlights: The burning of a large wooden effigy ('The Man') and massive, interactive art installations in a dust-storm environment.

name: Holi Festival
history: Ancient Hindu festival of colors, celebrating the victory of good over evil and the arrival of spring.
highlights: Crowds throwing vibrant colored powders and water at each other in the streets, specifically in the birthplace of Lord Krishna.

name: Oktoberfest
history: Began in 1810 to celebrate the marriage of Crown Prince Ludwig, evolving into the world's largest beer festival.
highlights: Drinking beer by the liter in massive tents, traditional Bavarian music, lederhosen, and pretzels.

name: Mardi Gras New Orleans
history: French for 'Fat Tuesday', reflecting the practice of the last night of eating rich foods before the ritual fasting of Lent.
highlights: Parades organized by 'Krewes' throwing beads and doubloons to crowds on Bourbon Street and St. Charles Avenue.

name: Il Palio
history: A medieval horse race held twice a year in the city's central square, dating back to the 17th century.
highlights: Ten horses representing city wards (contrade) racing around the Piazza del Campo amidst fierce local rivalries.

name: Dia De Los Muertos
history: A Mexican holiday where families welcome back the souls of their deceased relatives for a brief reunion.
highlights: Graveyards decorated with marigolds and candles, sand tapestries, and skeleton-themed parades (Comparsas).

name: Harbin Ice and Snow Festival
history: Established in 1963, it showcases the world's biggest ice sculptures, utilizing ice from the Songhua River.
highlights: A city of massive ice buildings and sculptures illuminated with colorful LED lights at night.

name: La Tomatina
history: Started accidentally in 1945 during a parade dispute, now the 'World's Biggest Food Fight'.
highlights: Thousands of participants throwing over-ripe tomatoes at each other for one hour until the streets run red.

name: Glastonbury Festival
history: A five-day festival of contemporary performing arts that began in 1970, influenced by hippie culture.
highlights: Headline performances on the Pyramid Stage and a vast array of alternative arts in the Green Fields.

name: Venice International Film Festival
history: Founded in 1932, it is the oldest film festival in the world and part of the Venice Biennale.
highlights: Screenings at the historic Palazzo del Cinema on the Lido and the Golden Lion awards.

name: Berlin International Film Festival
history: Also known as the Berlinale, founded in 1951, it is one of the 'Big Three' film festivals alongside Venice and Cannes.
highlights: Public screenings of hundreds of films and the awarding of the Golden and Silver Bears.

name: Sundance Film Festival
history: The largest independent film festival in the US, championed by Robert Redford to promote independent storytellers.
highlights: Premieres of groundbreaking independent films in a snowy mountain resort setting.

name: Toronto International Film Festival
history: Founded in 1976, TIFF is widely considered the most influential film festival after Cannes for Oscar buzz.
highlights: People's Choice Award and red carpet premieres in the heart of Toronto's Entertainment District.

name: Running of the Bulls
history: Part of the Festival of San Fermín, immortalized by Ernest Hemingway in 'The Sun Also Rises'.
highlights: Daredevils running ahead of a group of bulls through the narrow streets of the old quarter.

name: Carnevale di Venezia
history: Famous for its distinctive masks, allowing citizens to hide their identity and social status during celebrations.
