Exploring the Allegheny National Forest.
Viewing the confluence at Point State Park.

name: Orinoco River
overview: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers in South America, flowing primarily through Venezuela. Its delta is vast and rich in wildlife.
highlights:
Boat expeditions in the Orinoco Delta.
Spotting macaws, river dolphins, and howler monkeys.
Visiting Ciudad Bolívar.

name: Orange River
overview: The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa. It rises in the Drakensberg mountains and flows west to the Atlantic Ocean, forming part of the border with Namibia.
highlights:
Canoeing through the Richtersveld desert landscape.
Visiting Augrabies Falls.
Exploring the diamond-rich river mouth area.

name: Tigris River
overview: The Tigris flows from Turkey through Iraq, running parallel to the Euphrates. It passes through the heart of Baghdad and was vital to ancient Mesopotamia.
highlights:
Views of the river in historic Hasankeyf (Turkey).
Walking the corniche in Baghdad.
Exploring the Mesopotamian marshes.

name: Kama River
overview: The Kama River is the longest left tributary of the Volga River. It is a major transport route in Russia, flowing near the Ural Mountains.
highlights:
River cruises stopping in Perm.
Visiting the Kungur Ice Cave nearby.
Enjoying the scenic forested banks.

name: Benue River
overview: The Benue River is the major tributary of the Niger River. It is navigable for much of its length and is an important transportation route in Nigeria and Cameroon.
highlights:
Wildlife viewing in Benue National Park.
River transport in Makurdi.
Seeing the confluence with the Niger at Lokoja.

name: White Nile River
overview: The White Nile is one of the two main tributaries of the Nile. It loses much of its water in the Sudd wetlands before joining the Blue Nile in Khartoum.
highlights:
Boat safaris in Murchison Falls National Park (Uganda).
Viewing the source at Lake Victoria.
Navigating the Sudd swamp.

name: Blue Nile River
overview: The Blue Nile originates at Lake Tana in Ethiopia and provides the majority of the water for the main Nile River. It is known for its dramatic gorge.
highlights:
Visiting the Blue Nile Falls (Tis Abay).
Seeing the source at Lake Tana.
Viewing the confluence with the White Nile in Khartoum.

name: Limpopo River
overview: The Limpopo River forms a large arc, separating South Africa from Botswana and Zimbabwe. It is often described as the 'grey-green, greasy Limpopo'.
highlights:
Safari viewing in Mapungubwe National Park.
Spotting crocodiles and hippos.
Exploring the rugged bushveld terrain.

name: Senegal River
overview: The Senegal River forms the border between Senegal and Mauritania. It played a significant role in West African history and the trans-Saharan trade.
highlights:
Visiting the colonial city of Saint-Louis at the mouth.
Birdwatching in the Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary.
River cruises on the Bou El Mogdad.

name: Lualaba River
overview: The Lualaba River is the greatest headstream of the Congo River by volume. It flows entirely within the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
highlights:
Viewing the Boyoma Falls (Stanley Falls).
River fishing expeditions.
Seeing the dense equatorial rainforest.

name: Okavango River
overview: The Okavango River is unique because it does not flow into the sea. Instead, it empties into the Kalahari Desert, creating the massive Okavango Delta.
highlights:
Mokoro (dugout canoe) trips in the Delta.
World-class wildlife safaris (Big Five).
Birdwatching in the wetlands.

name: Uruguay River
overview: The Uruguay River forms the border between Uruguay and Argentina. It flows south to join the Paraná River at the Rio de la Plata.
highlights:
Visiting the Moconá Falls (longitudinal waterfall).
Relaxing at thermal springs in Salto and Paysandú.
Exploring the colonial town of Colonia del Sacramento nearby.

name: Columbia River
overview: The Columbia River is the largest river in the Pacific Northwest region of North America. It is known for its strong flow and deep gorge.
highlights:
Windsurfing in the Columbia River Gorge.
Viewing the Multnomah Falls nearby.
Visiting the Astoria-Megler Bridge near the ocean.

name: Yellowstone River
overview: The Yellowstone River is a tributary of the Missouri River. It is famous for flowing through Yellowstone National Park and remaining undammed.
highlights:
Viewing the Lower Falls in the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.
Fly fishing for trout.
Wildlife watching in the Lamar Valley.

name: Platte River
overview: The Platte River is a major river in Nebraska. Historically, it was a vital route for westward expansion along the Oregon and Mormon Trails.
highlights:
Witnessing the sandhill crane migration.
Airboat tours near Fremont or Omaha.
Visiting historic Fort Kearny.

name: Fraser River
overview: The Fraser River is the longest river within British Columbia. It flows through spectacular canyons before reaching the Strait of Georgia near Vancouver.
highlights:
White water rafting in Hell's Gate.
Salmon fishing expeditions.
Walking the dikes in Richmond/Steveston.

name: Brazos River
overview: The Brazos River is the 11th-longest river in the United States and flows entirely within Texas. It played a major role in the state's history.
highlights:
Canoeing near the Possum Kingdom Lake.
Visiting Washington-on-the-Brazos historic site.
Viewing the suspension bridge in Waco.

name: Peace River
overview: The Peace River originates in the Rockies of British Columbia and flows into the Slave River in Alberta. It is a major waterway of the Canadian North.
highlights:
Jet boating near Peace River town.
Exploring the Peace-Athabasca Delta.
Fossil hunting in the river valley.

name: Slave River
overview: The Slave River connects Lake Athabasca to Great Slave Lake. It is famous among kayakers for its world-class rapids near Fort Smith.
highlights:
Whitewater kayaking on the Rapids of the Drowned.
Pelican watching at the rapids.
Visiting Fort Smith.

name: Assiniboine River
overview: The Assiniboine River flows through the prairies of Saskatchewan and Manitoba, joining the Red River at 'The Forks' in Winnipeg.
highlights:
Skating on the river trail in winter at The Forks.
Canoeing through Beaudry Provincial Park.
Visiting the Assiniboine Park in Winnipeg.

name: Rio Negro
overview: The Rio Negro is the largest left tributary of the Amazon and the largest blackwater river in the world. Its dark waters contrast sharply where they meet the Amazon.
highlights:
Seeing the 'Meeting of Waters' near Manaus.
Exploring the Anavilhanas Archipelago.
Jungle trekking in the Amazon basin.

name: Magdalena River
overview: The Magdalena River is the principal river of Colombia, flowing northward to the Caribbean Sea. It was the primary transport route into the Andean interior.
highlights:
Visiting the historic town of Mompox (UNESCO).
Exploring the Tatacoa Desert near the river.
Seeing the archaeological site of San Agustín near the source.

name: Tapajos River
overview: The Tapajós is a major tributary of the Amazon River. It is known for its clear, blue-green waters and white sand river beaches.
highlights:
Relaxing on the beaches of Alter do Chão (Caribbean of the Amazon).
Exploring the Tapajós National Forest.
Sunset boat tours from Santarém.

name: Xingu River
overview: The Xingu River is a major tributary of the Amazon in Brazil. It is culturally significant for the indigenous peoples living in the Xingu Indigenous Park.
highlights:
Sport fishing for Peacock Bass.
Eco-tourism in the Altamira region.
Learning about indigenous cultures in the upper basin.

name: Niagara River
overview: The Niagara River connects Lake Erie to Lake Ontario and forms the border between New York (USA) and Ontario (Canada). It is world-famous for the massive Niagara Falls.
highlights:
Viewing the Horseshoe Falls and American Falls.
Taking the Maid of the Mist boat tour.
Walking along the White Water Walk.

name: Iguazu River
overview: The Iguazu River is a tributary of the Paraná River. It is renowned for the Iguazu Falls, a massive system of waterfalls on the border of Argentina and Brazil.
highlights:
Walking the Devil's Throat (Garganta del Diablo) trail.
Taking a boat ride under the falls.
Exploring the surrounding subtropical rainforest.

name: Rhine River
overview: The Rhine is one of the major European rivers, famous for its scenic Middle Rhine Valley which is dotted with castles and vineyards. It is a vital waterway for trade and tourism.
highlights:
Cruising the UNESCO World Heritage Middle Rhine Valley.
Viewing the Lorelei Rock.
Visiting historic cities like Cologne and Strasbourg.

name: Seine River
overview: The Seine is the quintessential river of Paris, flowing through the heart of the city. Its banks are a UNESCO World Heritage site, lined with iconic landmarks.
highlights:
Bateaux Mouches boat tours in Paris.
Walking along the romantic riverbanks (Les Berges).
Viewing the Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame, and Louvre from the water.

name: Loire River
overview: The Loire is the longest river in France. The Loire Valley is world-famous for its magnificent Renaissance châteaux and wines.
highlights:
Visiting Château de Chambord and Château de Chenonceau.
Cycling the Loire à Vélo route.
Wine tasting in the river valley vineyards.

name: Rhone River
overview: The Rhône rises in the Swiss Alps and flows through southeastern France to the Mediterranean. It is known for its deep valley and historical cities like Avignon.
highlights:
Seeing the Pont d'Avignon and Pope's Palace.
River cruises through Provence.
Visiting the vineyards of Côtes du Rhône.

name: Tagus River
overview: The Tagus (Tejo) is the longest river in the Iberian Peninsula. It empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon, forming a massive estuary.
highlights:
Sailing in the Tagus Estuary near Lisbon.
Viewing the Belém Tower and Monument to the Discoveries.
Visiting the historic city of Toledo in Spain.

name: Thames River
overview: The Thames is the most famous river in England, flowing through London. It has been a hub of activity for trade, royalty, and culture for millennia.
highlights:
Tower Bridge and the Tower of London.
The London Eye and Southbank promenade.
Rowing regattas at Henley-on-Thames.

name: Elbe River
overview: The Elbe River flows from the Czech Republic through Germany to the North Sea. It connects major cultural hubs like Dresden and Hamburg.
highlights:
Exploring the Port of Hamburg.
Viewing the sandstone formations in Saxon Switzerland.
Visiting the historic city center of Dresden.

name: Oder River
overview: The Oder River forms a significant part of the border between Poland and Germany. It flows into the Baltic Sea and is important for Central European trade.
highlights:
River cruises in Wrocław among its many islands.
Exploring the Oder Delta nature reserves.
Visiting the port city of Szczecin.

name: Vistula River
overview: The Vistula is the longest and most important river in Poland, flowing through Kraków and Warsaw. It is deeply tied to Polish national identity.
highlights:
Walking the river boulevards in Warsaw.
Viewing Wawel Castle from the river in Kraków.
Visiting the historic town of Toruń.

name: Donets River
overview: The Siverskyi Donets is a major river in Eastern Ukraine and Southern Russia. It is known for the chalk mountains along its banks in the Sviatohirsk area.
highlights:
Visiting the Sviatohirsk Lavra cave monastery.
Kayaking and camping in the river valley.
Viewing the white chalk cliffs.

name: Po River
overview: The Po is Italy's longest river, flowing eastward across northern Italy. Its vast fertile valley is the agricultural heartland of the country.
highlights:
River cruising in the Po Delta Biosphere Reserve.
Visiting Turin and Cremona.
Exploring the wetlands and birdwatching near the Adriatic.

name: Arno River
overview: The Arno is the river of Florence and Pisa. It is famous for the historic bridges that cross it and the Renaissance art and architecture on its banks.
highlights:
Crossing the Ponte Vecchio in Florence.
Watching the sunset over the river from Piazzale Michelangelo.
Walking the Lungarno promenades.

name: Guadalquivir River
overview: The Guadalquivir is the great river of Seville and Andalusia. It is the only major navigable river in Spain and is central to the region's history.
highlights:
Boat tours in Seville seeing the Torre del Oro.
Visiting the Doñana National Park at the delta.
Exploring the historic city of Córdoba.

name: Daugava River
overview: The Daugava (Western Dvina) flows into the Baltic Sea at Riga. It is a scenic river that has been a trade route since the Viking age.
highlights:
Views of Old Riga from the river banks.
Exploring the Daugavas Loki Nature Park.
River cruises in the Latvian countryside.

name: Pripyat River
overview: The Pripyat River is infamous for flowing through the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone. It passes the ghost city of Pripyat and serves as a site for dark tourism.
highlights:
Guided tours of the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone.
Viewing the sunken boats near the Pripyat port.
Observing nature reclaiming the abandoned riverbanks.

name: Morava River
overview: The Morava River forms part of the border between the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Austria. It flows into the Danube near Bratislava.
highlights:
Canoeing through the riparian forests.
Visiting Devin Castle at the confluence with the Danube.
Cycling along the EuroVelo trails.

name: Rubicon River
overview: The Rubicon is a shallow river in northeastern Italy. It is historically famous because Julius Caesar's crossing of it in 49 BC led to civil war.
highlights:
Visiting the bridge in Savignano sul Rubicone.
Reflecting on the historical phrase 'Crossing the Rubicon'.
Exploring the nearby Adriatic coast.

name: Neva River
overview: The Neva River flows from Lake Ladoga through Saint Petersburg to the Gulf of Finland. It is central to the city's 'Venice of the North' character.
highlights:
Watching the drawbridges open at night during White Nights.
Boat tours through the city's canals.
Viewing the Winter Palace from the water.

name: Severnaya Dvina River
overview: The Severnaya Dvina flows north into the White Sea at Arkhangelsk. It is a major waterway of the Russian North, known for historic wooden architecture.
highlights:
River cruises on the 'Gogol' paddle steamer.
Visiting the Malye Korely wooden architecture museum.
Exploring the historic port of Arkhangelsk.

name: River Clyde
overview: The River Clyde flows through Glasgow, Scotland. Once a powerhouse of shipbuilding, it is now a center for culture and waterfront regeneration.
highlights:
Visiting the Riverside Museum and Tall Ship Glenlee.
Walking the Clyde Walkway.
Seeing the Finnieston Crane and Clyde Arc bridge.

name: Moskva River
overview: The Moskva River flows through the heart of Moscow. Its embankments offer the best views of the Kremlin and the city's major landmarks.
highlights:
Radisson river cruises (year-round icebreakers).
Views of the Kremlin, Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, and Gorky Park.
Walking along the Zaryadye Park embankment.

name: Sogne River
overview: Referring to the river systems (Sogndalselvi) flowing into the Sognefjord. While the fjord is marine, the inflowing rivers offer spectacular salmon fishing and scenery.
highlights:
Salmon fishing in the clear waters.
Hiking along the river banks in Sogndal.
Connecting to the majestic Sognefjord tours.

name: Geiranger River
overview: The Geirangelva flows through the village of Geiranger into the famous UNESCO-listed Geirangerfjord. It features cascading waterfalls and rapids.
highlights:
Walking the Waterfall Walk (Storfossen).
Kayaking near the river mouth in the fjord.
Viewing the Seven Sisters waterfall nearby.

name: Tiber River
overview: The Tiber is the main river of Rome, rising in the Apennines. Legend says Rome was founded on its banks, and it remains an iconic part of the cityscape.
highlights:
Views of Castel Sant'Angelo and St. Peter's Basilica.
Walking on the Isola Tiberina.
Summer festivals along the river banks (Lungo il Tevere).

name: Vltava River
overview: The Vltava is the longest river in the Czech Republic and the soul of Prague. It flows under the famous Charles Bridge and offers stunning city panoramas.
highlights:
Crossing the Charles Bridge.
Pedal boating near Slovansky Island.
Cruising to see Prague Castle from the water.

name: Spree River
overview: The Spree River flows through Berlin, winding past major historical sights and Museum Island. It serves as a recreational hub for the city.
highlights:
Boat tours through the government district.
Relaxing at beach bars along the banks.
Exploring Museum Island (UNESCO).

name: Amstel River
overview: The Amstel is the river from which Amsterdam gets its name. It is iconic for the Skinny Bridge (Magere Brug) and the canal ring connected to it.
highlights:
Cruising the canals and the river.
Viewing the Magere Brug.
Watching the rowing events and historic houseboats.

name: Douro River
overview: The Douro flows from Spain across Portugal to Porto. The Douro Valley is the oldest demarcated wine region in the world, famous for Port wine.
highlights:
River cruises through the terraced vineyards.
Wine tasting in the Quintas.
Viewing the Dom Luís I Bridge in Porto.

name: Sava River
overview: The Sava is a major tributary of the Danube, meeting it in Belgrade. It flows through three capital cities: Ljubljana, Zagreb, and Belgrade.
highlights:
Visiting the confluence (Ušće) in Belgrade.
Rafting in the upper reaches in Slovenia.
Walking the river banks in Zagreb.

name: Drava River
overview: The Drava is a major river in Central Europe and a tributary of the Danube. It connects the Alps to the Pannonian Plain.
highlights:
Cycling the Drava Cycle Path.
Exploring the Kopački Rit Nature Park near the confluence.
Visiting the city of Osijek.

name: Weser River
overview: The Weser flows northward through Germany to the North Sea. It passes through Bremen and is associated with the fairy tale of the Pied Piper of Hamelin.
highlights:
Visiting the historic city of Bremen.
Touring the town of Hamelin (Hameln).
Seeing the Porta Westfalica gorge.

name: River Shannon
overview: The River Shannon is the longest river in Ireland. It divides the west of Ireland from the east and south and is a major destination for pleasure boating.
highlights:
Cruising on a houseboat rental.
Visiting the monastic site of Clonmacnoise.
Exploring scenic Lough Derg.

name: Singapore River
overview: The Singapore River flows through the Central Business District. Once the lifeline of trade, it is now a bustling tourism hub for dining and nightlife.
highlights:
Bumboat river cruises.
Dining at Clarke Quay and Boat Quay.
Photographing the Merlion and Marina Bay Sands.

name: Saigon River
overview: The Saigon River winds through Ho Chi Minh City. It serves as the city's main water supply and a key commercial and aesthetic feature.
highlights:
Dinner cruises seeing the city skyline.
Visiting the Bach Dang Wharf.
Exploring the Cu Chi Tunnels via boat.

name: Pearl River
overview: The Pearl River is an extensive river system in southern China, flowing through Guangzhou to the South China Sea between Hong Kong and Macau.
highlights:
Night cruises in Guangzhou viewing the Canton Tower.
Exploring the vibrant Pearl River Delta.
Views from the Hong Kong waterfront.

name: Kamo River
overview: The Kamo River runs through Kyoto. It is a favorite spot for locals and tourists to walk, picnic, and enjoy the seasonal beauty.
highlights:
Dining on 'Yuka' riverside terraces in Pontocho in summer.
Walking the river banks during cherry blossom season.
Crossing the stepping stones at the delta.

name: Sumida River
overview: The Sumida River flows through Tokyo and is famous for its bridges and the annual fireworks festival. It offers a classic view of the Tokyo Skytree.
highlights:
Taking the water bus (suijō-bus) to Asakusa or Odaiba.
Viewing the Tokyo Skytree from Sumida Park.
Attending the Sumidagawa Fireworks Festival.

name: Chao Phraya River
overview: The Chao Phraya is the major river of Thailand, flowing through Bangkok. It is the lifeblood of the city, bustling with ferries, barges, and cruise ships.
highlights:
Taking the express boat to Wat Arun.
Dinner cruises passing the Grand Palace.
Exploring the riverside Asiatique night market.

name: Red River
overview: The Red River (Hong River) flows from China through northern Vietnam and Hanoi to the Gulf of Tonkin. Its reddish-brown silt gives it its name.
highlights:
Walking across the historic Long Bien Bridge in Hanoi.
Visiting traditional pottery villages like Bat Trang.
Exploring the Red River Delta.

name: Godavari River
overview: The Godavari is India's second-longest river, known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South). It is sacred to Hindus.
highlights:
Boat rides in the scenic Papi Hills (Papikondalu).
Visiting the holy city of Nashik (Kumbh Mela site).
Seeing the vast delta in Andhra Pradesh.

name: Krishna River
overview: The Krishna River is a major river in south India. It flows east to the Bay of Bengal and is a key source of irrigation and power.
highlights:
Visiting the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam and Ethipothala Falls.
Seeing the Durga Temple in Vijayawada.
Exploring the Srisailam sanctuary.

name: Narmada River
overview: The Narmada River flows westward through central India. It is one of the holiest rivers, believed to wash away sins by merely looking at it.
highlights:
Marble Rocks boat ride in Bhedaghat.
Visiting the Dhuandhar Falls.
Seeing the massive Statue of Unity (world's tallest).

name: Sutlej River
overview: The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
highlights:
Views of the Kinnaur Valley in Himachal Pradesh.
Visiting the Bhakra Dam.
Seeing the river at the India-Pakistan border.

name: Jhelum River
overview: The Jhelum flows through the Vale of Kashmir. It is famous for the houseboats on its connecting lakes and its winding path through Srinagar.
highlights:
Houseboat stays in Srinagar.
River rafting in Pahalgam.
Crossing the historic bridges in Srinagar.

name: Chenab River
overview: The Chenab River is a major river of India and Pakistan. It is formed by the confluence of two rivers in the upper Himalayas.
highlights:
Viewing the Chenab Bridge (world's highest rail bridge).
Scenic drives along the river in Jammu region.
Historical romances of Punjab folklore associated with the river.

name: Songhua River
overview: The Songhua River flows through Northeast China and Harbin. It is famous for freezing over in winter, hosting the Ice and Snow Festival.
highlights:
Visiting the Harbin Ice and Snow Festival.
Strolling along Stalin Park on the riverbank.
Winter swimming and ice activities.

name: Liao River
overview: The Liao River is a principal river in southern Northeast China. It flows into the Bohai Sea and has been a site of ancient civilization.
highlights:
Birdwatching in the Liaohe Delta wetlands.
Seeing the Red Beach in Panjin.
Exploring the history of Liaoning province.

name: Ussuri River
overview: The Ussuri River forms part of the border between Russia and China. It is known for the Sino-Soviet border conflict and its pristine nature.
highlights:
Nature tours in the Ussurisky Nature Reserve.
Viewing the border from river banks.
Tiger spotting expeditions in the region.

name: Kura River
overview: The Kura River flows through the Caucasus Mountains and the capital city of Tbilisi, Georgia, before reaching the Caspian Sea.
highlights:
Boat tours in Tbilisi passing the Peace Bridge.
Views of the Metekhi Church on the cliff.
Exploring the Mtkvari valley cave towns like Uplistsikhe.

name: Kamchatka River
overview: The Kamchatka River flows through the Kamchatka Peninsula in Far East Russia. It is surrounded by volcanoes and is famous for salmon runs.
highlights:
Fishing for massive Pacific salmon.
Views of the Klyuchevskaya Sopka volcano.
Experiencing the remote wilderness of Kamchatka.

name: Shinano River
overview: The Shinano River is the longest river in Japan. It flows from the Japanese Alps to the Sea of Japan at Niigata.
highlights:
Viewing the Nagaoka Fireworks Festival (one of Japan's best).
River cruising in Niigata City.
Visiting the rice terraces in the basin.

name: Tone River
overview: The Tone River represents the largest drainage area in Japan. It is nicknamed 'Bando Taro' and flows through the Kanto plain north of Tokyo.
highlights:
Rafting in the upper reaches at Minakami.
Visiting the Suigo Sawara historic district (Little Edo).
Cycling along the extensive river paths.

name: Jordan River
overview: The Jordan River flows into the Dead Sea and holds immense religious significance as the site of the baptism of Jesus.
highlights:
Visiting the Baptism Site (Qasr el Yahud / Bethany Beyond the Jordan).
Kayaking in the Upper Jordan.
Floating in the nearby Dead Sea.

name: Tarim River
overview: The Tarim River is the principal river of the Xinjiang region. It flows into the Taklamakan Desert and ends in a salt lake system.
highlights:
Seeing the desert poplar (Populus euphratica) forests in autumn.
Exploring the edge of the Taklamakan Desert.
Road trips on the Tarim Desert Highway.

name: Han River, China
overview: The Han River (Hanjiang) is a major tributary of the Yangtze. It joins the Yangtze at Wuhan, dividing the city into three parts.
highlights:
River views at the confluence in Wuhan.
Visiting the ancient city of Xiangyang.
Cruising past the Yellow Crane Tower.

name: Han River, Korea
overview: The Han River flows through the center of Seoul. It is a major recreational area for citizens and a symbol of South Korea's economic growth.
highlights:
Picnicking at Yeouido Hangang Park.
Cycling along the dedicated river paths.
Watching the Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain.

name: Nakdong River
overview: The Nakdong is the longest river in South Korea, flowing south to the Korea Strait near Busan. It is historically significant and rich in migratory birds.
highlights:
Birdwatching at the Eulsukdo Migratory Bird Park.
Cycling the Cross-Country Cycling Road.
Visiting the historic Andong Hahoe Village nearby.

name: Taedong River
overview: The Taedong River flows through Pyongyang, the capital of North Korea. It features major landmarks like the Juche Tower on its banks.
highlights:
Views of the Juche Tower and Kim Il-sung Square.
River cruises in Pyongyang.
Seeing the Taedongmun Gate.

name: Yalu River
overview: The Yalu River (Amnok) forms the border between North Korea and China. It is historically significant for the Korean War.
highlights:
Walking on the 'Broken Bridge' in Dandong.
Boat tours along the border.
Viewing the Great Wall's eastern end at Hushan.

name: Geum River
overview: The Geum River flows through central South Korea into the Yellow Sea. It was the center of the ancient Baekje culture.
highlights:
Visiting Gongsanseong Fortress in Gongju.
Exploring the Busosanseong Fortress in Buyeo.
Walking the Geumgang Estuary bird sanctuary.

name: Yeongsan River
overview: The Yeongsan River is one of the four major rivers in South Korea, flowing through the southwest Honam region.
highlights:
Taking the Hwangpo sailboat experience in Naju.
Cycling along the Yeongsan River path.
Visiting the Mokpo modernization district near the mouth.

name: Chongchon River
overview: The Chongchon River flows through North Korea. It is historically notable as the site of major battles during the Korean War.
highlights:
Viewing the landscapes of the Myohyangsan mountains near the source.
Historical tours related to Korean War sites (if accessible).
 scenic river valleys.

name: Tumen River
overview: The Tumen River forms the border between North Korea, China, and Russia. It allows a unique view of three countries at once near the mouth.
highlights:
Visiting the Fangchuan scenic area (Tri-border view).
Observing the border bridge.
Experiencing the Korean-Chinese culture in Yanbian.

name: Koshi River
overview: The Koshi River is a major trans-boundary river. It is known for its high sediment load and rafting opportunities in Nepal.
highlights:
White water rafting in Nepal.
Visiting the Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve.
Fishing for Mahseer.

name: Ghaghara River
overview: The Ghaghara is a major tributary of the Ganges. It flows from Tibet through the Himalayas into the plains of India.
highlights:
Visiting the holy city of Ayodhya on the banks of its tributary (Saryu).
Birdwatching in the river basins.
Pilgrimage sites along the banks.

name: Teesta River
overview: The Teesta River flows through the Indian state of Sikkim and West Bengal to Bangladesh. Its turquoise waters are famous for rafting.
highlights:
River rafting near Kalimpong and Darjeeling.
Views of the river meeting the mountains.
Visiting the Coronation Bridge.

name: Yodo River
overview: The Yodo River flows from Lake Biwa to Osaka Bay. It passes through Uji and Osaka, playing a key role in the region's history.
highlights:
Hanami (cherry blossom viewing) at Sewaritei.
River cruises in Osaka (Aqua Liner).
Visiting Byodoin Temple in Uji near the river.

name: Kitakami River
overview: The Kitakami River flows through the Tohoku region. It is known for its tens of thousands of cherry trees planted along the banks at Tenshochi.
highlights:
Visiting Tenshochi Park for cherry blossoms.
River boat rides (Geibi Gorge tributary).
Exploring the Hiraizumi UNESCO sites nearby.

name: Jialing River
overview: The Jialing River is a major tributary of the Yangtze. It meets the Yangtze at Chongqing, creating a spectacular peninsula city landscape.
highlights:
Night views of the confluence at Chaotianmen.
Visiting the ancient fishing fortress of Diaoyu.
Exploring Langzhong Ancient City.

name: Nan River
overview: The Nan River is one of the two main tributaries of the Chao Phraya. It flows through the peaceful province of Nan in northern Thailand.
highlights:
Long-boat racing festivals in Nan province.
Visiting Wat Phumin.
Relaxing by the quiet riverside in Phitsanulok.

name: Pasak River
overview: The Pasak River flows through central Thailand. It is known for the Pasak Jolasid Dam, a popular stop for the scenic 'floating train'.
highlights:
Riding the 'Floating Train' across the reservoir.
Visiting sunflower fields in Lopburi.
Picnicking at the dam.

name: Melaka River
overview: The Melaka River flows through the historic city of Malacca. Once a trade route, it is now famous for its river cruise and street art.
highlights:
Taking the Melaka River Cruise.
Viewing the murals on riverside buildings.
Walking along the Jonker Walk nearby.

name: Perfume River
overview: The Perfume River (Huong River) flows through Hue, the former imperial capital. It is named after the scent of flowers that fall into the water in autumn.
highlights:
Dragon boat trips to Thien Mu Pagoda.
Listening to Hue folk songs on the river at night.
Visiting the Imperial City.

name: St. Johns River
overview: The St. Johns River is the longest river in Florida. It is unique for flowing north and is a haven for manatees and alligators.
highlights:
Airboat tours to see alligators.
Kayaking in the springs (e.g., Blue Spring).
Visiting Jacksonville's Riverwalk.

name: Hudson River
overview: The Hudson River flows from the Adirondacks to New York City. It is a cultural icon, separating Manhattan from New Jersey.
highlights:
Walking the High Line with river views.
Cruising past the Statue of Liberty.
Visiting the scenic Hudson Valley towns.

name: Potomac River
overview: The Potomac River flows through Washington D.C., and is known as the 'Nation's River'. It is lined with monuments and cherry blossoms.
highlights:
Viewing the monuments from a river cruise.
Walking along the Tidal Basin during Cherry Blossom Festival.
Visiting Great Falls Park.

name: Delaware River
overview: The Delaware River forms the border between Pennsylvania and New Jersey. It is famous for Washington's historic crossing in 1776.
highlights:
Tubing and canoeing in the Delaware Water Gap.
Visiting Washington Crossing Historic Park.
Exploring the Philadelphia waterfront (Penn's Landing).

name: Chicago River
overview: The Chicago River runs through downtown Chicago. It is an engineering marvel (flow reversed) and famous for being dyed green on St. Patrick's Day.
highlights:
Architecture Foundation River Cruise.
Walking the Chicago Riverwalk.
Kayaking through the skyscrapers.

name: San Antonio River
overview: The San Antonio River is famous for the River Walk (Paseo del Rio), a network of walkways along the banks in downtown San Antonio.
highlights:
Strolling the River Walk lined with restaurants.
Taking a river barge tour.
Visiting the San Antonio Missions (UNESCO).

name: Charles River
overview: The Charles River flows between Boston and Cambridge. It is a hub for collegiate rowing and hosts the famous Head of the Charles Regatta.
highlights:
Watching the rowing crews from the bridges.
Walking the Esplanade.
Attending the 4th of July Pops concert.

name: Chattahoochee River
overview: The Chattahoochee River flows through Georgia, forming part of the border with Alabama. It provides recreation for the Atlanta metro area.
highlights:
Tubing ('Shooting the Hooch') in summer.
Hiking in the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area.
Fishing for trout in the tailwaters.

name: Yazoo River
overview: The Yazoo River is a tributary of the Mississippi River. It flows through the Mississippi Delta, a region rich in blues music history.
highlights:
Exploring the Mississippi Blues Trail.
Visiting historic Vicksburg.
Fishing in the river basin.

name: Minnesota River
overview: The Minnesota River is a tributary of the Mississippi, joining it near Minneapolis/St. Paul. It flows through a scenic valley carved by glacial waters.
highlights:
Visiting Fort Snelling at the confluence.
Hiking in the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge.
Kayaking the gentle currents.

name: Illinois River
overview: The Illinois River is a principal tributary of the Mississippi River. It connects the Great Lakes to the Mississippi via the canal system.
highlights:
Eagle watching at Starved Rock State Park.
Boating on Peoria Lake.
Exploring the historic river towns.

name: St. Croix River
overview: The St. Croix River forms part of the border between Wisconsin and Minnesota. It is a National Scenic Riverway known for its clean water and basalt cliffs.
highlights:
Canoeing and camping on the river islands.
Visiting the Dalles of the St. Croix at Taylors Falls.
Taking a paddlewheel boat tour.

name: Atchafalaya River
overview: The Atchafalaya River is a distributary of the Mississippi and Red Rivers. It flows through the largest swamp wilderness in the United States.
highlights:
Swamp tours in the Atchafalaya Basin.
Birdwatching for eagles and osprey.
Experiencing Cajun culture in the river towns.

name: Ouachita River
overview: The Ouachita River flows through Arkansas and Louisiana. It is known for its scenic beauty in the Ouachita Mountains and excellent fishing.
highlights:
Fishing for bass and crappie.
Boating near Hot Springs National Park.
Exploring the Felsenthal National Wildlife Refuge.

name: Willamette River
overview: The Willamette River flows through the Willamette Valley and Portland, Oregon. It is central to the region's agriculture (wine) and urban life.
highlights:
Walking the waterfront loops in Portland.
Visiting the Willamette Valley wine country.
Kayaking through downtown Portland.

name: Shenandoah River
overview: The Shenandoah River is immortalized in the song 'Take Me Home, Country Roads'. It flows through the beautiful Shenandoah Valley in Virginia.
highlights:
Canoeing and tubing in the clear waters.
Views of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
Visiting Harpers Ferry National Historical Park.

name: Cape Fear River
overview: The Cape Fear River flows into the Atlantic in North Carolina. It is associated with Wilmington's historic riverfront and nearby beaches.
highlights:
Strolling the Wilmington Riverwalk.
Touring the Battleship North Carolina.
Taking a riverboat cruise.

name: Brisbane River
overview: The Brisbane River winds through the city of Brisbane. It is the backdrop for the city's outdoor lifestyle and cultural precincts.
highlights:
Riding the CityCat ferries.
Visiting South Bank Parklands and the artificial beach.
Climbing the Story Bridge for river views.

name: Swan River
overview: The Swan River flows through Perth, Western Australia. Its wide waters are perfect for sailing and are home to the famous black swans.
highlights:
Picnicking at Kings Park overlooking the river.
Cruising to the Swan Valley vineyards.
Visiting Elizabeth Quay.

name: Shotover River
overview: The Shotover River near Queenstown is famous for its fast-flowing, shallow waters through narrow canyons. It is a global hub for adventure tourism.
highlights:
Taking a high-speed Shotover Jet boat ride.
White water rafting.
Gold panning in the historic riverbed.

name: Dart River
overview: The Dart River flows into Lake Wakatipu near Glenorchy. It offers stunning scenery used as filming locations for 'The Lord of the Rings'.
highlights:
Jet boating deep into the Mt. Aspiring National Park.
Funyak (inflatable canoe) tours.
Viewing the Isengard filming locations.

name: Waikato River
overview: The Waikato is New Zealand's longest river. It flows from Lake Taupo to the Tasman Sea, featuring the powerful Huka Falls.
highlights:
Viewing the thundering Huka Falls.
River cruising on the Maid of the Mist.
Kayaking to natural hot springs.

name: Sepik River
overview: The Sepik River is the longest river on the island of New Guinea. It is often compared to the Amazon for its serpentine shape and isolated tribal cultures.
highlights:
Cultural tours to see Spirit Houses (Haus Tambaran).
Buying unique tribal wood carvings.
Expeditions into the remote rainforest.

name: Flinders River
overview: The Flinders River is the longest river in Queensland. It flows through sparsely populated outback country to the Gulf of Carpentaria.
highlights:
Fishing for Barramundi.
Camping in the remote outback.
Fossil hunting in the Hughenden region.

name: Diamantina River
overview: The Diamantina River is a classic outback river in Australia. It flows towards Lake Eyre and is known for its 'Channel Country' braided channels.
highlights:
Visiting Birdsville and the famous Birdsville Hotel.
Seeing the river in flood (rare event).
Experiencing the vast starry skies of the outback.

name: Minami River
overview: The Minami River in Tokushima Prefecture is renowned for its clear waters and is a sanctuary for loggerhead sea turtles at its mouth.
highlights:
Kayaking in the crystal clear water.
Watching sea turtles at Ohama Beach (river mouth).
Camping along the scenic banks.

name: Colorado River (Argentina)
overview: The Colorado River in Argentina marks the northern boundary of Patagonia. It flows from the Andes to the Atlantic Ocean.
highlights:
Irrigated agriculture tours (fruit orchards).
Gateway to Patagonian travel.
Fishing and camping in the valley.

name: Rio Negro (Argentina)
overview: The Rio Negro is the most important river of the Patagonia region in Argentina. It flows through a fertile valley known for apple and pear production.
highlights:
Visiting the city of Viedma near the mouth.
Exploring the fruit orchards of the valley.
Water sports in the calm river waters.

name: Santa Cruz River
overview: The Santa Cruz River flows from the glacial lakes near El Calafate to the Atlantic. It carries the turquoise meltwater of the Patagonian glaciers.
highlights:
Visiting Los Glaciares National Park (source).
Exploring the estuary near Puerto Santa Cruz.
Tracing the route of Charles Darwin's expedition.

name: Tigre River
overview: Referring to the waterways of the Paraná Delta near the town of Tigre. It is a popular weekend getaway for Buenos Aires residents.
highlights:
Taking a 'lancha colectiva' (water taxi).
Staying in island cabins in the Delta.
Visiting the Puerto de Frutos market.

name: Nairobi River
overview: The Nairobi River flows through the Kenyan capital. Efforts are underway to clean and restore the river to create green spaces in the city.
highlights:
Visiting the Nairobi National Museum nearby.
Walking in Michuki Park (restored river area).
Understanding urban river conservation efforts.

name: Chobe River
overview: The Chobe River runs along the northern border of Chobe National Park. It attracts huge herds of elephants and buffalo during the dry season.
highlights:
Sunset boat safaris watching elephants swim.
Staying on a houseboat (Chobe Princess).
Birdwatching for African Fish Eagles.

name: Ubangi River
overview: The Ubangi River is the largest tributary of the Congo River. It forms the border between the Central African Republic and the DRC.
highlights:
River transport adventures (ferries).
Viewing the Bangui rapids.
Exploring the dense rainforest banks.

name: Karun River
overview: The Karun is Iran's most effluent and only navigable river. It flows from the Zagros Mountains to the Shatt al-Arab.
highlights:
Visiting the ancient hydraulic system at Shushtar (UNESCO).
Walking the bridges in Ahvaz.
History of ancient civilizations in Khuzestan.

name: Severn River
overview: The River Severn is the longest river in the United Kingdom. It is famous for its tidal bore and the historic Ironbridge Gorge.
highlights:
Surfing the Severn Bore.
Visiting Ironbridge Gorge (UNESCO).
Exploring Shrewsbury and Worcester cathedrals.

name: Niagara Falls
overview: A massive group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River, straddling the US-Canada border.
highlights:
Includes Horseshoe Falls, American Falls, and Bridal Veil Falls.
Highest flow rate in North America.
Famous Maid of the Mist boat tours.

name: Mulafossur
overview: A breathtaking waterfall that cascades directly from a high cliff into the North Atlantic Ocean.
highlights:
Located on Vagar Island in the remote village of Gasadalur.
One of the most iconic and photographed spots in the Faroe Islands.
The village was one of the most isolated in Europe until a tunnel was built in 2004.

name: Yosemite Falls
overview: One of the tallest waterfalls in North America, located in Yosemite Valley.
highlights:
Consists of Upper, Middle, and Lower falls.
Best viewed in late spring when snowmelt is peak.
Iconic landmark of Yosemite National Park.

name: Bridalveil Fall
overview: A prominent waterfall in Yosemite Valley that flows year-round.
highlights:
Often the first waterfall seen when entering the valley.
Famous for its mist that flutters like a bridal veil.
Accessible via a short trail.

name: Vernal Fall
overview: A powerful waterfall on the Merced River, known for its mist trail.
highlights:
Hikers can walk the Mist Trail right alongside the falls.
Produces vibrant rainbows in the spray.
Located downstream of Nevada Fall.

name: Nevada Fall
overview: A major waterfall on the Merced River, located above Vernal Fall.
highlights:
Distinctive bent shape near the top.
Accessible via the Mist Trail or John Muir Trail.
Offers panoramic views of Liberty Cap.

name: Havasu Falls
overview: A stunning blue-green waterfall located within the Grand Canyon on Havasupai tribal land.
highlights:
Famous for its turquoise water and travertine pools.
Requires a long hike or helicopter ride to reach.
A sacred site for the Havasupai people.

name: Mooney Falls
overview: The tallest of the waterfalls in Havasu Canyon, known for its adventurous descent.
highlights:
Accessed by climbing down chains and ladders through a tunnel.
Spectacular drop into a large blue pool.
More secluded than Havasu Falls.

name: Palouse Falls
overview: The official state waterfall of Washington, dropping into a churning bowl.
highlights:
Remnant of the Ice Age Missoula Floods.
Surrounded by dramatic basalt cliffs.
Popular for photography and geology enthusiasts.

name: Shoshone Falls
overview: Known as the 'Niagara of the West', located on the Snake River.
highlights:
Higher than Niagara Falls.
Best viewed in spring when water flow is high.
Features a park with overlooks and picnic areas.

name: Multnomah Falls
overview: A towering two-tiered waterfall in the Columbia River Gorge.
highlights:
Iconic Benson Bridge spans the lower drop.
Most visited natural recreation site in the Pacific Northwest.
Accessible directly from the historic highway.

name: Snoqualmie Falls
overview: A famous waterfall east of Seattle, known for its cultural and hydroelectric significance.
highlights:
Featured in the TV series 'Twin Peaks'.
Sacred site for the Snoqualmie people.
Has observation decks and a hiking trail to the base.

name: Taughannock Falls
overview: The tallest single-drop waterfall east of the Rockies.
highlights:
Located in a scenic state park near Ithaca.
Plunges into a deep amphitheater of shale.
Accessible via rim and gorge trails.

name: Plitvice Falls
overview: A network of cascading waterfalls connecting 16 terraced lakes.
highlights:
Veliki Slap is the tallest waterfall in Croatia.
UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Famous for distinctive turquoise water colors.

name: Montmorency Falls
overview: A large waterfall located just minutes from downtown Québec City.
highlights:
Higher than Niagara Falls.
Features a suspension bridge over the crest.
Popular for ziplining and winter ice climbing.

name: Helmcken Falls
overview: The most famous waterfall in Wells Gray Provincial Park.
highlights:
Fourth highest waterfall in Canada.
Plunges into a massive canyon.
Creates a famous ice cone in winter.

name: Takakkaw Falls
overview: A magnificent waterfall in Yoho National Park, fed by the Daly Glacier.
highlights:
Second highest waterfall in Canada.
Name means 'magnificent' in Cree.
Easy access from the road.

name: Virginia Falls
overview: A massive waterfall on the South Nahanni River in Nahanni National Park.
highlights:
More than twice the height of Niagara Falls.
Features a central rock called Mason's Rock.
UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Cascada de Basaseachi
overview: The second highest waterfall in Mexico, located in the Copper Canyon region.
highlights:
Free-falling plunge surrounded by pine forests.
Visible from multiple viewpoints.
Part of a protected national park.

name: Angel Falls
overview: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, falling from Auyán-tepui.
highlights:
UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Requires a river trip to reach the base.
Inspired the setting for the movie 'Up'.

name: Iguazu Falls
overview: The largest waterfall system in the world, spanning the Argentina-Brazil border.
highlights:
Consists of 275 individual drops.
The 'Devil's Throat' is the most impressive section.
Surrounded by lush subtropical rainforest.

name: Kaieteur Falls
overview: The world's largest single drop waterfall by volume.
highlights:
Located in the Amazon rainforest.
Four times higher than Niagara Falls.
Famous for its raw power and remote location.

name: Gocta Falls
overview: A towering two-tiered waterfall known to locals but only revealed to the world in 2005.
highlights:
One of the tallest waterfalls in the world.
Accessible via a hike through cloud forest.
Associated with local legends of a mermaid.

name: Cascada de San Rafael
overview: Once Ecuador's highest waterfall, drastically changed by a sinkhole in 2020.
highlights:
Located in the Cayambe Coca National Park.
Historically a massive volume of water.
Surrounded by dense Amazonian vegetation.

name: Salto Grande
overview: A powerful waterfall located in Torres del Paine National Park.
highlights:
Connects Lake Nordenskjöld and Lake Pehoé.
Features vibrant turquoise glacial water.
Offers stunning views of the Paine Horns.

name: Sete Quedas
overview: A historic waterfall system that was submerged by the Itaipu Dam reservoir in 1982.
highlights:
Was once the world's largest waterfall by volume.
Consisted of 18 cataracts.
Now a submerged memory beneath the Paraná River.

name: Salto del Laja
overview: A famous horseshoe-shaped waterfall in central Chile.
highlights:
Major tourist stop on the Pan-American Highway.
Often called the 'Niagara of Chile'.
Popular for photography and nearby crafts.

name: Catarata del Toro
overview: A spectacular waterfall plunging into an extinct volcanic crater.
highlights:
Located in a private reserve with hummingbird gardens.
Vibrant colors from mineral-rich waters.
Offers a steep hike to the bottom.

name: Victoria Falls
overview: One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, known as 'The Smoke That Thunders'.
highlights:
Largest curtain of falling water in the world.
UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Famous for the Devil's Pool on the edge.

name: Tugela Falls
overview: A complex of seasonal waterfalls in the Drakensberg mountains.
highlights:
World's second tallest waterfall.
Best viewed after summer rains.
Accessible via a challenging hike to the amphitheater.

name: Kalambo Falls
overview: The second highest single-drop waterfall in Africa, on the Kalambo River.
highlights:
Important archaeological site nearby.
Breeding ground for the Marabou stork.
Situated on the Tanzania-Zambia border.

name: Wli Falls
overview: The highest waterfall in West Africa, known locally as Agumatsa Falls.
highlights:
Consists of upper and lower falls.
Surrounded by the Agumatsa Wildlife Sanctuary.
Home to a large colony of fruit bats.

name: Ruacana Falls
overview: A grand waterfall on the Kunene River bordering Namibia and Angola.
highlights:
Volume varies greatly due to an upstream dam.
Spectacular width during high flow.
Popular destination for adventure travelers.

name: Lumangwe Falls
overview: A wide waterfall on the Kalungwishi River, often called a miniature Victoria Falls.
highlights:
Remote and pristine atmosphere.
Located near other waterfalls like Kabwelume.
Great for camping and nature viewing.

name: Blue Nile Falls
overview: A famous waterfall on the Blue Nile river, known locally as Tis Abay.
highlights:
Produces continuous mist and rainbows.
Best viewed in the wet season (August-September).
Historically significant for the Nile ecosystem.

name: Boyoma Falls
overview: Formerly known as Stanley Falls, consisting of seven cataracts on the Lualaba River.
highlights:
Highest flow rate of any waterfall in the world.
Spans over 100km of river.
Local fishermen use unique wooden tripods.

name: Lofoi Falls
overview: One of the highest waterfalls in Central Africa, located in Kundelungu National Park.
highlights:
Spectacular single continuous drop.
Remote location requires 4x4 access.
Surrounded by pristine gallery forest.

name: Gullfoss
overview: Iceland's most famous waterfall, part of the Golden Circle route.
highlights:
Features a unique two-stage drop into a canyon.
Name means 'Golden Falls'.
Saved from industrial development by Sigridur Tomasdottir.

name: Seljalandsfoss
overview: A picturesque waterfall where visitors can walk behind the cascading water.
highlights:
Unique 360-degree viewing experience.
Visible from the Ring Road.
Spectacular at sunset.

name: Skógafoss
overview: One of the biggest and most beautiful waterfalls in Iceland.
highlights:
Produces double rainbows on sunny days.
Legend says a treasure chest is buried behind it.
Stairs allow access to the top for views.

name: Dettifoss
overview: The most powerful waterfall in Europe by water volume.
highlights:
Located in Vatnajökull National Park.
Features grey, glacial meltwater.
Filming location for the movie 'Prometheus'.

name: Godafoss
overview: The 'Waterfall of the Gods', a historic site in Icelandic Christianity.
highlights:
Horseshoe-shaped fall on the Skjálfandafljót river.
Easy access from the Ring Road.
Site where pagan idols were thrown into the water.

name: Dynjandi
overview: A magnificent series of waterfalls in the Westfjords, resembling a bridal veil.
highlights:
Widest waterfall in the Westfjords.
Requires a short hike past smaller waterfalls.
Stunning views of the fjord below.

name: Reichenbach Falls
overview: A series of waterfalls on the Reichenbach stream, famous in literature.
highlights:
Setting of the final showdown between Sherlock Holmes and Moriarty.
Accessible via a funicular railway.
Spectacular views of the Hasli Valley.

name: Staubbach Falls
overview: A signature waterfall of the Lauterbrunnen Valley, falling as a misty spray.
highlights:
One of the highest free-falling waterfalls in Europe.
Inspired poetry by Goethe.
Illuminated at night during summer.

name: Trümmelbach Falls
overview: A series of ten glacier-fed waterfalls inside a mountain.
highlights:
The only glacier waterfalls in the world accessible underground by lift.
Carries up to 20,000 liters of water per second.
Unique geological formation.

name: Krimml Waterfalls
overview: The highest waterfall in Austria, cascading in three stages.
highlights:
Located in Hohe Tauern National Park.
Features a scenic hiking trail to the top.
Known for the therapeutic effects of its mist.

name: Rhine Falls
overview: The most powerful waterfall in Europe, located on the High Rhine.
highlights:
Impressive width of 150 meters.
Boat trips can take visitors to the central rock.
Illuminated at night.

name: Giessbach Falls
overview: A romantic series of 14 cascades tumbling into Lake Brienz.
highlights:
Features the historic Grandhotel Giessbach.
Accessible by boat and funicular.
Bridges allow visitors to walk behind the falls.

name: Vøringsfossen
overview: Norway's most famous waterfall, plunging into a deep canyon.
highlights:
Spectacular viewing platforms overlook the drop.
Located near the Hardangervidda plateau.
Especially impressive water volume in summer.

name: Langfossen
overview: A towering waterfall that flows directly into the Åkrafjord.
highlights:
Voted one of the world's most beautiful waterfalls.
Crosses under the main road (E134).
No free fall, but a long, steep cascade.

name: Mardalsfossen
overview: One of the highest waterfalls in Europe, regulated for hydroelectric power.
highlights:
Only flows freely during the summer tourist season.
Two-tiered drop with a massive vertical fall.
Requires a hike to reach the base.

name: Kjosfossen
overview: A powerful waterfall located directly on the Flåm Railway line.
highlights:
Trains make a special stop for passengers to view it.
Legendary Huldra spirits perform dance shows in summer.
Provides power to the railway.

name: Pistyll Rhaeadr
overview: The highest single-drop waterfall in the UK.
highlights:
Features a natural rock arch in the middle.
Located in the Berwyn Mountains.
One of the Seven Wonders of Wales.

name: Steall Falls
overview: A dramatic waterfall in Glen Nevis, Scotland's second highest.
highlights:
Featured in 'Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire'.
Accessible via a scenic gorge walk.
Requires crossing a wire rope bridge.

name: Cascate del Marmore
overview: The world's tallest man-made waterfall, created by ancient Romans.
highlights:
Water flow is turned on and off on a schedule.
Three tiers surrounded by lush parkland.
Spectacular at night with lights.

name: Rinka Falls
overview: One of the highest free-falling waterfalls in Slovenia.
highlights:
Located at the end of the scenic Logar Valley.
Source of the Savinja River.
Popular hiking destination with a nearby eagle's nest bar.

name: Kravica Falls
overview: A large tufa cascade on the Trebižat River, often compared to Iguazu Falls.
highlights:
Popular spot for swimming in summer.
Forms a natural amphitheater of water.
Surrounded by lush green vegetation.

name: Detian Falls
overview: A transnational waterfall on the Quay Son River between Vietnam and China.
highlights:
Largest waterfall in Asia crossing a national border.
Picturesque multi-tiered cascades.
Bamboo raft tours available.

name: Huangguoshu Falls
overview: One of the largest waterfalls in China and East Asia.
highlights:
Features the Water-Curtain Cave behind the falls.
Part of a large cluster of 18 waterfalls.
Impressive width of 101 meters.

name: Hukou Falls
overview: The largest waterfall on the Yellow River, known for its golden muddy water.
highlights:
Symbol of the Chinese spirit.
Flow changes dramatically with seasons.
Creates thunderous noise resembling a pouring teapot.

name: Kegon Falls
overview: The most famous of Nikko's many waterfalls, flowing from Lake Chuzenji.
highlights:
Elevator takes visitors to the base.
Stunning autumn foliage colors.
Ranked as one of Japan's Three Great Waterfalls.

name: Nachi Falls
overview: Japan's tallest waterfall with a single uninterrupted drop.
highlights:
Worshipped as a deity in Shintoism.
Located near the Seiganto-ji temple pagoda.
Part of UNESCO Sacred Sites of the Kii Mountain Range.

name: Jog Falls
overview: The second-highest plunge waterfall in India, formed by the Sharavathi River.
highlights:
Consists of four segments: Raja, Rocket, Roarer, and Rani.
Spectacular during the monsoon season.
Located in a dense evergreen forest.

name: Dudhsagar Falls
overview: A four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi River, meaning 'Sea of Milk'.
highlights:
One of India's tallest waterfalls.
A railway bridge passes directly in front of the falls.
Located in the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary.

name: Chitrakote Falls
overview: Often called the 'Niagara of India' due to its wide horseshoe shape.
highlights:
Located on the Indravati River.
Width expands up to 300 meters in monsoon.
Popular for boating at the base.

name: Pagsanjan Falls
overview: One of the most famous waterfalls in the Philippines, accessible by canoe.
highlights:
Features a thrilling 'Shooting the Rapids' boat ride.
Filming location for 'Apocalypse Now'.
Located in a scenic gorge.

name: Khone Phapheng Falls
overview: The widest waterfall in the world, located on the Mekong River.
highlights:
Prevents navigation up the Mekong into China.
Home to the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin.
Known as the 'Niagara of the East'.

name: Erawan Falls
overview: A beautiful seven-tiered waterfall known for its emerald green ponds.
highlights:
Named after the three-headed elephant Erawan.
Popular for swimming in the limestone pools.
Located in Erawan National Park.

name: Mae Ya Waterfall
overview: One of the largest and most beautiful waterfalls in Thailand.
highlights:
Located in Doi Inthanon National Park.
Fans out in a triangular shape over 30 tiers.
Peaceful and less crowded than others.

name: Kuang Si Falls
overview: A three-tiered waterfall famous for its stunning turquoise blue pools.
highlights:
Popular day trip from Luang Prabang.
Includes a bear rescue center at the entrance.
Pools are open for swimming.

name: Tegenungan Waterfall
overview: A popular waterfall near Ubud, set in a lush jungle environment.
highlights:
Easy access with stairs down to the water.
Heavy flow, especially in the rainy season.
Scenic photo spots like the bird's nest.

name: Gitgit Waterfall
overview: One of Bali's most famous and highest waterfalls, located in the north.
highlights:
Surrounded by tropical trees and cocoa plantations.
Accessible via a walk past souvenir shops.
Legend says couples who visit may break up.

name: Sutherland Falls
overview: New Zealand's most famous tall waterfall, located on the Milford Track.
highlights:
Fed by the quill lake in a hanging valley.
Three distinctive leaps.
Must be hiked to or viewed by scenic flight.

name: Browne Falls
overview: Often cited as New Zealand's highest waterfall, cascading into Doubtful Sound.
highlights:
Less a free leap, more a steep cascade.
Surrounded by dense temperate rainforest.
Best viewed from a cruise or plane.

name: Purakaunui Falls
overview: A highly photographed three-tiered cascading waterfall.
highlights:
Iconic image of The Catlins region.
Short, easy walk through beech and podocarp forest.
Very picturesque and serene.

name: Barron Falls
overview: A steep tiered cascade on the Barron River near Kuranda.
highlights:
Spectacular in the wet season; a trickle in dry.
Viewable from the Kuranda Scenic Railway.
Surrounded by World Heritage rainforest.

name: Wallaman Falls
overview: Australia's highest permanent single-drop waterfall.
highlights:
Located in Girringun National Park.
Features a deep pool at the bottom.
Part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area.

name: Jim Jim Falls
overview: A majestic waterfall in Kakadu National Park, flowing over immense red cliffs.
highlights:
Only accessible by 4WD in the dry season.
Best viewed by air during the wet season.
Swimming in the plunge pool is popular in dry season.

name: Russell Falls
overview: One of Tasmania's most treasured waterfalls, located in Mt Field National Park.
highlights:
Features elegant tiered cascades.
Surrounded by giant swamp gum trees and tree ferns.
First falls in Tasmania to be protected.

name: Akaka Falls
overview: A towering waterfall on the Big Island, plunging into a deep gorge.
highlights:
Located within Akaka Falls State Park.
Accessible via a loop trail through lush rainforest.
Visible from several viewpoints.

name: Waihilau Falls
overview: One of the tallest waterfalls in the world, located in the Waimanu Valley.
highlights:
Extremely remote and difficult to access.
Surrounded by untouched natural beauty.
Requires a strenuous hike or helicopter to view.

name: Burney Falls
overview: A spectacular waterfall fed by underground springs, flowing at a constant rate.
highlights:
Called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' by Teddy Roosevelt.
Maintains flow even in dry summers.
Located in McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park.

name: Lower Falls (Yellowstone)
overview: The most famous waterfall in Yellowstone, plunging into the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.
highlights:
Almost twice as high as Niagara Falls.
Iconic view from Artist Point.
Showcases the yellow rocks that gave the park its name.

name: Upper Falls (Yellowstone)
overview: The upstream companion to the Lower Falls on the Yellowstone River.
highlights:
Marks the beginning of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.
Powerful flow and easy viewing access.
Spectacular views from the Brink of the Upper Falls trail.

name: Ramona Falls
overview: A strikingly beautiful cascading waterfall located in the Mount Hood Wilderness.
highlights:
Features a unique wall of hexagonal basalt columns.
Accessible via a loop trail with views of Mount Hood.
Popular day hike destination.

name: Silver Falls
overview: The crown jewel of Silver Falls State Park, specifically referring to the iconic South Falls.
highlights:
Visitors can walk directly behind the curtain of water.
Part of the famous 'Trail of Ten Falls'.
Surrounded by lush temperate rainforest.

name: Bridal Veil Falls
overview: The tallest free-falling waterfall in Colorado, located at the end of a box canyon.
highlights:
Overlooks the historic town of Telluride.
Features a historic power plant at the top.
Accessible by 4x4 vehicle or hiking.

name: Chilnualna Falls
overview: A series of cascades located in the Wawona area of Yosemite.
highlights:
Less crowded than Yosemite Valley waterfalls.
Comprised of five distinct tiers.
Trail offers great views of the Wawona basin.

name: Illilouette Falls
overview: A hidden gem in Yosemite, visible from the Panorama Trail.
highlights:
Flows into a tight canyon below Glacier Point.
Not visible from the main valley floor.
Best viewed from hiking trails.

name: Ribbon Fall
overview: The tallest single-drop waterfall in North America, located west of El Capitan.
highlights:
Often seasonal, flowing only in spring.
Drops into a narrow notch in the cliffs.
Spectacular thin stream of water.

name: Sentinel Fall
overview: A long series of cascades on the south side of Yosemite Valley.
highlights:
Flows over the Sentinel Rock formation.
Best viewed in peak snowmelt (spring).
Comparable in height to Yosemite Falls but less volume.

name: Cascada El Chiflon
overview: A stunning series of turquoise waterfalls, with Velo de Novia being the largest.
highlights:
Famous for its intense turquoise blue water.
Surrounded by lush jungle vegetation.
Visitors can hike up alongside the cascading river.

name: Cascada Velo de Novia
overview: A picturesque waterfall in the State of Mexico, popular for weekend getaways.
highlights:
Name means 'Bridal Veil Waterfall'.
Located in a park with picnic areas and crafts.
Easy access from the town of Avándaro.

name: Svartifoss
overview: Known as the 'Black Fall' due to the surrounding dark lava columns.
highlights:
Framed by hexagonal basalt columns.
Inspired the architecture of Hallgrímskirkja church.
Located in Vatnajökull National Park.

name: Háifoss
overview: The fourth highest waterfall in Iceland, situated in the Fossá river.
highlights:
Located in a dramatic gorge near the volcano Hekla.
Accompanied by a neighbor waterfall, Granni.
Requires a 4x4 vehicle to reach the parking lot.

name: Vinnufossen
overview: The tallest waterfall in Europe and one of the tallest in the world.
highlights:
Fed by the Vinnufonna glacier.
Cascades down a steep mountainside in multiple stages.
Easily visible from the highway.

name: Seven Sisters
overview: A famous set of seven distinct streams falling into the Geirangerfjord.
highlights:
UNESCO World Heritage Site feature.
Best viewed from a fjord cruise.
Opposite the 'Suitor' waterfall.

name: Storseterfossen
overview: A unique waterfall in Geiranger where visitors can walk behind the falling water.
highlights:
Path leads safely behind the curtain of water.
Requires a hike from the Vesterås farm.
Offers scenic views of the fjord valley.

name: Cascada de Cola de Caballo
overview: A beautiful fan-shaped waterfall at the head of the Ordesa Valley.
highlights:
Resembles a horse's tail ('Cola de Caballo').
Popular hiking destination in the Pyrenees.
Surrounded by towering limestone cliffs.

name: Cascada de Ézaro
overview: A waterfall that empties directly into the sea (Atlantic Ocean).
highlights:
One of the few waterfalls in Europe to fall into the ocean.
Illuminated on summer nights.
Located at the mouth of the Xallas River.

name: Tres Hermanas Falls
overview: The third tallest waterfall in the world, whose name means 'Three Sisters'.
highlights:
Consists of three tiered drops.
Located in a remote, protected national forest.
Surrounded by cloud forest vegetation.

name: Olo'upena Falls
overview: Often cited as the fourth tallest waterfall in the world, located on Molokai.
highlights:
Visible only from the ocean or air.
Plunges directly into the sea from high cliffs.
Located on the remote northern shore.

name: Yumbilla Falls
overview: A towering tiered waterfall in the Peruvian Amazon, taller than Gocta.
highlights:
Fifth tallest waterfall in the world.
Surrounded by pristine high jungle.
Relatively recently discovered by the outside world.

name: Skorga
overview: One of Norway's highest waterfalls, though less famous than others.
highlights:
Located in the Sunndal region.
Volume fluctuates significantly with snowmelt.
Often obscured by difficult terrain.

name: Balåifossen
overview: A tall, seasonal waterfall located in the Hardangerfjord region.
highlights:
Fed by melting snow from the high mountains.
Often dries up completely in late summer.
Among the highest drops in Europe when flowing.

name: Mattenbachfall
overview: A massive waterfall in the Lauterbrunnen Valley, often cited as Switzerland's highest.
highlights:
Flows down the steep flank of the valley.
Best seen during heavy rain or peak snowmelt.
Part of the 'Valley of 72 Waterfalls'.

name: Pu'uka'oku Falls
overview: Another massive waterfall on the sea cliffs of Molokai, near Olo'upena.
highlights:
Eighth tallest waterfall in the world.
Deeply etched into the volcanic cliff face.
Only viewable by helicopter or boat.

name: James Bruce Falls
overview: The highest measured waterfall in North America, located in Princess Louisa Inlet.
highlights:
Fed by a snowfield and glacier.
Splits into two parallel streams.
Flow is best in early summer.

name: Strupenfossen
overview: A high waterfall in the Myklebustdalen valley.
highlights:
Fed by the Myklebustbreen glacier.
Cascades down a steep, rocky face.
Often active only in summer.

name: Ramnefjellsfossen
overview: Historically listed as one of the world's highest, located at Lovatnet lake.
highlights:
Also known as Utigordsfossen.
Fed by the Ramnefjellbreen glacier.
Associated with historic landslide tsunamis in the lake.

name: Colonial Creek Falls
overview: Currently considered the tallest waterfall in the continental United States.
highlights:
Located in North Cascades National Park.
Rarely visited due to difficult access.
Surpasses Yosemite Falls in total height.

name: Mongefossen
overview: One of the tallest single-drop waterfalls in the world.
highlights:
Visible from the Rauma Railway.
Flow is regulated for hydropower, reducing its volume.
Spectacular height when flowing.

name: Mutarazi Falls
overview: The highest waterfall in Zimbabwe, located in Nyanga National Park.
highlights:
Features a skywalk and zipline.
Drops into the Honde Valley.
Second highest in Africa after Tugela.

name: Kjelfossen
overview: A towering waterfall visible from the village of Gudvangen.
highlights:
Consists of three separate streams.
Looks incredibly high from the fjord level.
Often called 'The Kettle Falls'.

name: Johannesburg Falls
overview: A high-volume cascade falling from Johannesburg Mountain.
highlights:
Located in North Cascades National Park.
Fed by active glaciers.
Very difficult to view close up.

name: Cloudcap Falls
overview: A tall waterfall descending from Seahpo Peak in the North Cascades.
highlights:
Often ignored despite its great height.
Visible from the Cascade River Road.
Multi-step cascade.

name: Cascades de Trou de Fer
overview: A breathtaking waterfall dropping into a massive volcanic canyon.
highlights:
Located in the 'Iron Hole' gorge.
Best viewed by helicopter due to remote terrain.
Surrounded by lush tropical vegetation.

name: Ølmåafossen
overview: A tall, ribbon-like waterfall in the Romsdalen valley.
highlights:
Highest waterfall in the Romsdalen region.
Best flow during spring thaw.
Often overlooked due to nearby Mongefossen.

name: Manawainui Falls
overview: A tall, steep waterfall located in Manawainui Gulch on Maui.
highlights:
Situated in Haleakala National Park.
Highly seasonal and often dry.
Viewable from a distance or air.

name: Kjeragfossen
overview: A waterfall that plunges from the famous Kjerag plateau.
highlights:
Located near the Kjeragbolten boulder.
Only flows significantly in wet weather.
Drops into the scenic Lysefjord.

name: Avalanche Basin Falls
overview: A towering waterfall in Glacier National Park, fed by the Sperry Glacier.
highlights:
One of the tallest waterfalls in the Rockies.
Viewable from the Avalanche Lake trail.
Surrounded by a spectacular cirque basin.

name: Harrison Basin Falls
overview: A massive cascade in Glacier National Park, south of Avalanche Basin.
highlights:
Fed by the Harrison Glacier.
Very remote and difficult to access.
Flows down a series of steep steps.

name: Haloku Falls
overview: Another of the giant waterfalls on the Molokai north shore.
highlights:
Drops directly into the ocean.
Located near Olo'upena and Pu'uka'oku.
Best seen by boat or helicopter.

name: Chamberlain Falls
overview: A spectacular waterfall cascading into Doubtful Sound.
highlights:
One of New Zealand's tallest waterfalls.
Visible from cruise boats in the sound.
Plunges from Lake Chamberlain.

name: Døntefossen
overview: A tall waterfall in Romsdalen, consisting of four distinct drops.
highlights:
Scenic backdrop to the Rauma River.
Easily visible from the valley floor.
Fed by mountain snowmelt.

name: Kadamaian Falls
overview: A massive waterfall cascading down the slopes of Mount Kinabalu.
highlights:
One of the tallest waterfalls in Southeast Asia.
Visible from Kota Belud on clear days.
Access is extremely difficult.

name: Spirefossen
overview: A long cascading waterfall that joins the Strupenfossen system.
highlights:
Shares the same glacier source as Strupenfossen.
Highly seasonal flow.
Dominates the valley view when active.

name: Lake Unknown Falls
overview: A waterfall flowing from the aptly named Lake Unknown.
highlights:
Located in Mount Aspiring National Park.
Remote and requires difficult hiking.
Drops into the Dart River valley.

name: Cuquenan Falls
overview: Also known as Salto Kukenan, it plunges from the Kukenan Tepui.
highlights:
Second tallest major waterfall in Venezuela.
Neighbor to Mount Roraima.
Visible from great distances in the Gran Sabana.

name: Salto Yutaj
overview: A massive waterfall in the Venezuelan jungle, one of the world's highest.
highlights:
Located in a remote, unexplored region.
Discovered relatively recently.
Consists of twin drops.

name: Cascade Blanche
overview: One of the most prominent waterfalls in the Salazie Cirque.
highlights:
Extremely tall and slender appearance.
Visible from the road to Hell-Bourg.
Often shrouded in mist.

name: La Chorrera Falls
overview: The tallest waterfall in Colombia, located near Choachí.
highlights:
Multi-stepped drop surrounded by cloud forest.
Accessible via a scenic hike.
Popular day trip from Bogotá.

name: Kunchikal Falls
overview: The highest waterfall in India by total height.
highlights:
Formed by the Varahi River.
Cascades down rocky boulders rather than a free fall.
Located near the Agumbe rainforest.

name: Tågfossen
overview: A very high seasonal waterfall in the Sunndal region.
highlights:
Often ignored in favor of Vinnufossen.
Best viewed during spring snowmelt.
Cascades down a steep cliff face.

name: Tverrgrovfossen
overview: Another giant waterfall in Romsdalen, near Mongefossen.
highlights:
High volume during the thaw.
Contributes to the dramatic scenery of the valley.
Less famous but visually imposing.

name: Salto de Iguapo
overview: A remote waterfall in the Amazon rainforest of Venezuela.
highlights:
Little known and rarely visited.
Part of the immense Tepui landscape.
Requires an expedition to reach.

name: Kveåfossen
overview: A long, steep waterfall in Sognefjord.
highlights:
Visible from the road to the Nigardsbreen glacier.
Flows down a near-vertical cliff.
Scenic stop for photographers.

name: Høvlafossen
overview: A tall waterfall located near the famous Vinnufossen.
highlights:
Part of the cluster of giants in Sunndal.
Seasonal flow dependent on snow.
Impressive vertical drop.

name: Cascada de Ventisquero Colgante
overview: A stunning waterfall flowing directly from the Hanging Glacier.
highlights:
Located in Queulat National Park.
One of the most iconic sights in Patagonia.
Water falls from under a massive ice cap.

name: Los Chorros de Cura
overview: A prominent waterfall in Henri Pittier National Park.
highlights:
Tallest temporary waterfall in Venezuela when not raining (always flows).
Actually flows year round.
Surrounded by cloud forest.

name: Krokfossen
overview: A waterfall located in the scenic Mørkridsdalen valley.
highlights:
Requires a hike to view properly.
Surrounded by wild and raw nature.
Impressive spray and noise.

name: Svellofossen
overview: A little-known but very tall waterfall in the Hardanger region.
highlights:
Often overlooked by tourists.
Best seen from the fjord side.
Tall single drop section.

name: Heggurfossen
overview: A graceful waterfall plunging into the Tafjord.
highlights:
Fed by a mountain lake.
Slender and elegant appearance.
Visible from the road along the fjord.

name: Hannoki Falls
overview: The tallest waterfall in Japan, but seasonal.
highlights:
Only flows when snow melts (April-July).
Located next to Shomyo Falls.
Twin falls phenomenon when flowing.

name: Wall of Tears
overview: A series of many waterfalls cascading down a cliff face on Maui.
highlights:
Located near the summit of Puu Kukui.
Countless streams create a 'weeping' wall effect.
Featured in 'Jurassic Park'.

name: Lake Frances Falls
overview: A towering waterfall in Glacier National Park.
highlights:
Flows from Lake Frances.
Spectacular drop into a high alpine bowl.
Requires a backcountry hike.

name: Cerberus Falls
overview: A massive waterfall near Icefall Lake.
highlights:
Named after the three-headed dog of Hades.
Remote and rarely visited.
Surrounded by peaks of the Rockies.

name: Flueseelifall
overview: A high waterfall in the Simmental valley.
highlights:
Located in a nature reserve.
Two main drops.
Scenic hiking area.

name: Cascada de Piedra Bolada
overview: The highest waterfall in Mexico, located in the Copper Canyon.
highlights:
Also known as Cascada de Huajumar.
Seasonal flow, best in rainy season.
Spectacular view from across the canyon.

name: Keana'awi Falls
overview: A tall waterfall in the Koolau Gap on Maui.
highlights:
Surrounded by lush rainforest.
Often shrouded in clouds.
Difficult to see without aerial tour.

name: Hverfandi
overview: A powerful overflow waterfall from the Kárahnjúkar Dam.
highlights:
Only exists when the reservoir is full (late summer).
Would be one of Iceland's most powerful falls if permanent.
Spectacular contrast of concrete and wild water.

name: Edmonton Great Divide Waterfall
overview: An artificial waterfall on the High Level Bridge.
highlights:
Created to celebrate Alberta's centennial.
Operates only on holiday weekends in summer.
Currently undergoing refurbishment discussions.

name: Lake Peigneur
overview: Famous for a 1980 disaster where a lake drained into a salt mine, creating a temporary massive whirlpool-waterfall.
highlights:
The 'waterfall' lasted only days.
Swallowed barges and trees.
Now a calm lake again with a changed ecosystem.

name: Murchison Falls
overview: A powerful waterfall where the Nile forces its way through a narrow gorge.
highlights:
The entire Nile River squeezes through a 7m gap.
Extreme power and thunderous noise.
Famous location for wildlife boat safaris.

name: Howick Falls
overview: A tall waterfall on the Umgeni River located in the town of Howick.
highlights:
Known to the Zulu as 'The Tall One'.
Legend says a giant serpent lives in the pool.
Viewing platforms offer easy access.

name: Athirappilly Falls
overview: The largest waterfall in Kerala, often called the 'Niagara of India'.
highlights:
Featured in many Bollywood movies (e.g., Baahubali).
Located on the Chalakudy River.
Surrounded by dense forest and wildlife.

name: Rainbow Falls
overview: A picturesque waterfall located within Hilo town.
highlights:
Famous for morning rainbows in the mist.
Flows over a natural lava cave.
Legend says it is home to the moon goddess Hina.

name: Wailua Falls
overview: A double-tiered waterfall made famous by the TV show 'Fantasy Island'.
highlights:
Easily viewable from the roadside.
Historically used by chiefs for diving feats.
Surrounded by lush tropical greenery.

name: Latourell Falls
overview: A single-plunge waterfall in the Columbia River Gorge.
highlights:
Notable for the bright yellow lichen on the rock face.
Basalt columns flank the waterfall.
Closest major waterfall to Portland.

name: Shannon Falls
overview: The third highest waterfall in BC, located along the Sea-to-Sky Highway.
highlights:
Popular picnic stop near Squamish.
Legend says it was formed by a sea serpent.
Easy access via a short trail.

name: Brandywine Falls
overview: A spectacular waterfall south of Whistler.
highlights:
Viewable from a high observation deck.
Likely named after a wager involving brandy.
Surrounded by volcanic rock formations.

name: Hraunfossar
overview: A series of rivulets streaming out of a lava field.
highlights:
Water emerges directly from the Hallmundarhraun lava.
Name means 'Lava Falls'.
Creates a turquoise color contrast with the rock.

name: Barnafoss
overview: A turbulent waterfall just upstream from Hraunfossar.
highlights:
Name means 'Children's Falls' due to a tragic legend.
Features a natural stone arch (now collapsed).
Powerful, churning glacial water.

name: Tequendama Falls
overview: A historic waterfall on the Bogotá River.
highlights:
Features an abandoned haunted hotel (now a museum) on the cliff.
