Culturally significant to the Muisca people.
Spectacular drop into a misty canyon.

name: Chukchi Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean located between Alaska and Russia. It serves as a vital migration corridor for marine mammals and connects to the Bering Sea via the Bering Strait.
highlights: Polar bear populations, walrus haul-outs, and the seasonal ice edge.

name: East Siberian Sea
overview: A marginal sea in the Arctic Ocean, located off the coast of Siberia. It is one of the least studied Arctic seas due to its harsh climate and heavy ice cover.
highlights: New Siberian Islands, vast ice shelves, and remote Arctic coastline.

name: Laptev Sea
overview: Located off the coast of Siberia, this sea is a major source of sea ice for the Arctic Ocean. It receives freshwater from the Lena River.
highlights: The Lena Delta, walrus habitats, and the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago.

name: Kara Sea
overview: Part of the Arctic Ocean north of Siberia, separated from the Barents Sea by Novaya Zemlya. It is historically significant for Arctic exploration and trade routes.
highlights: Novaya Zemlya, vast natural gas reserves, and Arctic convoys history.

name: Barents Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean, located off the northern coasts of Norway and Russia. It is distinguished by relatively warm currents making it a rich fishing ground.
highlights: The Svalbard archipelago, vast cod fisheries, and the Midnight Sun.

name: Queen Victoria Sea
overview: A body of water in the Arctic Ocean, stretching north of the chaotic scattering of islands in the Russian Arctic.
highlights: Franz Josef Land, extreme remote ice conditions, and polar exploration history.

name: Wandel Sea
overview: Also known as the McKinley Sea, this body of water lies off the northeast coast of Greenland. It is covered by ice year-round.
highlights: Nordostrundingen, extreme northern geography, and thick sea ice.

name: Greenland Sea
overview: Located between Greenland, Svalbard, and Iceland. It serves as a major conduit for water exchange between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans.
highlights: Deep water formation, seal breeding grounds, and drift ice.

name: Lincoln Sea
overview: A body of water in the Arctic Ocean, stretching from Cape Columbia in Canada to Cape Morris Jesup in Greenland. It contains the thickest sea ice in the Arctic.
highlights: Ellesmere Island coast, multi-year ice, and proximity to the North Pole.

name: The Northwest Passages
overview: A famous sea route connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans through the Canadian Arctic Archipelago.
highlights: Franklin's lost expedition sites, complex archipelagos, and shifting ice floes.

name: Hudson Bay
overview: A large body of saltwater in northeastern Canada. It is the second-largest bay in the world and freezes over completely in winter.
highlights: Polar bear capital (Churchill), beluga whale migration, and the Canadian Shield coastline.

name: Beaufort Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean located north of the Northwest Territories, the Yukon, and Alaska. It is known for its severe climate and oil reserves.
highlights: Mackenzie River delta, pingos on the coastline, and thick pack ice.

name: Norwegian Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean, located northwest of Norway. It serves as a transition zone between the boreal North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean.
highlights: Deep fjords along the Norwegian coast, rich herring stocks, and offshore energy platforms.

name: North Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean located between Great Britain, Scandinavia, and mainland Europe. It is a key region for shipping and energy production.
highlights: Offshore wind farms, major shipping lanes, and oil fields.

name: Baltic Sea
overview: An arm of the Atlantic Ocean, enclosed by Scandinavia, Finland, the Baltic countries, and the North European Plain. It is one of the world's largest bodies of brackish water.
highlights: The Stockholm Archipelago, amber beaches, and historic Hanseatic trade routes.

name: English Channel
overview: The body of water that separates Southern England from northern France and links the southern part of the North Sea to the Atlantic Ocean.
highlights: The White Cliffs of Dover, busy shipping traffic, and the Channel Tunnel route.

name: Irish Sea
overview: Separates the islands of Ireland and Great Britain. It is connected to the Atlantic Ocean by the North Channel and St George's Channel.
highlights: Isle of Man, ferry routes, and significant tidal energy potential.

name: Celtic Sea
overview: The area of the Atlantic Ocean off the south coast of Ireland. It is bordered by Saint George's Channel, the Bristol Channel, and the English Channel.
highlights: Rich marine life, important shipping lanes, and proximity to Cornwall.

name: Bay of Biscay
overview: A gulf of the northeast Atlantic Ocean located south of the Celtic Sea. It lies along the western coast of France and the northern coast of Spain.
highlights: Rugged coastlines, heavy storms, and deep submarine canyons.

name: Gulf of Cádiz
overview: An arm of the Atlantic Ocean between Cabo de São Vicente in Portugal and the Strait of Gibraltar.
highlights: Historical naval battles, important shipping routes, and coastal wetlands.

name: Alboran Sea
overview: The westernmost portion of the Mediterranean Sea, lying between the Iberian Peninsula and the north of Africa. It connects to the Atlantic Ocean via the Strait of Gibraltar.
highlights: Migration route for cetaceans, biodiversity hotspots, and strategic naval history.

name: Bosporus
overview: A narrow, natural strait and an internationally significant waterway located in northwestern Turkey. It forms part of the continental boundary between Europe and Asia.
highlights: Istanbul skyline, historic fortifications, and busy maritime traffic.

name: Dardanelles
overview: A narrow, natural strait and internationally significant waterway in northwestern Turkey that forms part of the continental boundary between Europe and Asia, connecting the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
highlights: Gallipoli campaign sites, ancient Troy nearby, and strategic geopolitical importance.

name: Mar Menor
overview: A coastal saltwater lagoon in the Iberian Peninsula located south-east of the autonomous community of Murcia, Spain, near Cartagena.
highlights: High salinity warm waters, therapeutic mud baths, and unique ecosystem.

name: Balearic Sea
overview: A body of water in the Mediterranean Sea near the Balearic Islands. It is an important tourist destination and fishing area.
highlights: The Balearic Islands (Mallorca, Ibiza), crystal clear waters, and sailing routes.

name: Gulf of Lion
overview: A wide embayment of the Mediterranean coastline of Languedoc-Roussillon and Provence in France. It is known for the strong Mistral wind.
highlights: Camargue delta, steep calanques, and major ports like Marseille.

name: Ligurian Sea
overview: An arm of the Mediterranean Sea, between the Italian Riviera (Liguria) and the island of Corsica. It is known for its deep waters and cetacean sanctuary.
highlights: Cinque Terre coast, Portofino, and whale watching opportunities.

name: Tyrrhenian Sea
overview: Part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. It is bounded by Corsica and Sardinia to the west and Sicily to the south.
highlights: Active volcanoes (Stromboli), Amalfi Coast, and the Aeolian Islands.

name: Adriatic Sea
overview: A body of water separating the Italian Peninsula from the Balkan Peninsula. It extends from the Plain of the Po to the Strait of Otranto.
highlights: Dalmatian coast islands, historic Dubrovnik and Venice, and warm summer waters.

name: Ionian Sea
overview: An elongated bay of the Mediterranean Sea, south of the Adriatic Sea. It is bounded by southern Italy, Albania, and Greece.
highlights: Deepest point of the Mediterranean (Calypso Deep), Greek islands like Corfu and Zakynthos.

name: Aegean Sea
overview: An elongated embayment of the Mediterranean Sea located between the Greek and Anatolian peninsulas. It is dotted with numerous islands.
highlights: Cyclades and Dodecanese islands, ancient Greek history, and turquoise waters.

name: Sea of Marmara
overview: The inland sea, entirely within the borders of Turkey, that connects the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea, thus separating Turkey's Asian and European lands.
highlights: Princes' Islands, key shipping route, and resort towns.

name: Levantine Sea
overview: The easternmost part of the Mediterranean Sea. It is bordered by Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Egypt, and Libya.
highlights: Warmest waters in the Mediterranean, Suez Canal access, and ancient ports.

name: Libyan Sea
overview: A portion of the Mediterranean Sea located north of the African coast (Libya and Egypt) and south of Crete.
highlights: Ancient trade routes, deep waters, and coastal desert landscapes.

name: Gulf of Gabès
overview: A gulf on the east coast of Tunisia in the Mediterranean Sea. It is known for its shallow waters and significant tidal range.
highlights: Djerba island, sponge fishing history, and unique tidal ecosystems.

name: Strait of Sicily
overview: The strait between Sicily and Tunisia. It separates the Tyrrhenian Sea and the western Mediterranean Sea from the eastern Mediterranean Sea.
highlights: Pantelleria island, strategic chokepoint, and complex currents.

name: Sea of Sardinia
overview: A body of water in the Mediterranean Sea between the Spanish archipelago of Balearic Islands and the Italian island of Sardinia.
highlights: Deep ocean floor, isolation, and pristine marine environment.

name: Black Sea
overview: A large inland sea situated between Southeastern Europe, the Caucasus, and Anatolia. It is connected to the Mediterranean via the Bosporus and to the Sea of Azov via the Kerch Strait.
highlights: Anoxic lower water layers, ancient trade routes, and seaside resorts.

name: Bay of Arguin
overview: A large bay on the Atlantic coast of Mauritania. It is part of the Banc d'Arguin National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
highlights: Major breeding ground for migratory birds, shallow waters, and biodiversity.

name: Yawri Bay
overview: A bay on the coast of Sierra Leone, south of the Freetown Peninsula. It is an important area for artisanal fishing and bird life.
highlights: Mangrove forests, mudflats, and diverse bird species.

name: Gulf of Guinea
overview: The northeasternmost part of the tropical Atlantic Ocean. It contains the intersection of the Equator and the Prime Meridian (Null Island).
highlights: Oil reserves, Null Island, and the volcanic islands of the Cameroon line.

name: Luanda Bay
overview: A bay protecting the harbor of Luanda, the capital of Angola. It is formed by a sand spit known as the Ilha de Luanda.
highlights: Luanda skyline, the Marginal promenade, and busy port traffic.

name: Walvis Bay
overview: A natural deep-water harbor in Namibia, protected by the Pelican Point sand spit. It is rich in marine life due to the Benguela Current.
highlights: Flamingo colonies, Dune 7, and southern right whale migration.

name: Saldanha Bay
overview: A natural harbor on the south-western coast of South Africa. It is the largest natural port in the country and an iron ore export hub.
highlights: West Coast National Park, calm waters for sailing, and aquaculture.

name: Table Bay
overview: A natural bay on the Atlantic coast of South Africa, overlooked by Cape Town and Table Mountain. It has been a famous haven for ships for centuries.
highlights: Robben Island, view of Table Mountain, and the Victoria & Alfred Waterfront.

name: False Bay
overview: A body of water defined by the Cape Peninsula to the west and Cape Hangklip to the east. It is known for its warmer waters compared to Table Bay.
highlights: Great white shark population (Seal Island), Boulders Beach penguins, and surfing.

name: North Water Polynya
overview: A recurring polynya (area of open water amid sea ice) located in northern Baffin Bay. It is one of the most biologically productive ecosystems in the Arctic.
highlights: Year-round open water, vital habitat for narwhals and polar bears.

name: Baffin Bay
overview: Located between Baffin Island and the west coast of Greenland. It is covered by ice for most of the year but serves as a key passage for Arctic wildlife.
highlights: Icebergs calving from Greenland, deep waters, and Inuit fishing grounds.

name: Davis Strait
overview: A northern arm of the Atlantic Ocean that connects Baffin Bay with the Labrador Sea. It is known for its extreme tides and complex currents.
highlights: Deep-water shrimp fisheries, iceberg drift path, and dramatic coastlines.

name: Labrador Sea
overview: An arm of the North Atlantic Ocean between the Labrador Peninsula and Greenland. It plays a crucial role in the formation of deep ocean water.
highlights: Rough seas, deep convection currents, and migration route for Atlantic salmon.

name: Gulf of St. Lawrence
overview: The outlet of the North American Great Lakes via the Saint Lawrence River into the Atlantic Ocean. It is a highly productive semi-enclosed sea.
highlights: Whale watching (Tadoussac), Prince Edward Island, and diverse marine life.

name: Gulf of Maine
overview: A large gulf of the Atlantic Ocean on the east coast of North America. It is renowned for having some of the highest tidal ranges in the world.
highlights: Historic lighthouses, lobster fisheries, and cold nutrient-rich waters.

name: Nantucket Sound
overview: A roughly triangular body of water off the coast of Massachusetts, bounded by Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard, and Nantucket.
highlights: Rich sailing history, warm summer waters, and shoals.

name: Vineyard Sound
overview: The stretch of the Atlantic Ocean separating the Elizabeth Islands and the southwestern part of Cape Cod from the island of Martha's Vineyard.
highlights: Strong tidal currents and scenic ferry routes.

name: Buzzards Bay
overview: A bay of the Atlantic Ocean adjacent to Massachusetts. It is a popular destination for fishing and boating.
highlights: Cape Cod Canal entrance, sheltered harbors, and scallop fisheries.

name: Narragansett Bay
overview: A bay and estuary on the north side of Rhode Island Sound. It forms New England's largest estuary.
highlights: Newport sailing culture, diverse islands, and the Claiborne Pell Bridge.

name: Rhode Island Sound
overview: A strait off the coast of Rhode Island, at the eastern entrance to Long Island Sound.
highlights: Offshore wind farms and important shipping lanes.

name: Block Island Sound
overview: A strait in the open Atlantic Ocean, separating Block Island from the mainland of Rhode Island.
highlights: Deep water fishing and connection between Long Island Sound and the Atlantic.

name: Fishers Island Sound
overview: A body of water on the coast of the United States, between Fishers Island, New York, and the coast of Connecticut.
highlights: Historic Mystic Seaport nearby, calm protected waters.

name: Long Island Sound
overview: A tidal estuary of the Atlantic Ocean, lying between Connecticut to the north and Long Island, New York, to the south.
highlights: Gold Coast mansions, oyster farming, and recreational boating.

name: New York Bay
overview: The collective name for the marine areas surrounding the river mouth of the Hudson River into the Atlantic Ocean.
highlights: Statue of Liberty, Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, and busy container ports.

name: Jamaica Bay
overview: A saline to brackish bay on the southern side of Long Island, New York. It is a major wildlife refuge near JFK Airport.
highlights: Wildlife Refuge, bird watching, and salt marshes.

name: Raritan Bay
overview: A bay of the Atlantic Ocean located between New York and New Jersey, forming part of the New York Bight.
highlights: Key entryway to the Port of New York and New Jersey.

name: Sandy Hook Bay
overview: A triangular bay along the coast of New Jersey, formed by the Sandy Hook spit.
highlights: Sandy Hook Lighthouse, beaches, and recreational fishing.

name: Delaware Bay
overview: A major estuary outlet of the Delaware River on the Northeast Atlantic coast of the United States.
highlights: Horseshoe crab migration, oyster grounds, and historic lighthouses.

name: Chesapeake Bay
overview: The largest estuary in the United States, separating the Delmarva Peninsula from the mainland of Virginia and Maryland.
highlights: Blue crabs, Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel, and historic Jamestown nearby.

name: Albemarle Sound
overview: A large estuary on the coast of North Carolina. It is separated from the Atlantic Ocean by the Outer Banks.
highlights: Shallow brackish water, Outer Banks barrier islands, and cypress swamps.

name: Pamlico Sound
overview: The largest lagoon along the North American East Coast, separated from the Atlantic Ocean by the Outer Banks.
highlights: Graveyard of the Atlantic, fierce storms, and waterfowl habitat.

name: American Mediterranean Sea
overview: A combined oceanographic term for the waters of the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea. It is a semi-enclosed sea of the Atlantic Ocean.
highlights: Tropical hurricanes, vast coral reefs, and major tourism hubs.

name: Bay of All Saints
overview: Also known as Baía de Todos os Santos, it is the principal bay of the Brazilian state of Bahia and the largest bay in Brazil.
highlights: Salvador city, colonial history, and tropical islands like Itaparica.

name: Guanabara Bay
overview: An oceanic bay located in Southeast Brazil in the state of Rio de Janeiro. It is surrounded by tropical forests and the city of Rio.
highlights: Sugarloaf Mountain view, Rio de Janeiro harbor, and Niterói bridge.

name: Lagoa dos Patos
overview: The largest lagoon in Brazil and the second largest in Latin America, located in the state of Rio Grande do Sul.
highlights: Sandbar barrier, diverse birdlife, and the port city of Porto Alegre.

name: Argentine Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean off the southeastern coast of Argentina. It covers the continental shelf of Argentina.
highlights: Rich fisheries, Southern Right Whales (Valdes Peninsula), and penguin colonies.

name: Inner Seas off the West Coast of Scotland
overview: A maritime area designated by the IHO, separating the Inner Hebrides from the Outer Hebrides and the Scottish mainland.
highlights: Scenic Scottish islands, whiskies of Islay and Skye, and strong tidal streams.

name: Denmark Strait
overview: An oceanic strait between Greenland (to the northwest) and Iceland (to the southeast). It connects the Greenland Sea to the Irminger Sea.
highlights: Denmark Strait cataract (world's highest underwater waterfall), heavy pack ice.

name: Irminger Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the North Atlantic Ocean. It is named after the Danish vice-admiral Carl Ludvig Christian Irminger.
highlights: Deep ocean redfish habitats, key area for ocean currents.

name: Andaman Sea
overview: A body of water to the southeast of the Bay of Bengal, south of Myanmar, west of Thailand, and east of the Andaman Islands.
highlights: Similan Islands diving, limestone karsts, and vibrant coral reefs.

name: Antongil Bay
overview: The largest bay in Madagascar, located on the northeast coast. It is surrounded by lush rainforests.
highlights: Humpback whale breeding ground, Masoala National Park.

name: Arabian Sea
overview: A region of the northern Indian Ocean bounded on the north by Pakistan and Iran, on the west by the Gulf of Aden, and on the east by India.
highlights: Historic monsoon trade routes, major shipping lanes, and rich fisheries.

name: Bay of Bengal
overview: The northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bounded on the west and northwest by India, on the north by Bangladesh, and on the east by Myanmar.
highlights: The Sundarbans (largest mangrove forest), Cox's Bazar beach, and cyclones.

name: Gulf of Aden
overview: A deepwater gulf between Yemen to the north, the Arabian Sea to the east, Djibouti to the west, and the Guardafui Channel to the south.
highlights: Critical shipping route to Suez Canal, pirate history, and rich marine biodiversity.

name: Gulf of Oman
overview: A strait that connects the Arabian Sea with the Strait of Hormuz, which then runs to the Persian Gulf.
highlights: Strategic oil transit route, deep waters close to shore, and sea turtles.

name: Laccadive Sea
overview: A body of water bordering India, the Maldives, and Sri Lanka. It is known for its warm stable water temperature.
highlights: Lakshadweep islands, coral atolls, and pearl fisheries.

name: Mafia Channel
overview: A channel lying between the Mafia Island and the mainland of Tanzania.
highlights: Whale sharks, protected marine park, and unspoiled coral reefs.

name: Mentawai Strait
overview: A strait separating Sumatra from the Mentawai Islands in Indonesia.
highlights: World-class surfing breaks, deep trench waters, and seismic activity zone.

name: Mozambique Channel
overview: An arm of the Indian Ocean located between the Southeast African countries of Madagascar and Mozambique.
highlights: Coelacanth habitat, ancient trade history, and massive eddies.

name: Pemba Channel
overview: The strait separating Pemba Island from mainland Tanzania. It is known for its deep waters and big game fishing.
highlights: Marlin fishing grounds, clove trade history, and deep drop-offs.

name: Persian Gulf
overview: A mediterranean sea in Western Asia. The body of water is an extension of the Indian Ocean through the Strait of Hormuz.
highlights: World's largest oil reserves, pearl diving heritage, and man-made islands.

name: Red Sea
overview: A seawater inlet of the Indian Ocean, lying between Africa and Asia. It is the world's northernmost tropical sea.
highlights: Vibrant coral reefs (Dahab, Sharm El Sheikh), high salinity, and biblical history.

name: Sea of Zanj
overview: A historical name for the part of the western Indian Ocean adjacent to the region in the African Great Lakes referred to as Zanj.
highlights: Swahili coast culture, spice trade routes, and dhow sailing.

name: Zanzibar Channel
overview: A strait in south-eastern Africa, separating the island of Unguja (Zanzibar) from mainland Tanzania.
highlights: Stone Town views, spice tours access, and traditional dhows.

name: Bering Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean. It forms the divide between the two largest landmasses on Earth: Eurasia and The Americas.
highlights: King crab fisheries (Deadliest Catch), Aleutian Islands, and harsh weather.

name: Chilean Sea
overview: The portion of the Pacific Ocean lying west of the Chilean mainland. It is officially known as the Mar Chileno.
highlights: Humboldt Current, rich fisheries, and deep trenches.

name: Gulf of Alaska
overview: An arm of the Pacific Ocean defined by the curve of the southern coast of Alaska.
highlights: Glaciers calving into the sea, Kodiak Island bears, and salmon runs.

name: Gulf of Santa Catalina
overview: A gulf in the Pacific Ocean on the west coast of North America, east of Santa Catalina Island.
highlights: Catalina Island, dolphin watching, and Southern California coast.

name: Salish Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean located in the Canadian province of British Columbia and the U.S. state of Washington.
highlights: Orca pods, San Juan Islands, and ferry networks.

name: Gulf of California
overview: Also known as the Sea of Cortez, it is a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean that separates the Baja California Peninsula from the Mexican mainland.
highlights: Rich biodiversity ('Aquarium of the World'), gray whale breeding, and Baja desert landscapes.

name: Gulf of the Farallones
overview: A gulf of the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Northern California, extending outward from the Golden Gate.
highlights: Farallon Islands wildlife refuge, Great White Sharks, and shipwrecks.

name: Gulf of Fonseca
overview: A gulf in Central America, bordering El Salvador, Honduras, and Nicaragua.
highlights: Volcanic islands, mangrove wetlands, and shared maritime borders.

name: Gulf of Guayaquil
overview: A large body of water on the Pacific coast of South America. It is the largest estuary on the Pacific coast of South America.
highlights: Puná Island, mangrove ecosystems, and access to the Galapagos.

name: Gulf of Nicoya
overview: An inlet of the Pacific Ocean on the coast of Costa Rica. It separates the Nicoya Peninsula from the mainland of Costa Rica.
highlights: Tortuga Island, marine parks, and bioluminescence.

name: Gulf of Panama
overview: A gulf in the Pacific Ocean, formed by the southeastern coast of Panama.
highlights: Pearl Islands (Archipiélago de las Perlas), Panama Canal entrance, and whale watching.

name: Grau Sea
overview: The official name for the body of water in the Pacific Ocean under the control of Peru.
highlights: Rich anchovy fisheries, cold Humboldt Current, and coastal deserts.

name: San Francisco Bay
overview: A shallow estuary in the U.S. state of California. It is surrounded by a contiguous region known as the San Francisco Bay Area.
highlights: Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz Island, and Silicon Valley tech hubs.

name: Arafura Sea
overview: A shallow sea lying between Australia and New Guinea, bordering the Gulf of Carpentaria and the Timor Sea.
highlights: Rich shrimp fisheries, pearl farming, and shallow continental shelf.

name: Balabac Strait
overview: A strait connecting the South China Sea with the Sulu Sea, separating Balabac Island (Philippines) from Borneo (Malaysia).
highlights: Important maritime passage, coral reefs, and biodiversity corridor.

name: Bali Sea
overview: A body of water north of the island of Bali and south of Kangean Island in Indonesia.
highlights: Ocean currents circulation, proximity to Bali tourist hubs.

name: Bali Strait
overview: A stretch of water separating Java and Bali. It connects the Indian Ocean and the Bali Sea.
highlights: Ferry traffic between Java and Bali, strong currents.

name: Banda Sea
overview: A sea in the Maluku Islands of Indonesia, connected to the Pacific Ocean but surrounded by hundreds of islands.
highlights: Spice Islands history, deep Weber Deep, and scuba diving.

name: Bangka Strait
overview: A strait separating the islands of Sumatra and Bangka in Indonesia.
highlights: Maritime boundary, tin mining history nearby.

name: Celebes Sea
overview: A sea of the western Pacific Ocean, bordered by the Sulu Archipelago, Mindanao, the Sangihe Islands, Sulawesi, and Borneo.
highlights: Diverse marine habitats, pirate history, and deep basins.

name: Ceram Sea
overview: One of several small seas between the scattered islands of Indonesia (Maluku).
highlights: Remote islands, tropical marine life, and seismic activity.

name: Davao Gulf
overview: A gulf situated in the southeastern portion of Mindanao in the Philippines.
highlights: Samal Island, Davao City waterfront, and rich biodiversity.

name: Flores Sea
overview: A sea covering the waters north of Flores Island in Indonesia.
highlights: Komodo National Park nearby, vibrant coral reefs.

name: Gaspar Strait
overview: A strait that separates the islands of Belitung and Bangka in Indonesia.
highlights: Historical shipwrecks, passage to Java Sea.

name: Gulf of Carpentaria
overview: A large, shallow sea enclosed on three sides by northern Australia.
highlights: Morning Glory Cloud phenomenon, prawn fisheries, and remote coastline.

name: Gulf of Thailand
overview: A shallow inlet of the South China Sea, bordered by Cambodia, Thailand, and Vietnam.
highlights: Popular islands (Koh Samui, Koh Tao), tourism, and oil deposits.

name: Gulf of Boni
overview: Also known as the Gulf of Bone, it divides the South and Southeast Peninsulas of Sulawesi.
highlights: Deep waters, ecological diversity within Sulawesi.

name: Gulf of Tomini
overview: The equatorial gulf that separates the Minahassa (Northern) and East Peninsulas of Sulawesi.
highlights: Togian Islands, calm waters, and diving spots.

name: Halmahera Sea
overview: A regional sea located in the central eastern part of the Australasian Mediterranean Sea.
highlights: Mining activities nearby, deep basins.

name: Java Sea
overview: A large shallow sea on the Sunda Shelf, lying between the Indonesian islands of Borneo, Java, Sumatra, and Sulawesi.
highlights: Battle of the Java Sea site, oil exploration, and busy shipping.

name: Karimata Strait
overview: A wide strait connecting the South China Sea to the Java Sea, separating Sumatra and Borneo.
highlights: Belitung Island beaches, major shipping lane.

name: Lombok Strait
overview: A strait connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean, located between the islands of Bali and Lombok.
highlights: Wallace Line boundary, deep water passage for supertankers.

name: Madura Strait
overview: A stretch of water separating the Indonesian islands of Java and Madura.
highlights: Suramadu Bridge, salt production history.

name: Makassar Strait
overview: A strait located between the islands of Borneo and Sulawesi in Indonesia.
highlights: Mahakam River delta, deep oceanic trench, and oil traffic.

name: Malacca Strait
overview: A narrow stretch of water between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra. One of the most important shipping lanes in the world.
highlights: Global trade chokepoint, historic ports (Melaka, Penang, Singapore).

name: Molucca Sea
overview: Located in the western Pacific Ocean, within the country of Indonesia, bordered by Halmahera and Sulawesi.
highlights: Geologically active plate collision zone, spice trade route.

name: Mindoro Strait
overview: A strait in the Philippines separating Mindoro Island from Busuanga Island (Palawan).
highlights: Apo Reef (world's second-largest contiguous coral reef system).

name: Ombai Strait
overview: A strait separating the Alor Archipelago from the islands of Wetar, Atauro, and Timor.
highlights: Migration corridor for whales and dolphins.

name: Philippine Inland Sea
overview: The enclosed waters within the Philippine archipelago, surrounded by the major islands of Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
highlights: Center of Philippine marine biodiversity, inter-island ferry network.

name: Riau Strait
overview: A narrow strait in the Riau Archipelago of Indonesia.
highlights: Busy local shipping, proximity to Batam and Bintan.

name: Savu Sea
overview: A small sea within Indonesia, named after the island of Savu (Sawu). It connects to the Indian Ocean.
highlights: Savu Sea Marine National Park, cetacean migration.

name: Chao'an Bay
overview: A coastal bay in Guangdong Province, China, near the Chao'an District of Chaozhou. It is part of the biologically rich coastal waters of eastern Guangdong.
highlights: Aquaculture rafts, proximity to Shantou, and coastal fisheries.

name: Da Nang Bay
overview: A sheltered bay on the central coast of Vietnam, opening into the South China Sea. It is a natural harbor of significant historical and economic importance.
highlights: Port of Da Nang, Hai Van Pass views, and Son Tra Peninsula.

name: Daya Bay
overview: A bay in Guangdong Province, China, to the northeast of Hong Kong. It is the site of major energy infrastructure.
highlights: Daya Bay Nuclear Power Plant, marine research stations, and coastal islands.

name: Dongshan Bay
overview: A bay located in the southern part of Fujian Province, China. It is known for its tourism and connection to Dongshan Island.
highlights: Dongshan Island beaches, windsurfing competitions, and seafood.

name: Futou Bay
overview: A bay on the coast of Fujian Province, China. It serves as a local fishing ground and transport route.
highlights: Local fishing fleets and coastal villages.

name: Guang'ao Bay
overview: A bay located near Shantou in Guangdong Province. It is part of the designated port and logistics area of the region.
highlights: Deep-water port facilities and maritime logistics.

name: Guanghai Bay
overview: A bay located in Taishan, Guangdong Province. It is an area of significant industrial development and power generation.
highlights: Guanghai Harbor, power stations, and reclamation projects.

name: Gulf of Tonkin
overview: A large arm of the South China Sea, lying between the coast of northern Vietnam and China's Hainan Island.
highlights: Ha Long Bay (UNESCO site), Red River Delta, and major fisheries.

name: Haimen Bay
overview: A bay located at the mouth of the Lianjiang River in the Chaoyang District of Shantou, China.
highlights: Historical Haimen Fortress, fishing port, and sea views.

name: Haitang Bay
overview: One of the major bays in Sanya, Hainan Province. It is known as the 'National Coast' due to its luxury resort developments.
highlights: Luxury resorts (Atlantis Sanya), Wuzhizhou Island, and pristine beaches.

name: Hiechechin Bay
overview: Historical name often associated with Jieshi Bay (Jieshiwan) in Guangdong Province. It is located near Lufeng.
highlights: Xuanwu Mountain nearby, traditional fishing grounds, and coastal defense history.

name: Honghai Bay
overview: Also known as Red Sea Bay, located in Shanwei, Guangdong. It is a semi-enclosed bay famous for hosting the Asian Games sailing events.
highlights: The 'Covered Waves' (Zhelang) peninsula, international sailing center, and power plant.

name: Huangmao Sea
overview: An estuary and bay in the western Pearl River Delta, China. It is crossed by the Huangmao Sea Channel Bridge.
highlights: Major bridge infrastructure, wetland ecosystems, and shipping lanes.

name: Jiuzhouyang
overview: The body of water off the coast of Zhuhai and Macau, at the mouth of the Pearl River Estuary.
highlights: Ferry routes to Hong Kong, Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge views.

name: Leizhou Bay
overview: A bay on the eastern side of the Leizhou Peninsula in Guangdong, China. It faces the South China Sea.
highlights: Dugong habitat conservation, shallow tidal flats, and oyster farming.

name: Lingayen Gulf
overview: A large gulf on northwestern Luzon in the Philippines. It is defined by the Zambales Mountains and the Cordillera Central.
highlights: Hundred Islands National Park, historical WWII landing site.

name: Luzon Strait
overview: The strait connecting the Philippine Sea to the South China Sea, situated between Taiwan and Luzon.
highlights: Key strategic waterway, internal waves generation, and Batanes Islands.

name: Mirs Bay
overview: Also known as Dapeng Bay, located between the New Territories of Hong Kong and the Dapeng Peninsula of Shenzhen.
highlights: Ping Chau Island, marine parks, and container terminals.

name: Natuna Sea
overview: A shallow sea around the Natuna Islands of Indonesia, connecting the South China Sea to the Java Sea.
highlights: Natuna Regency, offshore gas fields, and rich fisheries.

name: Qiongzhou Strait
overview: Also known as the Hainan Strait, it separates the Leizhou Peninsula of Guangdong from Hainan Island.
highlights: Main ferry route to Hainan, busy shipping traffic.

name: Taiwan Strait
overview: A strait separating the island of Taiwan from mainland China. It connects the South China Sea to the East China Sea.
highlights: Strategic geopolitical significance, Penghu archipelago, and wind farms.

name: Sanya Bay
overview: One of the major bays in Sanya city, Hainan. It has a long sandy beach known as the Coconut Dream Corridor.
highlights: Phoenix Island, sunsets, and public beaches.

name: Sun and Moon Bay
overview: Also known as Riyue Bay, located in Wanning, Hainan. It is famous for surfing.
highlights: Surfing competitions, tropical scenery, and coastal geology.

name: West Philippine Sea
overview: The official designation by the government of the Philippines for the parts of the South China Sea that are within the country's exclusive economic zone.
highlights: Scarborough Shoal, rich marine resources, and strategic waters.

name: Yalong Bay
overview: A 7.5 km long crescent-shaped bay in Sanya, Hainan. It is known for its high-quality beach and luxury hotels.
highlights: Crystal clear water, coral reefs, and tropical forest park nearby.

name: Zhanjiang Bay
overview: A bay in the Zhanjiang area of Guangdong, China. It is a deep-water harbor and serves as the headquarters of the South Sea Fleet.
highlights: Military port, Zhanjiang Bay Bridge, and seafood markets.

name: Zhelin Bay
overview: A bay located at the border of Guangdong and Fujian provinces. It is known for its extensive aquaculture industries.
highlights: Floating fish farms, cage culture, and historic port.

name: Zhenhai Bay
overview: A bay located in Enping/Taishan, Guangdong Province. It is rich in mangrove forests and coastal fisheries.
highlights: Mangrove ecosystems, oyster farming, and rural coastal scenery.

name: Straits of Johor
overview: A narrow strait that separates the State of Johor (Malaysia) to the north from Singapore to the south.
highlights: Johor–Singapore Causeway, Malaysia–Singapore Second Link, and coastal reclamation.

name: Sulu Sea
overview: A body of water in the southwestern area of the Philippines, separated from the South China Sea by Palawan and from the Celebes Sea by the Sulu Archipelago.
highlights: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park (UNESCO site), pearl diving, and rich biodiversity.

name: Sunda Strait
overview: The strait between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra. It connects the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean.
highlights: Krakatoa (Anak Krakatau) volcano, strategic shipping lane, and strong tidal currents.

name: Timor Sea
overview: A relatively shallow sea bounded to the north by the island of Timor, to the east by the Arafura Sea, and to the south by Australia.
highlights: Significant oil and gas reserves, WWII history, and tropical cyclones.

name: Wetar Strait
overview: A deep strait separating the eastern part of the island of Timor from the island of Wetar. It is part of the boundary between the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
highlights: Major migration route for whales and dolphins, deep waters.

name: Bass Strait
overview: A strait separating the island state of Tasmania from the Australian mainland (Victoria). It is known for its rough waters and oil/gas fields.
highlights: King Island, Flinders Island, and the treacherous crossing for sailors.

name: Bay of Plenty
overview: A large bight on the northern coast of New Zealand's North Island. It was named by James Cook in 1769 due to the abundant resources he found there.
highlights: White Island (active volcano), Mount Maunganui beaches, and kiwi fruit orchards nearby.

name: Bismarck Sea
overview: A sea in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, enclosed by the Bismarck Archipelago and the island of New Guinea.
highlights: Battle of the Bismarck Sea (WWII), rich marine biodiversity, and volcanic islands.

name: Coral Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the South Pacific off the northeast coast of Australia. It contains the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system.
highlights: Great Barrier Reef, WWII Battle of the Coral Sea, and diverse shark populations.

name: East China Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean east of China, connecting to the South China Sea by the Taiwan Strait and to the Sea of Japan by the Korea Strait.
highlights: Busy shipping routes to Shanghai, rich fishing grounds, and disputed gas fields.

name: Fourth Kuril Strait
overview: A strait in the Kuril Islands separating Paramushir Island from Onekotan Island. It connects the Sea of Okhotsk with the Pacific Ocean.
highlights: Remote volcanic islands, strategic naval passage, and marine wildlife.

name: Great Australian Bight
overview: A large open bay off the central and western parts of the southern coastline of mainland Australia.
highlights: Nullarbor Plain cliffs, southern right whale calving grounds, and stormy seas.

name: Hauraki Gulf
overview: A coastal feature of the North Island of New Zealand. It lies between the Auckland Region, the Hauraki Plains, and the Coromandel Peninsula.
highlights: Waiheke Island vineyards, Rangitoto volcano, and sailing culture.

name: Hawke's Bay
overview: A large bay on the east coast of the North Island of New Zealand. The region surrounding it is famous for its wines.
highlights: Art Deco city of Napier, Cape Kidnappers gannet colony, and vineyards.

name: Hitokappu Bay
overview: Also known as Kasatka Bay, located on Iturup Island. Historically significant as the assembly point for the Pearl Harbor attack fleet.
highlights: Historical WWII site, remote Kuril landscape, and foggy conditions.

name: Koro Sea
overview: A sea within the Pacific Ocean, separating the Lau Group archipelago from the main islands of Fiji (Viti Levu and Vanua Levu).
highlights: Deep ocean basins, coral reefs, and Fijian island culture.

name: Kuril Strait
overview: Often refers to the First Kuril Strait separating the Kamchatka Peninsula from Shumshu Island.
highlights: Passage between Russia and the Pacific, rugged volcanic coastlines.

name: Philippine Sea
overview: A marginal sea east and northeast of the Philippines occupying an estimated surface area of 5 million square kilometers.
highlights: Mariana Trench (deepest point on Earth), frequent typhoons, and WWII naval battles.

name: Poverty Bay
overview: A large bay on the east coast of the North Island of New Zealand. It is the site of Captain Cook's first landing in New Zealand.
highlights: Young Nick's Head, Chardonnay vineyards nearby, and surfing breaks.

name: Sea of Japan (East Sea)
overview: A marginal sea between the Japanese archipelago, Sakhalin, the Korean Peninsula, and the mainland of the Russian Far East.
highlights: Rich fishing grounds, deep basins, and minimal tides.

name: Sea of Okhotsk
overview: A marginal sea of the western Pacific Ocean, lying between the Kamchatka Peninsula on the east, the Kuril Islands on the southeast, and the island of Hokkaido to the south.
highlights: Drift ice (Ryuhyo), rich crab fisheries, and oil reserves.

name: Seto Inland Sea
overview: The body of water separating Honshū, Shikoku, and Kyūshū, three of the four main islands of Japan. It is known for its calm waters and thousands of islands.
highlights: Itsukushima Shrine, Shimanami Kaido cycling route, and art islands (Naoshima).

name: Solomon Sea
overview: A sea located within the Pacific Ocean, bounded by Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands. It was a major theatre of war during WWII.
highlights: Deep ocean trenches, diverse coral reefs, and WWII shipwrecks.

name: Spencer Gulf
overview: The westernmost of two large inlets on the southern coast of Australia, facing the Great Australian Bight.
highlights: Giant Cuttlefish migration, Eyre Peninsula coastline, and aquaculture.

name: Tasman Sea
overview: A marginal sea of the South Pacific Ocean between Australia and New Zealand. It is named after the Dutch explorer Abel Tasman.
highlights: Lord Howe Island, Balls Pyramid, and the Sydney to Hobart yacht race route.

name: Uchiura Bay
overview: Also known as Volcano Bay, it is a bay located southeast of the Oshima Peninsula in Hokkaido, Japan.
highlights: Scallop farming, volcanic landscapes, and hot springs nearby.

name: Vries Strait
overview: A strait in the Kuril Islands separating the islands of Iturup and Urup. It connects the Sea of Okhotsk with the Pacific Ocean.
highlights: Strategic passage, nutrient-rich waters, and remote island geography.

name: Sahara Desert
overview: The largest hot desert in the world, covering most of North Africa. It features vast sand dunes, rocky plateaus, and occasional oases.
highlights:
Riding camels across the Great Sand Sea.
Watching the sunset over the dunes of Merzouga.
Visiting ancient trade routes and oases like Siwa.

name: Namib Desert
overview: A coastal desert in Southern Africa, considered the oldest desert in the world. It is famous for its towering red sand dunes meeting the Atlantic Ocean.
highlights:
Climbing Dune 45 and Big Daddy in Sossusvlei.
Seeing the surreal dead trees of Deadvlei.
Witnessing the desert meet the ocean at Sandwich Harbour.

name: Gobi Desert
overview: A vast, cold desert region in northern China and southern Mongolia. It is known for its dunes, mountains, and rare animals like the snow leopard.
highlights:
Exploring the Khongoryn Els singing sand dunes.
Visiting the Flaming Cliffs, a famous dinosaur fossil site.
Riding Bactrian camels in the vast steppe.

name: Salar de Uyuni
overview: The world's largest salt flat, located in southwest Bolivia. During the rainy season, a thin layer of water transforms it into a giant mirror.
highlights:
Taking perspective-bending photos on the white salt crust.
Visiting Incahuasi Island covered in giant cacti.
Seeing the mirror effect during the wet season.

name: Atacama Desert
overview: The driest non-polar desert on Earth, located in northern Chile. It offers lunar landscapes, geysers, and some of the clearest skies for astronomy.
highlights:
Watching the sunset at Valle de la Luna (Moon Valley).
Stargazing tours under incredibly clear skies.
Visiting the El Tatio Geysers at sunrise.

name: White Sands National Park
overview: Located in New Mexico, this park protects the world's largest gypsum dunefield. The glistening white sands create a unique, snow-like landscape.
highlights:
Sledding down the steep white gypsum dunes.
Hiking the Alkali Flat Trail.
Watching the sunset turn the white sands into pink and purple.

name: Rub' al Khali
overview: The Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert in the world, encompassing much of the southern Arabian Peninsula.
highlights:
Experiencing the vast silence of the endless dunes.
Dune bashing in 4x4 vehicles.
Camping overnight in the deep desert.

name: Lençóis Maranhenses
overview: A unique national park in Brazil featuring vast white sand dunes. During the rainy season, fresh water collects in the valleys, creating thousands of blue lagoons.
highlights:
Swimming in the freshwater lagoons between dunes.
Flying over the park to see the dune-lagoon pattern.
Watching the sunset from the top of a high dune.

name: Wahiba Sands
overview: Also known as Sharqiya Sands, this desert in Oman is famous for its amber-colored sands and traditional Bedouin culture.
highlights:
Dune bashing and sandboarding.
Staying in a traditional desert camp.
Meeting local Bedouin families and seeing their livestock.

name: Simpson Desert
overview: A large area of dry, red sandy plain and dunes in Central Australia. It possesses the world's longest parallel sand dunes.
highlights:
Driving across the 1,100 parallel sand dunes.
Visiting the Big Red dune, the largest in the desert.
Experiencing the remote Australian Outback.

name: Taklamakan Desert
overview: A desert in southwest Xinjiang in Northwest China. It is bounded by the Kunlun Mountains to the south and the Pamir Mountains to the west.
highlights:
Traveling the desert highway that crosses the shifting sands.
Visiting the ancient Silk Road oases.
Seeing the populus euphratica forests in autumn.

name: Dasht-e Lut
overview: A large salt desert in southeastern Iran. It holds the record for some of the highest surface temperatures ever recorded on Earth.
highlights:
Exploring the Kaluts (yardangs), massive natural sand castles.
Witnessing the extreme heat and arid landscape.
Photography of the unique geological formations.

name: Dasht-e Kavir
overview: The Great Salt Desert of Iran, located in the middle of the Iranian Plateau. It features salt marshes and mud flats.
highlights:
Viewing the vast salt polygons and crusts.
Visiting the Kavir National Park.
Stargazing in the dark desert skies.

name: Erg Chebbi Dunes
overview: One of Morocco's two large ergs (seas of dunes). The large orange dunes are a popular tourist destination near Merzouga.
highlights:
Camel trekking into the dunes at sunset.
Luxury camping under the stars.
Sandboarding down the high dunes.

name: Erg Chigaga Dunes
overview: The largest and wildest sand dune field in Morocco, located in the Drâa-Tafilalet area. It is more remote and less crowded than Erg Chebbi.
highlights:
Experiencing the raw, untouched Sahara landscape.
Lengthy off-road 4x4 journeys to reach the dunes.
Peaceful camping away from mass tourism.

name: Badain Jaran Desert
overview: Located in China, this desert is home to the tallest stationary dunes on Earth and over 100 spring-fed lakes nestled between the mega-dunes.
highlights:
Climbing the Biluthu Peak, the world's highest stationary dune.
Seeing the mysterious lakes amidst the sand.
Hearing the booming sound of the singing sands.

name: Karakum Desert
overview: A desert in Central Asia occupying about 70 percent of Turkmenistan. It is famous for the Darvaza Gas Crater.
highlights:
Visiting the 'Door to Hell' (Darvaza Gas Crater) at night.
Exploring the ruins of ancient Merv.
Crossing the desolate landscapes of Central Asia.

name: Thar Desert
overview: Also known as the Great Indian Desert, it forms a natural boundary between India and Pakistan. It is the most densely populated desert in the world.
highlights:
Camel safaris from the Golden City of Jaisalmer.
Attending the Desert Festival in February.
Visiting traditional Rajasthani villages.

name: Kalahari Desert
overview: A large semi-arid sandy savanna in Southern Africa. Unlike true deserts, it supports more plant life and a diverse array of wildlife.
highlights:
Safari game drives to see black-maned lions.
Interacting with the indigenous San people.
Visiting the Makgadikgadi Pans during the wet season.

name: Simien Lava Desert
overview: Often referred to as the Danakil Depression, this is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth, featuring lava lakes and colorful hydrothermal fields.
highlights:
Hiking to the active lava lake of Erta Ale volcano.
Seeing the colorful sulfur springs of Dallol.
Witnessing the camel caravans carrying salt.

name: Huacachina Sand Dunes
overview: A desert oasis surrounded by massive sand dunes in southwestern Peru. It is a premier destination for sandboarding and dune buggies.
highlights:
Riding high-speed dune buggies across the steep dunes.
Sandboarding down the massive slopes.
Watching the sunset over the oasis from the dune ridge.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
overview: A cave system in New Zealand known for its population of Arachnocampa luminosa, a glowworm species found exclusively in New Zealand.
highlights:
Taking a boat ride under a galaxy of glowworms.
Exploring the limestone formations of the Cathedral Cave.
Learning about the Maori legends associated with the caves.

name: Reed Flute Cave
overview: A landmark and tourist attraction in Guilin, China. It is a natural limestone cave with multicolored lighting and has been interesting to visitors for over 1200 years.
highlights:
Viewing the illuminated stalactites and stalagmites.
Reading ink inscriptions on the walls dating back to the Tang Dynasty.
Seeing the Crystal Palace of the Dragon King.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
overview: A national park in the Chihuahuan Desert of southern New Mexico. It features more than 119 caves, including the massive Big Room.
highlights:
Walking through the Big Room, the largest single cave chamber in North America.
Watching the bat flight program at sunset.
Exploring the intricate formations like the Hall of Giants.

name: Son Doong Cave
overview: The world's largest cave by cross-section, located in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park. It has its own localized weather system and jungle.
highlights:
Camping inside the massive caverns.
Seeing the 'Garden of Edam' jungle growing inside the cave.
Witnessing sunbeams penetrating the roof collapses.

name: Škocjan Caves
overview: A cave system in Slovenia which possesses one of the world's largest known underground river canyons.
highlights:
Crossing the bridge over the massive underground canyon.
Seeing the Reka River disappear underground.
Exploring the massive Martel's Chamber.

name: Mammoth Cave
overview: The longest known cave system in the world, located in Kentucky. It preserves a diverse group of cave fauna and distinct geological features.
highlights:
Taking the Historic Tour through the Rotunda.
Seeing the Frozen Niagara formation.
Squeezing through the Fat Man's Misery passage.

name: Špania Dolina Karst Landscape
overview: Located near Banská Bystrica, this area is historically famous for copper mining but is set within a dramatic landscape of mountains and geological features.
highlights:
Hiking the mining nature trails.
Viewing the historic mining dumps and shafts.
Exploring the surrounding Starohorské vrchy mountains.

name: Puerto Princesa Underground River
overview: A subterranean river in Palawan, Philippines. It flows directly into the sea, and its lower portion is subject to tidal influences.
highlights:
taking a paddle boat tour inside the cave.
Seeing unique rock formations and bats.
Exploring the surrounding biodiversity of the national park.

name: Jeita Grotto
overview: A system of two separate, but interconnected, karstic limestone caves spanning nearly 9 kilometres in the Nahr al-Kalb valley.
highlights:
Taking a boat ride on the underground lake in the lower grotto.
Walking the pathways of the upper grotto to see massive stalactites.
Riding the cable car for a panoramic view of the valley.

name: Hang En Cave
overview: The third largest cave in the world, located near Son Doong. It features a massive main chamber and a campsite on a sandy beach inside the cave.
highlights:
Camping on the beach inside the cave.
Swimming in the turquoise pools.
Witnessing thousands of swifts returning to the cave at dusk.

name: Phong Nha Cave
overview: A cave in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, famous for its rock formations with imaginative names like the 'Lion', 'Fairy Caves', and 'Royal Court'.
highlights:
Approaching the cave entrance by boat on the Son River.
Exploring the wet cave and dry cave sections.
Admiring the Cham inscriptions on the cave walls.

name: Devetashka Cave
overview: A huge karst cave near Devetaki, Bulgaria. It is known for its seven large holes in the ceiling which illuminate the vast interior.
highlights:
Seeing the 'Eyes of God' ceiling openings.
Observing the colony of bats inhabiting the cave.
Walking through the massive entrance hall.

name: Benagil Sea Cave
overview: A stunning sea cave in the Algarve region of Portugal, featuring a natural skylight or 'eye' in its ceiling.
highlights:
Kayaking or boat touring into the cave.
Photographing the sunlight streaming through the ceiling eye.
Relaxing on the hidden beach inside the cave.

name: Blue Grotto
overview: A sea cave on the coast of the island of Capri, southern Italy. Sunlight passing through an underwater cavity creates a brilliant blue reflection.
highlights:
Entering the small opening in a traditional rowboat.
Singing Neapolitan songs inside the echoing chamber.
Marveling at the electric blue color of the water.

name: Aven d'Orgnac
overview: A grand cave site located in the Ardèche, France. It is designated as a Grand Site de France due to its exceptional underground landscape.
highlights:
Descending into the massive chambers.
Seeing the 'pine cone' stalagmites.
Visiting the Cité de la Préhistoire museum nearby.

name: Postojna Cave
overview: A karst cave system near Postojna, Slovenia. It is the second-longest cave system in the country and one of its top tourism sites.
highlights:
Riding the underground electric train.
Seeing the 'Brilliant' stalagmite.
Spotting the olm (proteus), a cave-dwelling aquatic salamander.

name: Jeju Manjanggul Lava Tube
overview: One of the finest lava tunnels in the world, located on Jeju Island. It is a designated UNESCO World Natural Heritage site.
highlights:
Walking through the massive lava tube.
Seeing the world's largest lava column.
Observing the unique lava flow lines on the walls.

name: Kamchatka Ice Caves
overview: Formed by the hot springs flowing beneath the glacial ice near the Mutnovsky volcano. The roofs are thin enough to let sunlight through.
highlights:
Seeing the multicolored lights filtering through the ice.
Exploring the connection between fire (volcano) and ice.
Photographing the surreal, tunnel-like structures.

name: Waitomo Ruakuri Cave
overview: New Zealand's longest guided underground walking tour. It offers a blend of glowworms and intricate limestone formations.
highlights:
Descending the spiral entrance ramp.
Hearing the roar of the hidden underground waterfall.
Seeing fossils and limestone shawls.

name: Shilin Stone Forest
overview: A notable set of limestone formations located in Yunnan Province. The tall rocks resemble petrified trees creating a forest of stone.
highlights:
Walking through the maze of towering stone pinnacles.
Visiting the Ashima Rock associated with local legend.
Experiencing the unique karst geography.

name: Great Blue Hole
overview: A giant marine sinkhole off the coast of Belize. It was made famous by Jacques Cousteau and is a world-class scuba diving site.
highlights:
Diving to see the stalactites formed when the cave was dry.
Aerial tours to see the perfect circular dark blue shape.
Spotting reef sharks and marine life.

name: Perito Moreno Glacier
overview: A glacier in Los Glaciares National Park. It is one of the few glaciers in the world that is advancing rather than retreating.
highlights:
Watching massive ice chunks calve into the lake.
Trekking on the ice surface.
Walking the boardwalks for panoramic views.

name: Vatnajökull Ice Caves
overview: Crystal blue ice caves formed within Vatnajökull, Europe's largest glacier. They are ephemeral wonders, changing shape every season.
highlights:
Exploring the vibrant blue ice tunnels.
Photography of the light refracting through the ice.
Experiencing the inside of a glacier.

name: Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon
overview: A large glacial lake in southeast Iceland, on the edge of Vatnajökull National Park. It is filled with icebergs breaking off from the glacier.
highlights:
Taking a boat tour among the floating icebergs.
Seeing seals swimming in the lagoon.
Visiting the nearby Diamond Beach.

name: Franz Josef Glacier
overview: A temperate maritime glacier in Westland Tai Poutini National Park. It descends from the Southern Alps to rainforest level.
highlights:
Heli-hiking onto the glacier ice.
Walking to the terminal face viewpoint.
Relaxing in the hot pools nearby.

name: Hubbard Glacier
overview: A tidewater glacier located in Alaska and the Yukon. It is one of the most active calving glaciers in North America.
highlights:
Cruising close to the massive glacier face.
Hearing the 'white thunder' of calving ice.
Observing wildlife like seals and otters on ice floes.

name: Columbia Icefield
overview: The largest icefield in the Rocky Mountains of North America. It feeds several major glaciers including the Athabasca Glacier.
highlights:
Riding the Ice Explorer onto the Athabasca Glacier.
Walking the Skywalk glass-floored observation platform.
Driving the scenic Icefields Parkway.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord
overview: A fjord in western Greenland declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is filled with massive icebergs calved from the Sermeq Kujalleq glacier.
highlights:
Hiking the boardwalks to view the icefjord.
Taking a midnight sun boat tour among icebergs.
Listening to the cracking and rumbling of the ice.

name: Fox Glacier
overview: Located near Franz Josef Glacier, it is another accessible glacier on New Zealand's West Coast, known for its dramatic icefalls.
highlights:
Heli-hiking to remote parts of the glacier.
Seeing the reflection of Mt. Cook in Lake Matheson nearby.
Exploring the terminal face walk.

name: Aletsch Glacier
overview: The largest glacier in the Alps, located in Switzerland. It is part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch protected area.
highlights:
Viewing the curved 'river of ice' from Eggishorn.
Hiking along the glacier edge.
Visiting the Jungfraujoch observatory.

name: Skaftafell Ice Cave
overview: Ice caves found in the Skaftafell nature reserve (part of Vatnajökull National Park). They are famous for their deep blue color.
highlights:
Guided hiking on the glacier tongue.
Exploring the crystal blue caves in winter.
Seeing the Svartifoss waterfall nearby.

name: Mendenhall Ice Caves
overview: Located inside the Mendenhall Glacier near Juneau, Alaska. These stunning blue caves are accessible via hike or canoe.
highlights:
Kayaking across Mendenhall Lake.
Hiking to the glacier face and ice caves.
Seeing the Nugget Falls adjacent to the glacier.

name: Svínafellsjökull
overview: An outlet glacier of Vatnajökull, known for its sharp ridges and deep crevasses. It has been a filming location for several movies.
highlights:
Glacier hiking on the rugged ice surface.
Admiring the contrast between blue ice and black volcanic ash.
Photography of the dramatic ice ridges.

name: Grey Glacier
overview: A glacier in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, located in Torres del Paine National Park. It feeds the Grey Lake.
highlights:
Boat navigation to the glacier face.
Ice hiking on the glacier.
Crossing the suspension bridges for a view of the ice field.

name: Lamplugh Glacier
overview: An 8-mile-long glacier located in Glacier Bay National Park, Alaska. It is known for its vivid blue ice.
highlights:
Viewing the glacier from a cruise ship.
Kayaking in the calm waters near the glacier.
Spotting wildlife in the bay.

name: Pasterze Glacier
overview: The longest glacier in Austria, lying at the foot of the Grossglockner. It is accessible via the Grossglockner High Alpine Road.
highlights:
Visiting the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe viewpoint.
Hiking down to the glacier tongue.
Seeing marmots and ibexes in the area.

name: Grand Canyon
overview: A steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona. It is unmatched throughout the world for its intricate and colorful landscape.
highlights:
Hiking the Bright Angel Trail.
Viewing the sunrise from Mather Point.
Rafting down the Colorado River.

name: Antelope Canyon
overview: A slot canyon on Navajo land east of Page, Arizona. It is famous for its wave-like structure and light beams.
highlights:
Photography of the light beams in Upper Antelope Canyon.
Walking through the narrow sandstone walls.
Experiencing the spiritual significance to the Navajo people.

name: Bryce Canyon
overview: Famous for its crimson-colored hoodoos, which are spire-shaped rock formations. It is a natural amphitheater rather than a canyon.
highlights:
Hiking the Navajo Loop and Queens Garden trail.
Watching the sunrise at Sunrise Point.
Stargazing under the dark night skies.

name: Zion Canyon
overview: The main feature of Zion National Park, featuring steep red cliffs. It was carved by the North Fork of the Virgin River.
highlights:
Hiking the Narrows by wading up the river.
Climbing the Angels Landing trail.
Driving the Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway.

name: Fish River Canyon
overview: The largest canyon in Africa, located in the south of Namibia. It features a gigantic ravine, in total about 100 miles long.
highlights:
Hiking the multi-day Fish River Canyon Trail.
Enjoying the view from the Hell's Bend viewpoint.
Soaking in the Ai-Ais Hot Springs.

name: Serengeti National Park
overview: A vast ecosystem in east-central Africa, primarily spanning northern Tanzania. It is world-renowned for its massive annual migration of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles.
highlights:
Witnessing the Great Migration of over two million ungulates across the plains.
Spotting the Big Five (lion, leopard, rhino, elephant, and Cape buffalo) in their natural habitat.
Experiencing a hot air balloon safari over the vast savanna at sunrise.

name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
overview: A scenic canyon on the Jinsha River, a primary tributary of the upper Yangtze. It is one of the deepest and most spectacular river canyons in the world.
highlights:
Hiking the high trail for dramatic views.
Seeing the rushing water at the Tiger Leaping Stone.
Experiencing the Naxi minority culture.

name: Taroko Gorge
overview: A 19-km-long canyon situated north of Hualien on Taiwan's east coast. It is famous for its marble walls and the Liwu River.
highlights:
Walking the Swallow Grotto trail.
Visiting the Eternal Spring Shrine.
Seeing the Qingshui Cliff nearby.

name: Blyde River Canyon
overview: One of the largest canyons on Earth, and it may be the largest 'green canyon' due to its lush subtropical foliage.
highlights:
Viewing the Three Rondavels formations.
Visiting Bourke's Luck Potholes.
Driving the Panorama Route.

name: Cape of Good Hope
overview: A rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula in South Africa, known for its spectacular scenery.
highlights:
Standing at the scenic southwesternmost point of the African continent.
Spotting ostriches and baboons in the nature reserve.
Taking the funicular to the Cape Point lighthouse.

name: Glacier National Park
overview: A vast wilderness area in Montana's Rocky Mountains, featuring glacier-carved peaks and valleys running to the Canadian border.
highlights:
Driving the spectacular Going-to-the-Sun Road.
Hiking to the Hidden Lake overlook.
Spotting mountain goats and grizzly bears.

name: Death Valley
overview: A desert valley in Eastern California, known as one of the hottest and driest places on Earth.
highlights:
Visiting Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America.
Watching the sunrise at Zabriskie Point.
Exploring the salt flats and colorful badlands.

name: Amalfi Coast
overview: A stretch of coastline along the southern edge of Italy's Sorrentine Peninsula, famous for its rugged terrain, scenic beauty, and picturesque towns.
highlights:
Driving the winding coastal road with breathtaking Mediterranean views.
Exploring the pastel-colored houses of Positano.
Visiting the stunning gardens of Ravello.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
overview: A large volcanic caldera in Tanzania, serving as a huge natural enclosure for a vast variety of wildlife.
highlights:
Going on a safari to spot the Big Five within the crater.
Witnessing the dense population of lions and hyenas.
Viewing flamingos on Lake Magadi.

name: Jiuzhaigou Valley
overview: A nature reserve and national park in Sichuan province, China, renowned for its multi-level waterfalls, colorful lakes, and snow-capped peaks.
highlights:
Admiring the vivid colors of Five Flower Lake.
Viewing the majestic Nuorilang Waterfall.
Experiencing the pristine alpine scenery.

name: Zhangjiajie National Forest
overview: Famous for its quartzite-sandstone pillars, which served as inspiration for the Hallelujah Mountains in the movie Avatar.
highlights:
Riding the Bailong Elevator, the highest outdoor elevator.
Walking across the glass bridge.
Viewing the pillar formations from Yuanjiajie.

name: Wave Rock
overview: A natural rock formation in Western Australia that is shaped like a tall breaking ocean wave. It forms the north side of a solitary hill.
highlights:
'Surfing' the rock for a photo opportunity.
Exploring the Mulka's Cave nearby.
Seeing the changing colors of the rock at different times of day.

name: The Wave
overview: A sandstone rock formation located in Arizona near the Utah border. It is famous for its colorful, undulating forms and is difficult to access due to permit limits.
highlights:
Hiking the rugged trail to the formation.
Photography of the sweeping sandstone lines.
Experiencing the solitude of the protected area.

name: Giant's Causeway
overview: An area of about 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption in Northern Ireland.
highlights:
Walking on the hexagonal basalt stones.
Visiting the Wishing Chair and the Organ.
Learning about the legend of Finn MacCool.

name: Meteora Rock Landscape
overview: A rock formation in central Greece hosting one of the largest and most precipitously built complexes of Eastern Orthodox monasteries.
highlights:
Visiting the monasteries perched on high cliffs.
Hiking between the rock pillars.
Witnessing the spiritual atmosphere and sunset views.

name: King's Canyon
overview: A majestic canyon in Watarrka National Park in Australia's Northern Territory. It features 100-meter-high sandstone walls.
highlights:
Walking the Rim Walk for spectacular views.
Visiting the Garden of Eden waterhole.
Seeing the domes of the Lost City.

name: Coyote Buttes South
overview: A remote section of the Paria Canyon-Vermilion Cliffs Wilderness. It features delicate and colorful sandstone formations similar to The Wave.
highlights:
Exploring the Cottonwood Teepees formations.
Photography of the colorful sandstone layers.
Enjoying the remote wilderness with fewer crowds than The Wave.

name: Monument Valley
overview: A region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of vast sandstone buttes. It is an iconic symbol of the American West.
highlights:
Driving the 17-mile scenic loop.
Taking a guided tour with a Navajo guide.
Watching the sunrise behind the Mitten Buttes.

name: Cappadocia Fairy Chimneys
overview: A historical region in Central Anatolia, Turkey, known for its unique 'fairy chimney' rock formations and ancient cave dwellings.
highlights:
Taking a hot air balloon ride at sunrise.
Staying in a cave hotel.
Exploring the underground cities like Derinkuyu.

name: Valle de la Luna
overview: Located in the Atacama Desert, this valley has stone and sand formations which have been carved by wind and water, resembling the surface of the moon.
highlights:
Watching the sunset change the colors of the valley.
Exploring the salt caverns.
Climbing the Great Dune for a panoramic view.

name: Valley of Fire
overview: Nevada's oldest state park, known for its stunning red sandstone formations, the Aztec Sandstone, which formed from shifting sand dunes.
highlights:
Seeing the Fire Wave formation.
Visiting the Elephant Rock.
Spotting ancient petroglyphs on the rocks.

name: Samaria Gorge
overview: A national park in Crete and one of the longest gorges in Europe. It is a major tourist attraction of the island.
highlights:
Hiking the full 16km trail from Omalos to Agia Roumeli.
Passing through the narrow 'Iron Gates'.
Seeing the kri-kri (Cretan goat).

name: Gorges du Verdon
overview: A river canyon in southeastern France. It is often considered to be one of Europe's most beautiful river canyons, famous for its turquoise-green water.
highlights:
Kayaking or pedal boating in the canyon.
Driving the scenic rim roads.
Hiking the Sentier Martel trail.

name: Uluru
overview: A massive sandstone monolith in the heart of the Northern Territory's arid 'Red Centre'. It is sacred to indigenous Australians.
highlights:
Watching the rock change color at sunrise and sunset.
Walking around the base of the rock.
Visiting the cultural center to learn about Anangu culture.

name: Devils Tower
overview: A laccolithic butte composed of igneous rock in the Bear Lodge Ranger District of the Black Hills, Wyoming. It was the first US National Monument.
highlights:
Hiking the Tower Trail around the base.
Climbing the tower (for experienced climbers).
Spotting prairie dogs near the entrance.

name: Pedra da Gávea
overview: A monolithic mountain in Tijuca Forest, Rio de Janeiro. It is one of the highest mountains in the world that ends directly in the ocean.
highlights:
Hiking the challenging trail to the top.
Taking a photo at the famous 'Lion's Head'.
Enjoying panoramic views of Rio de Janeiro.

name: Split Apple Rock
overview: A geological rock formation in Tasman Bay, New Zealand. It is made of granite and looks like an apple cleft in half.
highlights:
Kayaking out to the rock.
Swimming in the calm waters nearby.
Photography of the unique formation.

name: Dimmuborgir Lava Formations
overview: A large area of unusually shaped lava fields east of Mývatn in Iceland. The name means 'Dark Castles'.
highlights:
Walking through the maze of lava pillars.
Seeing the Kirkjan (The Church) natural arch.
Learning about the Yule Lads folklore.

name: The Twelve Apostles
overview: A collection of limestone stacks off the shore of Port Campbell National Park, by the Great Ocean Road in Victoria, Australia.
highlights:
Viewing the stacks from the boardwalks.
Visiting at sunset for golden lighting.
Taking a helicopter ride for an aerial view.

name: Old Man of Storr
overview: A large pinnacle of rock on the Isle of Skye, Scotland. It was created by a massive ancient landslide.
highlights:
Hiking up to the base of the pinnacle.
Enjoying views over the Sound of Raasay.
Photography of the dramatic landscape.

name: Reynisfjara Basalt Columns
overview: A world-famous black-sand beach found on the South Coast of Iceland, featuring massive basalt stacks and a pyramid of basalt columns.
highlights:
Climbing on the hexagonal basalt columns.
Seeing the Reynisdrangar sea stacks.
Watching the powerful waves (from a safe distance).

name: Kjeragbolten
overview: A famous boulder wedged in a mountain crevasse by the edge of Kjerag mountain in Norway, suspended above a deep abyss.
highlights:
Standing on the boulder for a photo (if brave enough).
Hiking the challenging trail to the site.
Views of the Lysefjord below.

name: Trolltunga
overview: The 'Troll's Tongue', a rock formation jutting horizontally out of a mountain about 700 meters above the north side of the lake Ringedalsvatnet.
highlights:
Hiking the long and scenic trail.
Sitting on the edge of the rock tongue.
Enjoying the panoramic fjord views.

name: Preikestolen
overview: The Pulpit Rock, a steep cliff which rises 604 meters above Lysefjorden. It has an almost flat top creating a famous viewing platform.
highlights:
Hiking the moderate trail to the cliff.
Looking down the sheer drop into the fjord.
Taking a fjord cruise to see the cliff from below.

name: Darvaza Gas Crater
overview: Known as the 'Door to Hell', this natural gas field collapsed into a cavern and has been burning continuously since 1971.
highlights:
Witnessing the fiery crater glowing in the dark desert night.
Camping near the crater rim.
Experiencing the heat and roar of the flames.

name: Mount Erebus Ice Fumaroles
overview: The southernmost active volcano on Earth, located in Antarctica. It features unique ice towers (fumaroles) formed by escaping steam freezing instantly.
highlights:
seeing the towering ice chimneys emitting steam.
Observing the persistent lava lake in the crater.
Experiencing the extreme Antarctic volcanic environment.

name: Mount Etna Lava Fields
overview: Europe's most active volcano, located in Sicily. The landscape is a mix of smoking craters, fresh black lava flows, and fertile vineyards.
highlights:
Trekking to the summit craters.
Walking across the desolate Valle del Bove.
Seeing the contrast between black lava and green forests.

name: Dallol Hydrothermal Area
overview: A cinder cone volcano in the Danakil Depression. It is known for its unearthly colors, salt formations, and acidic hot springs.
highlights:
Photography of the neon yellow and green sulfur pools.
Seeing the salt pillars and terraces.
Experiencing one of the hottest places on Earth.

name: Kīlauea Volcano
overview: An active shield volcano in the Hawaiian Islands. It is home to the Halemaʻumaʻu crater and extensive lava fields.
highlights:
Driving the Chain of Craters Road.
Walking through the Thurston Lava Tube.
Viewing the glow of the lava lake (when active).

name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
overview: New Zealand's best one-day hike, traversing an active volcanic landscape with craters, steam vents, and emerald-colored lakes.
highlights:
Hiking past the Red Crater and Emerald Lakes.
Views of Mount Ngauruhoe (Mount Doom).
Traversing the South Crater flat.

name: Mount Bromo Caldera
overview: An active somatic volcano in East Java, sitting inside the massive Tengger Sand Sea caldera.
highlights:
Watching the sunrise over the caldera from King Kong Hill.
Crossing the Sea of Sand on horseback or jeep.
Climbing the stairs to the rim of the smoking crater.

name: Landmannalaugar
overview: A region in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve in the Highlands of Iceland. It is known for its multicolored rhyolite mountains and lava fields.
highlights:
Bathing in the natural geothermal hot springs.
Hiking through the colorful Brennisteinsalda mountain.
Walking the Laugavegur trail.

name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
overview: A vast ocean of lava flows with scattered islands of cinder cones and sagebrush in Idaho.
highlights:
Exploring the lava tubes and caves.
Hiking up the Inferno Cone for a panoramic view.
Seeing the spatter cones.

name: Wau-en-Namus
overview: An extinct volcano in southern Libya. It features a dark basaltic ash field contrasting with three multi-colored lakes in its caldera.
highlights:
Viewing the black sand against the desert backdrop.
Seeing the green, blue, and red lakes.
Camping in the remote Saharan landscape.

name: Erta Ale Lava Lake
overview: A continuously active basaltic shield volcano in the Afar Region of northeastern Ethiopia. It holds one of the world's longest-existing lava lakes.
highlights:
Trekking at night to the crater rim.
Watching the bubbling and churning molten lava.
Sleeping under the stars near the volcano.

name: Nyiragongo Lava Lake
overview: An active stratovolcano in the Virunga Mountains. It contains the world's largest and most fluid lava lake.
highlights:
Hiking to the summit to view the boiling lava lake.
Spending the night in shelters on the crater rim.
Views of the surrounding rainforest and Lake Kivu.

name: Nisyros Volcano Caldera
overview: A volcanic Greek island with a massive caldera. Visitors can walk right into the hydrothermal craters.
highlights:
Walking on the floor of the Stefanos crater.
Feeling the heat and smelling the sulfur.
Exploring the traditional village of Nikia on the rim.

name: Askja Caldera
overview: A massive caldera in the Dyngjufjöll mountains. It contains the deepest lake in Iceland and the warm geothermal crater lake Viti.
highlights:
Swimming in the warm milky blue waters of Viti.
Hiking across the desolate volcanic desert.
Seeing the contrast between the blue lake and black sand.

name: Mount Yasur
overview: An active volcano on Tanna Island, Vanuatu. It is known as the 'Lighthouse of the Pacific' due to its continuous Strombolian eruptions.
highlights:
Standing on the rim while the volcano explodes with lava bombs.
Feeling the ground shake with every eruption.
mailing a letter from the world's only underwater post office nearby.

name: Mount Nyamuragira Lava Fields
overview: Africa's most active volcano, located near Nyiragongo. It creates massive lava fields that flow into the surrounding forests.
highlights:
Observing the newest lava flows in the region.
Exploring the unique vegetation reclaiming the lava.
Seeing the shield volcano structure.

name: Hekla Volcano Landscape
overview: One of Iceland's most active volcanoes, historically known as the 'Gateway to Hell'. The surrounding landscape is a mix of tephra and lava.
highlights:
Hiking to the summit for views of the highlands.
Seeing the vast fields of volcanic pumice.
Experiencing the raw, barren power of the landscape.

name: Tolbachik Lava Fields
overview: A volcanic complex in Kamchatka. The 'Dead Forest' and the vast lava flows from the 1975 and 2012 eruptions are spectacular.
highlights:
Walking through the ghostly Dead Forest.
Exploring the fresh, sharp lava flows.
Climbing the cinder cones for a view of the volcanic range.

name: El Malpais Lava Beds
overview: A national monument in New Mexico featuring rough, hardened lava flows, cinder cones, and lava tube caves.
highlights:
Exploring the lava tube caves like Junction Cave.
Seeing the Sandstone Bluffs overlooking the lava fields.
Hiking the Zuni-Acoma Trail.

name: Mount Sinabung Lava Flows
overview: A highly active volcano in North Sumatra. The landscape around it has been reshaped by recent pyroclastic flows and ash.
highlights:
Viewing the volcano from a safe distance zone.
Seeing the 'ghost villages' abandoned due to eruptions.
Witnessing the ash plumes rising.

name: Uzon Caldera
